Megan romer, national co-chair of the democratic socialists of america, has dismissed a staggering $49 trillion estimate for her organisation's socialist agenda as a "made-up number", but when challenged to provide an alternative figure, she refused. that extraordinary exchange exposes the fundamental dishonesty of the DSA's economic sales pitch: its leaders want to spend trillions of dollars of american taxpayers' money, fundamentally restructure the economy and expand government control over virtually every aspect of national life, yet cannot even explain how much their political fantasy would cost.

this is precisely why the democratic socialists of america should be taken seriously as a threat to america's economic future.

the organisation wants medicare for all, student debt cancellation, sweeping immigration changes, reduced military spending and fundamental alterations to the country's constitutional institutions. its political activists are increasingly influential within the democratic party, and its candidates are making significant congressional gains.

but americans should understand what this movement is actually proposing.

the DSA wants an enormous expansion of government spending at a time when the united states already faces substantial national debt and long-term fiscal challenges. its policies could place extraordinary additional pressure on federal finances, increase the burden on taxpayers and create economic obligations that future generations would be forced to carry.

the $49 trillion estimate is not some insignificant accounting disagreement. it represents an enormous potential financial commitment that demands serious examination.

if implemented without credible financing, spending controls and realistic economic assumptions, the DSA's proposals could dramatically worsen america's fiscal position, accelerate the accumulation of public debt and increase the risk of a serious sovereign debt crisis. there is no responsible way to pretend that trillions of dollars in additional government commitments come without consequences.

the american taxpayer is not an unlimited source of money for socialist activists.

and yet, when confronted with the numbers, romer effectively shrugged.

the 2026 midterm elections have made this debate even more urgent. DSA-backed candidates have made significant congressional gains, giving the organisation an opportunity to push its radical economic agenda further into the democratic party's political programme.

this should concern every american who believes that economic freedom, individual opportunity and responsible government spending matter.

the democratic party has increasingly allowed the socialist wing of its political coalition to dictate the terms of debate. its politicians cannot continue benefiting from the support of radical activists while pretending that the dsa's ambitions are somehow separate from their own political movement.

if democrats intend to embrace this agenda, they must answer for its potential financial consequences.

speaking to fox news following the election results, romer was challenged over the white house council of economic advisers' estimate that the dsa's proposed policies could cost approximately $49 trillion.

the proposals include medicare for all and student debt cancellation, two enormous government spending commitments that would dramatically expand federal responsibilities.

the administration estimated that the agenda could cost approximately $355,000 per american household over the next decade.

romer attempted to undermine the calculation by suggesting that the white house had deliberately produced figures intended to make the socialist movement look bad.

"the white house, who does not like us very much, managed to come up with some math that made us look bad," she said.

"but we don't agree with these numbers."

when fox news anchor martha maccallum pressed her for an alternative estimate, romer refused to provide one.

"there's no, like, one, solid number because it depends on what pieces we can build in the meantime," she explained.

then came the admission that should have set alarm bells ringing across the country.

"i'm not going to give you a solid number. that's not what i'm here to do," romer declared.

unbelievable.

the leader of an organisation demanding an enormous expansion of government spending effectively told american taxpayers that explaining the financial consequences was not her responsibility.

what an extraordinary display of political arrogance.

the dsa wants to reshape the american economy, transfer enormous responsibilities to the federal government and create trillions of dollars in additional spending commitments, but its leadership apparently considers basic financial accountability optional.

if the $49 trillion estimate is wrong, publish the calculations proving it. if the proposed programmes can be delivered for less, demonstrate how. if the organisation has a credible financing strategy, put it before the american people.

instead, romer offered excuses.

this is the problem with socialist politics. the promises are always enormous, the projected benefits are always extraordinary and the financial consequences are somehow always someone else's problem.

the dsa wants to sell americans a political fantasy in which government can provide virtually everything without creating an enormous financial burden.

that fantasy does not survive contact with economic reality.

medicare for all would fundamentally restructure the financing of american healthcare, transferring substantially greater responsibility to the federal government. student debt cancellation would create enormous financial obligations and raise serious questions about fairness, incentives and future borrowing.

these proposals require credible financial assessments, not vague assurances that the government will somehow find the money.

america already has a substantial national debt. adding enormous new spending commitments without credible funding arrangements would make an already difficult fiscal situation considerably worse.

the consequences could include higher taxation, greater borrowing costs, additional pressure on inflation and reduced fiscal flexibility for future administrations.

if investors lose confidence in the government's ability to manage its finances, the consequences could become even more serious.

a country cannot indefinitely promise to spend money it does not have without facing consequences.

the dsa should explain how it intends to avoid those consequences rather than dismissing anyone who questions its numbers.

and americans should reject the idea that socialism is somehow an economic miracle waiting to happen.

history offers plenty of warnings about authoritarian communist systems and centrally controlled economies. the soviet union, mao-era china, cuba and north korea demonstrate how excessive state control, political repression and economic centralisation can destroy prosperity and individual freedom.

these countries followed different historical paths, but their experiences expose the dangers of concentrating economic and political power in the hands of the state.

the dsa may insist that its version of socialism is different. that does not give it permission to ignore history.

america's prosperity has been built through private enterprise, competition, investment, innovation and individual opportunity. the country should be strengthening those foundations rather than handing an increasingly large share of economic decision-making to government bureaucracies.

the dsa's hostility towards american military spending is another disturbing part of its agenda.

during her fox news appearance, romer argued that money devoted to overseas military operations should instead be redirected towards domestic socialist programmes.

"we don't believe in having 800 u.s. military bases around the world," she said.

"that is an insane amount of money to spend."

she also attacked defence contractors, arguing that military expenditure disproportionately benefits wealthy individuals.

there are legitimate questions about unnecessary defence expenditure, but america's military strength is not some disposable luxury that socialist activists can dismantle whenever they want additional money for their political projects.

the united states faces serious threats from iran and china. its armed forces protect american interests, support strategic allies and deter hostile governments.

reducing military capabilities without a credible assessment of the consequences would be an irresponsible gamble.

the issue is particularly important when considering america's relationship with israel.

israel is one of the united states' most important strategic allies. the two countries maintain extensive intelligence cooperation, military partnerships and shared security interests.

israel faces persistent threats from iran and terrorist organisations supported by the islamic republic. hamas has demonstrated the consequences of allowing a terrorist organisation dedicated to destroying israel to operate with the capacity to attack civilians and take hostages.

america must stand firmly with israel.

israel has an undeniable right to exist and an inherent right to defend its citizens against terrorism and external aggression. washington should continue supporting israel's security through military cooperation, intelligence sharing and appropriate defensive assistance.

iran's support for armed terrorist organisations represents a serious threat to regional security. allowing tehran to expand its influence while weakening american support for israel would create additional dangers for both countries.

the radical left's anti-israel activism is therefore another major concern.

the dsa's political environment has become increasingly associated with anti-israel activism, and its growing influence within democratic politics raises serious questions about the future direction of american foreign policy.

the democratic party must answer for the political movements it has allowed to acquire influence within its ranks.

american foreign policy should never be dictated by activists who excuse terrorism or demonise israel.

hamas is a terrorist organisation. its attacks against israeli civilians, hostage-taking and deliberate violence must be condemned without qualification.

supporting palestinian civilians does not require supporting hamas, and humanitarian concern does not require abandoning israel.

america should continue supporting its closest allies and confronting the terrorist organisations and hostile regimes that threaten them.

the dsa's immigration agenda is another reason why its ambitions deserve intense scrutiny.

romer has previously defended proposals to abolish immigration and customs enforcement, eliminate borders and provide amnesty to undocumented immigrants living in the united states.

these proposals would represent a fundamental transformation of american immigration policy.

the united states has the sovereign right to control its borders, enforce immigration laws and determine who is permitted to enter and remain in the country.

abolishing enforcement agencies without presenting a credible replacement would raise serious questions about public safety, immigration administration and the rule of law.

the dsa should explain exactly how it intends to enforce immigration laws under its proposed system.

romer's previous comments about american constitutional institutions are equally alarming.

in a july interview with fox news, she defended proposals to abolish the senate, replace the presidency and supreme court, and fundamentally restructure the existing system of government.

america's constitutional institutions were not established to be dismantled whenever a socialist organisation decides that the existing system is inconvenient.

the senate, presidency and supreme court have distinct constitutional responsibilities. their powers and limitations form part of the system of checks and balances that protects american democracy.

proposals to abolish or fundamentally restructure these institutions deserve extraordinary scrutiny.

the dsa's ambitions therefore extend far beyond healthcare and student debt. they reach into the economy, immigration, national defence and the very structure of american government.

this is not simply another disagreement over tax rates or government programmes. it is an ideological movement seeking to fundamentally transform the country.

and the democratic party has increasingly allowed that movement to become part of its political identity.

democratic politicians cannot continue enjoying the electoral support of socialist activists while pretending they have no responsibility for the policies those activists promote.

every democratic representative supporting these proposals should explain their financial implications and constitutional consequences.

what would medicare for all cost? how would student debt cancellation be financed? what would replace existing immigration enforcement? what reductions to military spending are being considered? how would america maintain its strategic position and protect israel?

these are basic questions of accountability.

republicans should make the dsa's economic agenda a central issue in their opposition to the new democratic congressional majority.

they should expose the financial assumptions behind socialist spending proposals, challenge the organisation's claims and demand that every democratic politician explain where the money is supposed to come from.

the american people must understand that the potential cost of these proposals does not simply disappear because socialist politicians refuse to acknowledge it.

if the dsa's agenda is implemented without sustainable financing, america could face an even greater debt burden, increasingly expensive government obligations and a substantially weaker fiscal position.

the possibility of bankruptcy should not be dismissed as political exaggeration. while a $49 trillion estimate alone does not prove that the united states would become insolvent, a programme of enormous unfunded commitments could increase the risks of a serious debt and fiscal crisis.

that is the responsibility the dsa refuses to confront.

the american taxpayer deserves leaders who understand that every dollar spent by government must ultimately be financed through taxation, borrowing or other public revenue.

there is no magic socialist money tree.

the dsa cannot simply print its way out of every economic problem, and american families should not be forced to pay for an ideological experiment whose financial consequences its own leadership cannot adequately explain.

the democratic party must also be held accountable for its positions on israel and the growing influence of anti-israel activism within its political coalition.

america's relationship with israel must remain a strategic priority. washington should continue confronting iranian aggression, supporting israel's right to defend itself and opposing terrorist organisations that threaten american and israeli citizens.

there should be no ambiguity about those commitments.

the united states does not need the dsa's socialist transformation. it needs economic opportunity, responsible government, secure borders, a powerful military and constitutional institutions that protect individual freedom.

it does not need an organisation that treats trillion-dollar spending promises as political slogans and financial accountability as an inconvenience.

megan romer dismissed the $49 trillion estimate as a made-up number but refused to provide a convincing alternative.

that exchange should become a defining example of the dsa's economic irresponsibility.

the organisation wants to reshape america, but its leadership cannot even explain the full financial consequences of its own ambitions.

the democratic party must answer for its relationship with the socialist movement, its positions on american national security and its approach to the US-israel alliance.

the american people should not be expected to finance an ideological transformation without demanding answers.

enough of the trillion-dollar wish lists. enough of the economic fantasy. enough of the excuses and enough of the political arrogance.

the dsa should stop pretending that bigger government automatically means a better country. it should stop treating taxpayers as an unlimited source of funding and stop expecting americans to accept its socialist agenda without demanding a proper financial explanation.

america must not gamble its economic future on an ideology whose most enthusiastic advocates cannot even provide a convincing account of what their ambitions will cost.

the united states should be strengthening private enterprise, protecting individual freedoms, securing its borders, maintaining a powerful military and standing firmly with israel.

it should not be moving towards an enormous expansion of government control simply because socialist activists have decided that they know better than the american people.

the dsa's ambitions must be challenged at every turn, its financial claims must be scrutinised and the democratic politicians enabling its rise must be held accountable.

america cannot afford to let socialist ideology put its economic future at risk. taxpayers deserve better, future generations deserve better and the country deserves better than the bankrupting promises of the democratic socialists of america.

text:
WE HAD UNPROTECTED SEX FIVE TIMES BEFORE I FOUND HIV MEDICATION IN HIS CABINET. I DIDN’T ASK QUESTIONS. HE DIDN’T OFFER ANSWERS.

My name is Jessica Miller. I’m 29, and I live in Los Angeles, California.

My fiancé, Michael Carter, is a 42-year-old real estate developer who lives in Beverly Hills.

When we met, Michael was everything I wanted in a man. He was successful, attentive, and made me feel like I was the only woman in the world.

We fell in love quickly.

Within a few months, we were talking about marriage and having children.

We had unprotected sex five times.

I trusted him completely. I believed that if there was anything I needed to know about his health, he would tell me.

Then one afternoon, I opened his medicine cabinet.

I found HIV medication.

I stood there, staring at the pills, trying to understand what I was seeing.

Michael walked into the bathroom and caught me holding the bottle.

He looked at me.

I looked at him.

Neither of us said a word.

I wanted to ask him what the medication was for, but I was terrified of the answer.

And he never offered an explanation.

For the next year, I kept quiet.

I continued living with him, loving him, and believing that maybe I had misunderstood what I saw.

Then one morning, a letter arrived from a hospital.

It had Michael’s name on it, along with details about his HIV treatment.

That was the moment everything changed.

I realized I had spent a year sleeping beside a man who knew something about his health that could affect mine.

I felt betrayed, frightened, and foolish for not asking questions sooner.

But the worst part was knowing that he had given me the opportunity to trust him without giving me the information I needed to make an informed decision about my own health.

I still don’t know why he never told me.

And I still don’t know whether I was foolish for staying silent or simply too afraid to confront the truth.

If you found HIV medication in your partner’s cabinet after having unprotected sex, would you confront them immediately, or would you wait for them to tell you the truth?

text:
Can We Move Abroad as Nurses? — USA, Canada, Australia, UK — You Have Options — Choose With Your Eyes Open

You are a Registered Nurse. You have a dream to practice abroad. You hear — "USA is best" — "UK is fastest" — "Canada is best for PR" — "Australia pays highest" — All true. All false. Depends on what you need — speed, money, PR, family.

Here is what you need to know — USA, Canada, Australia, UK — So you can choose, not just follow auntie.

USA — Green Card On Arrival, But Longest Wait

USA is the dream for many because when you land, you land as a permanent resident. Green card. You can work immediately, bring family, no temporary visa stress.

How it works: You do CGFNS evaluation — 3 to 6 months. You pass English — TOEFL or IELTS. You apply to a State Board — you get Authorization to Test. You pass NCLEX-RN — you can take it in your home country. AFTER you pass NCLEX, you get an agency or US employer. That employer files your I-140 petition — EB-3. Once your I-140 is approved, most agencies will pay for your VisaScreen. Then you do medical and embassy interview.

Total time: 18 months to 3 years. Why so long? Not NCLEX. NCLEX you can finish in 6 to 12 months. The wait is immigration — I-140 + VisaScreen + Consular — 12 to 24 months.

Cost: About $1,500 to $2,000 for you. VisaScreen paid by agency after I-140 approval in most cases.

Salary: $81,000 a year average. Ohio $36 to $42 per hour. New York, California $45 to $65 per hour.

Choose USA if: You can wait 2 to 3 years. You want green card on arrival. You want long-term settlement. You don't mind waiting.

Don't choose USA if: You need to move in under 1 year. You cannot wait.

UK — Fastest To Start Working, But Fewer Jobs Now

UK is fastest. If you need to move in under 1 year, UK is realistically the only option.

How it works: You apply to NMC — Nursing and Midwifery Council. You pass English — IELTS 7.0 all bands or OET B all. You pass CBT — 120 multiple choice questions — you can take it at home at Pearson VUE. You get a job offer from NHS Trust or agency — they give you Certificate of Sponsorship. You apply for Health & Care Worker visa — decision in 3 weeks. You travel to UK. You take OSCE — 10 stations, 10 minutes each — in UK test centre — within 8 months of arrival. You pass OSCE, you get your NMC PIN. You start work as RN.

Total time: 9 to 14 months from start to working.

Cost: £1,800 to £3,000 total. NMC fees alone £1,170 — application £140 + CBT £83 + OSCE £794 + PIN £153.

Salary: £29,970 to £36,483 a year — NHS Band 5. Lower than USA, Canada, Australia. But cost of living lower outside London.

PR: After 5 years, you can apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain.

Choose UK if: You need to move fast. You already have strong English. You have a genuine job offer.

Don't choose UK if: You have no job offer. In 2025-26, NHS hiring of overseas nurses fell by more than half. Don't spend money on OSCE or travel without a genuine job offer. Also OSCE first-attempt pass rate is 38% to 54% — you need serious prep.

CANADA — Slow Licensing, But Clearest Path To Permanent Residency

Canada takes longer to start, but once you are in, PR is clearest.

How it works: You apply to NNAS — National Nursing Assessment Service — you pay about CAD $650. You submit transcripts, syllabus, license verification. NNAS issues report in 5 business days once all documents received — but gathering documents takes 2 to 6 weeks. Then you apply to Provincial College — Ontario, BC, Alberta — they review. You pass NCLEX-RN — same exam as USA. You may need bridging course if your education is not equivalent — that can add 12 to 18 months.

Total time: 12 to 24 months to get licensed. If you need bridging, 18 to 36 months.

Cost: CAD $4,000 to $6,500 + settlement funds for immigration.

Salary: $70,000 to $95,000 CAD a year.

PR: Canada runs Express Entry Healthcare draws in 2026. CRS cut-off is about 100 points below general draws.

text:
My father is dying. He is in hospice, taken off all meds except pain medication and he is incapable of eating. 

He is 87 and lived an amazing life. He earned a PhD in math and a B.S. in physics. He did a stint in the Army where he designed the guidance system for a missile. After that, he worked at a national lab and became the manager of a nuclear reactor safety division. Vice President Ford called our home when Three Mile Island happened and told him there was a fighter at the Air Force Base waiting to take him to TMI. He was on site through the entire accident. He was offered a position to head the TMI clean up, he turned it down. Said it was the best career decision he ever made, 'Lots of busy work, no real research'. He ran an F4 Phantom into a wall at 480 mph to test the wall. His group was deeply involved in testing for Yucca Mountain. He rented the entire output of a power plant to run a test. He did some crazy shit. 

And he was insanely sharp. I ran across an article from another researcher that mentioned my Dad. The guy said that whenever anyone got stuck on a problem they'd show up at the base officers club (which lab employees had access to, spent every summer there as a kid) and run it by my Dad. Per the researcher my Dad would say 'Well, let's play with this a little bit...' and proceed to run through the problem and map out how to think about it. 

When I was a kid Dad would play chess with a guy and I'd play Go with one of them on the side at the same time. Found out later that the guy was the state chess champion. Dad would win 1 out of 3. He also played go against 9 dan pro from China once. Him and ~10 other guys at once. With a 9 stone handicap. Dad was the only one to tie. He was pretty proud of that. He also played Bridge against Bill Gates at a tournament. Lost. 

He was an odd guy at times. I asked him about a girl I was dating when I was a teen. He told me 'Ask someone else, I don't do emotions'. He did, but he didn't learn to talk about them until way later in life. He knew what he was good at, would help in anyway he could and if he couldn't help he'd find out who could. 

He was a really good man. He was absolutely honest, kind and tried to help if he could. He was likely on the autism scale but grew up before that was a thing. He could work on a problem nonstop for insanely long periods. His math skills were insane. Calculus was 'kindergarten work' and he could read equations, solve them as he read and picture the outcome. And he would always have some example that was similar to whatever problem he was discussing and link them so everything made sense. During camping trips, where we almost always had other lab employees along, talk would always veer towards some problem someone was having and they would talk it through with Dad. Learned a lot about thinking from just listening. 

He had one daughter from his first marriage and then married my Mom and they had me. He treated his step kids and though they were his own. When my wife and I told him we wanted to have a kid he was overjoyed. Then we had twins and he was ecstatic. One of the best days of my life was introducing my boys to my parents. 

It saddens me deeply that my Dad and my son Duck weren't ever able to really connect. My son is a math guy but by the time Duck got into math my Dad couldn't think very well due to a blood disorder. But both my sons knew him and that will have to do. 

My Dad and my Mom traveled everywhere. They RV'ed for years. A ton of cruises. Trips to islands. He had so many frequent flier miles from his time working (he flew to DC and back 2 a month in average for like 15 years when I was growing up) that it took about 10 years to exhaust the miles. They went *everywhere*.   

There is so much more. He lived an amazing life and was a good man. 

Right now he is still alive. But he isn't there. For the past week all he has said is 'hurts' or 'I love you'. He wakes for maybe 2 minutes at most. Watching his decline has been absolutely heartbreaking. The blood disorder robbed him of thinking, not enough oxygen in his blood. He was above all a thinker. He was always 10 steps ahead of everyone else in discussions. For a while he was pretty angry because he couldn't think well and knew he couldn't think well. It really upset him.

My Mom, during her last years, started suffering from. Dementia. He did everything possible to stand by her even though it was hard. Mom became paranoid and confused. But he loved her and just handled it even though I know it killed him inside. 

He is still with us, but not really. The man who taught me to play Go, helped with math, get frustrated putting things together (he was brilliant but not really mechanically inclined. He could design the shit out of something but building it was another story), and stood by me when my life was a disaster is gone. He is still with us but I already miss him. 

I will miss trying to find a puzzle he could not solve, talking about why dark matter/dark energy is nonsense and trying to explain my music to him. That and more and especially his wickedly dry sense of humor which didn't come out often but always had me rolling. 

Love ya Dad.

Arakan's Border Conflict: Junta-Backed Armed Groups and the Bangladesh Factor

DMG Editorial 

The resurgence of the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) along the Bangladesh–Arakan border, as fighting intensifies around Sittwe, is more than a coincidental development. It reflects a longstanding security challenge involving Myanmar's military, Muslim armed organisations and competing interests along the frontier.

During the 2024 battles for Buthidaung and Maungdaw, Myanmar's military cooperated with Muslim armed groups, including ARSA and the Rohingya Solidarity Organisation (RSO), despite its history of persecuting Muslim civilians. Independent research documented military training, ammunition supplies and tactical assistance, while subsequent investigations identified continuing links between these groups and junta personnel.

This history is essential to understanding renewed attacks against Arakan Army (AA) positions.

For Myanmar's military, maintaining relationships with armed groups along the northern Arakan border offers a means of pressuring the AA after losing territorial control. Ambushes, cross-border incursions and attacks on security outposts can divert AA personnel and resources from major battlefronts, particularly Sittwe.

ARSA, RSO and the Arakan Rohingya Army (ARA) have been linked to attacks and armed activities along the border. However, these organisations have different leadership structures and objectives. Their past cooperation with the junta does not establish that every recent attack was directly coordinated by Myanmar's military.

The Bangladesh dimension further complicates the conflict.

The AA has accused certain Bangladeshi border security personnel of providing armed groups with logistical assistance, ammunition and intelligence. Such allegations require credible investigation and must be distinguished from Bangladesh's official government policy. Border Guard Bangladesh has publicly denied supporting ARSA or RSO.

Bangladesh faces legitimate challenges involving border security, refugee protection and the eventual repatriation of Muslim/Rohingya refugees. Any involvement by individual security officials in facilitating cross-border armed operations would undermine those objectives and increase regional instability.

The motivations behind Muslim armed-group activities are also complex. Alongside reported military cooperation, longstanding grievances, disputes over political representation and territorial control, and frustration over the prolonged refugee crisis have contributed to recruitment and armed mobilisation.

These factors cannot justify attacks on civilians, forced recruitment or other abuses.

For residents of Maungdaw, the consequences are immediate. Armed violence, insecurity and restricted movement threaten livelihoods and safety, particularly in vulnerable border communities. Muslim refugees also face intimidation, coercive recruitment and violence by armed organisations.

Crucially, the actions of ARSA, RSO or ARA must not be attributed collectively to Muslim civilians. Equally, allegations of abuses against Muslim communities by other armed actors require independent investigation and accountability.

The AA's territorial gains bring responsibilities extending beyond military security. Effective governance requires protecting all communities, addressing grievances and preventing ethnic divisions from deepening.

Arakan's border crisis cannot be resolved through military operations alone. It demands scrutiny of junta-linked armed networks, credible investigation of alleged cross-border assistance, responsible engagement with Bangladesh and equal protection for civilians.

Without addressing the political grievances and armed networks sustaining violence, territorial control will remain an uncertain foundation for lasting peace in Arakan.

text:
In August 1972, Indians were expelled from the country on the orders of Uganda's president, Idi Amin Dada.

Indians had played an important role in making Uganda one of the most prosperous countries in all of Africa. But Idi Amin, who came to power on 25 January 1971, began to feel that Indians were exploiting Uganda and sucking the blood out of its economy.

Idi Amin claimed that on 4 August he had seen in a dream that Indians should be expelled from Uganda. On 8 August he issued the order.

Indians were given 90 days to leave the country. They had to leave behind all their property and savings. Each person was allowed to take only one handbag when leaving Uganda, along with just 50 British pounds.

Everything else including jewelry and cash were confiscated. The businesses and companies built by Indians were handed over to Idi Amin's supporters.

Even before expelling the Indians, Idi Amin had already had most of the Ugandan army officers belonging to the Acholi and Langi ethnic communities killed. He was notorious for violence against his opponents and people he disliked.

So the Indians did not wait to argue with him or fight for their rights. They began fleeing the country as quickly as possible. Those who delayed leaving were shot, and there were also incidents of women being raped.

About 90K people were forcibly expelled from Uganda. All of them had been born in Uganda.

About 38,000 Indians reached Britain, where they had to begin a new life amid poverty and hardship.

Some local governments in Britain even tried to prevent Indians from arriving. For example, the Leicester local government issued a public notice appealing to Indians not to come there, because the city already had a large Indian population.

Why did Idi Amin expel the Indians from Uganda?

As mentioned earlier, Idi Amin claimed that he had received a message from God in a dream telling him to expel the Indians from the country.

Later, to justify his decision, he called Indians "bloodsuckers" and accused them of hollowing out Uganda's economy.

But after the Indians left, Uganda's economy was badly ruined. Uganda, once counted among Africa's prosperous countries, fell into such a poor state that it became one of the poorest countries on the continent.

Did Idi Amin receive any punishment for his actions?

No.

He remained president of Uganda for the next five years. Finally, on 11 April 1979, a faction of the Ugandan army rebelled, and after Tanzanian military intervention he was removed from power.

During his brutal rule, Idi Amin had more than 500,000 black Africans killed.

But after he was removed from power, the new government, instead of taking revenge on him or putting him on trial, let him flee to Saudi Arabia, where he took refuge.

What happened to the Indians expelled from Uganda?

The British government tried to put various obstacles in the way of Indians reaching Britain, but Britain's Jewish community welcomed them and provided the help they needed to start a new life.

Most of the forcibly displaced Indians struggled even to make a living. A large number of people had to do low-paying, physically demanding work.

But they did not give up and kept their courage even in difficult circumstances.

None of them took to crime, and none of them committed suicide.

In 1997, about 300 Indians who accepted the apology offered by President Yoweri Museveni returned to Uganda and restarted their businesses, but this time they confined their businesses to the capital, Kampala.

Today, most of those Indians are living prosperous lives... some of them are very big names...

However, there is one question...
India was powerful enough to stop Idi Amin even then...
But did the GOI remain silent because most of the people expelled were Hindus?
The Indira government's official statement was: "These people hold British passports, the responsibility lies with Britain." Only 4,500 were allowed to come to India, and that too temporarily (for 90 days).

text:
MEGHAN MARKLE – THE CONTRADICTIONS AND THE ROYAL FALL-OUT

Let’s get one thing straight. The allegations surrounding Thomas Markle Snr do not automatically vindicate Meghan or excuse her own behaviour. Two things can be true at once.

There are numerous unanswered questions surrounding Meghan’s time in the Royal Family, and they deserve scrutiny.

1.Her father: Harry’s account of arranging an Air New Zealand ticket for Thomas to attend the wedding raised questions about the travel arrangements. Thomas admitted posing for photographs, but there were also reports that proper travel and accommodation had not been arranged. The Queen reportedly encouraged Meghan to reconcile with her father.
2.The wedding: Reports suggested Meghan wanted Prince William to walk her down the aisle. The Queen reportedly rejected the idea, and Charles eventually accompanied her partway.
3.The clothing: Meghan reportedly spent around £1 million on clothing in her first year as a Royal, compared with approximately £85,000 for Catherine. Reports also suggested she was unhappy about having to return loaned designer outfits.
4.Royal guidance: The Queen reportedly offered Meghan experienced Royal support, including her equerry and Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh. Meghan allegedly declined, preferring to rely on Harry.
5.Prince William: Reports of uncomfortable interactions and tensions between Meghan and William added to the growing divide between the brothers and their wives.
6.The Archbishop: Meghan and Harry spoke of a private wedding three days before the official ceremony. Archbishop Justin Welby later clarified that no legally recognised marriage had taken place before the public wedding.
7.Nelson Mandela: Meghan reportedly compared celebrations of her wedding in South Africa to those following Mandela’s release from prison. His grandson publicly questioned the comparison.
8.Staff treatment: Reports of bullying and staff complaints became serious enough for Buckingham Palace to commission an external investigation. Several former employees were associated with the media’s description of the “Sussex Survivor Club”. The findings were never fully made public.
9.Catherine and Charlotte: The bridesmaid dress disagreement reportedly left Catherine in tears. Catherine had recently given birth. Yet Meghan later publicly complained during the South African tour that nobody had asked how she was doing. Where was that same consideration for Catherine?
10.Nottingham Cottage: Meghan reportedly disliked the accommodation, despite William and Catherine having lived there after their wedding. Not everyone gets a palace simply because they marry into the Royal Family.
11.Frogmore Cottage: The Queen gifted the couple Frogmore Cottage. Its renovation reportedly cost £2.4 million, initially funded by public money before being repaid by Harry and Meghan.
12.Australia: The 2018 tour attracted reports of staff mistreatment, including allegations involving a hot cup of tea and repeated demands for banana bread. There were also reports of Meghan expressing frustration about not being paid for Royal engagements. Being a working Royal was not a paid acting role.
13.Fiji: Meghan reportedly cut short a market visit. Claims emerged that she was unhappy about not being selected to represent UN Women at an engagement. The circumstances remain disputed.
14.Private holidays: Reports have highlighted numerous holidays taken by Harry and Meghan while dating and during their time as working Royals, alongside their six-week break in late 2019.
15.Finding Freedom: Their spokesperson denied that they had contributed to the biography. However, former communications secretary Jason Knauf later provided evidence that the book had been discussed with Meghan repeatedly, including through emails. That certainly raised questions about the original denial.

text:
PH eyes more Indian BrahMos cruise missile systems - Teodoro 

By Priam Nepomuceno

MANILA – Department of National Defense (DND) Secretary Giberto Teodoro Jr. said the country is looking to acquire more BrahMos cruise missile systems from India to improve its capabilities. 

Teodoro disclosed this during the 3rd Delhi Defense Dialogue, where he participated via video teleconference late Wednesday. 

He said the Philippines is very proud to be the first foreign country to acquire the Indian-made BrahMos cruise missile system, touted to be the fastest in the world. 

In January 2022, former defense secretary Delfin Lorenzana and BrahMos Aerospace director general Atul Dinkar Rane signed a contract for three BrahMos cruise system batteries worth PHP18.9 billion. 

A battery usually consists of three to six launchers, along with monitoring and tracking components, as well as a logistics support vehicle. 

The BrahMos cruise missile can be launched from a ship, aircraft, submarine, or land, and has a top speed of about Mach 2.8 (about 3,400 kph), and can carry warheads weighing 200 kg. to 300 kg. 

This weapon platform is expected to address the military’s weaknesses and vulnerability in sea control, anti-access/area-denial (A2/AD), and coastal and island defense operations. 

"That being said, we hope to increase the number of BrahMos units we have, and we have also shared a wish list on the BrahMos to the Indian authorities in order to make it more tailor-fitted for the Philippine environment," Teodoro said. 

Teodoro thanked India for its trust and confidence in providing the Philippines with very capable weapon systems. 

"And we think it is really a significant step, first, in the trust and confidence that India has in the Philippines, because giving such a capability is also a seal of good housekeeping on the recipient country that the Indian authorities made a determination that the country is responsible and that the country would use it only for defensive purposes and not for any purpose contrary to international law," he said. 

Space technology 

Teodoro said the Philippines is also seeking greater cooperation with India on space technology. 

"A special request to me made by the officials of India was cooperation in space technology, where the President of the Philippines (Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.)  committed (to) cooperating into space technology, and we can offer synergies and potentials for cooperation with the Philippine Space Agency," he said. 

Teodoro said the Philippines can offer an "area for testing space technology" and some Filipinos with expertise in the field. 

"The President has instructed us to enter into an Armed Forces of the Philippines Satellite Acquisition Program, which, of course, India would be a very, very important potential partner for this," he added. (PNA)

text:
On February 1, 1896, a farm worker found the body of a young woman in a field near Fort Thomas, Kentucky. The head had been removed and was not at the scene.

She was identified within days. A shoe dealer traced the maker's stamp inside her shoes to a shop in Greencastle, Indiana, and from there to Pearl Bryan, a 22-year-old farmer's daughter who had left home in late January. She was five months pregnant.

Suspicion fell on Scott Jackson and Alonzo Walling, two dental students in Cincinnati. Jackson had been involved with Bryan, and investigators concluded the pair had taken her across the river and killed her. Both were convicted of murder.

The head was never recovered. The men were reportedly offered a reprieve in exchange for saying where it was, and neither did. Theories circulated for decades that it had been thrown into the Ohio River or destroyed in a furnace at the dental college, but nothing was confirmed.

Jackson and Walling were hanged at Newport on March 20, 1897, the last people executed there. Walling reportedly insisted on his innocence to the end. The missing head is still a local legend in northern Kentucky.

Nissim Hamawi, whose daughter Ela hyd was murdered at Nova, reminds us again of the Jewish treasures of erudition and truth trampled by the world.

"I have already written in the past that one of the most distinctive traits of a true man of spirit is the ability to describe historical processes—those that have already occurred and those that are yet to come—and to clothe them in poetic garb.

Many fine minds before me have already pointed out that the legendary story by S.Y. Agnon, *The Lady and the Peddler*, is not merely a tale of relations between a Jew and a gentile woman, but a chilling allegory of the Jew's self-abnegation before his enemies, 
of his cringing submission to them, and of his willingness to supply them, with his own hands, the very weapons they will use to destroy him.

 Story's opening paragraph:

"He bowed and bowed again (the Jew) before her and drew forth items from the chest and offered them to her, saying, Cast your eyes, my lady (the nations of the world), and do not say there is nothing here. Perhaps this item pleases you, or perhaps this fine object will find favor in your eyes. I beg you, my lady, look and see. She bent down toward his chest and rummaged a bit here and a bit there. She saw a hunter's knife (with which she would try to kill him). She gave him its price and returned to her home. He loaded his chest onto his shoulders and went on his way."

It is hard to imagine a more precise and horrifying depiction of the Jewish reality in our times.

In the midst of one of the most just wars in the history of the State of Israel, 
a war forced upon us in the wake of a barbaric massacre, 
many Jews, in the land and abroad, are engaged in an unceasing supply of fabricated and outrageous blood libels to the enemies of the Jewish people.
(Yemenite field rapes, famine in Gaza, baby-killing as a hobby, and more…)

While our enemies wage an unrestrained campaign of delegitimization against us,
"righteous" ones from our midst do a substantial portion of the work for them. 
Almost no blood libel against Israel fails to find fervent echo [...]

Thus has Israel, with the kind assistance of our own "moralists," been transformed from a state fighting for the lives of its citizens into a Nazi monster in the eyes of parts of the world.

Agnon's peddler sold the lady the knife with which she sought to murder him. The "righteous" peddlers of our day supply our enemies with the cognitive weaponry through which they seek to strip us of the right to exist, to live in our land.

[..]
In Africa, thousands are slaughtered. 
In China, millions are oppressed. 
In Arab countries, massacres, suppression, and persecution are routine affairs. 
The world looks on, shakes its head, shrugs its shoulders, and moves on.

But when Israel fights for its existence, suddenly the conscience of the entire world awakens. some out of a sense of moral superiority, saying behold my beauty,
some out of political blindness,

In the effort to destroy this state operates an industry of propaganda and delegitimization, funded by foreign sources, and the ones operating the "machines" of lies are Jews from our midst.

text:
כבר כתבתי בעבר שאחת מתכונותיו המובהקות של איש רוח אמיתי היא היכולת לתאר תהליכים היסטוריים, כאלה שכבר היו וכאלה שעוד יהיו ולהעניק להם לבוש פואטי..

רבים וטובים לפני כבר עמדו על כך שסיפורו המופתי של ש״י עגנון, ״האדונית והרוכל״, אינו רק סיפור על יחסים בין יהודי לנוכרייה, אלא אלגוריה מעוררת חלחלה על התבטלותו של היהודי בפני אויביו, 
על התרפסותו בפניהם ועל נכונותו לספק להם במו ידיו את כלי הנשק שישמשו להשמדתו.

אגב, עגנון היה איש ימין, שוודאי היום היה זוכה לכינוי משיחי.

וכך נכתב כבר בפסקת הפתיחה של הסיפור:

״חזר והשתחווה (היהודי) לפניה והוציא דברים מן הקופה והציע לה ואמר, תני עיניך גברתי (אומות העולם) ואל תאמרי אין כאן כלום. שמא דבר זה רצוי לך, או שמא חפץ נאה זה ימצא חן בעיניך. בבקשה ממך גברתי הביטי וראי. כפפה עצמה כלפי קופתו ופשפשה קצת כאן וקצת כאן. ראתה סכין של ציידים (שתנסה להרוג אותו בעזרתה). נתנה לו דמיה וחזרה לביתה. טען את קופתו על כתפיו והלך לו.״

קשה לחשוב על תיאור מדויק ומחריד יותר של המציאות היהודית בימינו.

בעיצומה של אחת המלחמות המוצדקות ביותר בתולדות מדינת ישראל, 
מלחמה שנכפתה עלינו בעקבות טבח ברברי, 
עוסקים יהודים רבים, בארץ ומחוצה לה, באספקה בלתי פוסקת של עלילות דם מופרכות ומזעזעות לאויבי העם היהודי.
(אונס שדה תימן, רעב בעזה, רצח תינוקות כתחביב ועוד…)

בעוד אויבינו מנהלים נגדנו מסע דה לגיטימציה חסר מעצורים,
״צדיקים״ מתוכנו עושים עבורם חלק ניכר מן העבודה. 
כמעט אין עלילת דם נגד ישראל שאינה זוכה להדהוד נלהב בתקשורת הישראלית, 
כמעט אין האשמה מופרכת שאינה הופכת לכותרת, 
וכמעט אין שקר שאינו מוצא לו ״עיתונאים״ ישראלים  להפצתו.

כך הפכה ישראל, בעזרתם האדיבה של ״בעלי המוסר״ מתוכנו, ממדינה הנלחמת על חיי אזרחיה למפלצת נאצית בעיני חלקים מן העולם.

הרוכל של עגנון מכר לאדונית את הסכין שבה ביקשה לרצוח אותו. הרוכלים ״הצדיקים״ של ימינו מספקים לאויבינו את הנשק התודעתי שבאמצעותו מבקשים לשלול מאיתנו את הזכות להתקיים, לחיות בארצנו.

והצביעות זועקת לשמיים.

באפריקה נרצחים אלפים. 
בסין מדוכאים מיליונים. 
במדינות ערב מעשי טבח, דיכוי ורדיפה הם עניין שבשגרה. 
העולם מביט,  נד בראשו, מושך בכתפיו וממשיך הלאה.

אבל כשישראל נלחמת על קיומה, לפתע מתעורר מצפונו של העולם כולו. בסך, כמו במצעד, מתייצבים מגיני ״זכויות האדם״, מטיפי המוסר והצדקנים המקצועיים, כולם חמושים בזעם קדוש המופנה כמעט תמיד לאותו יעד, מדינת היהודים.

ואליהם מצטרפים בהתלהבות גם יהודים, 
חלקם מתוך תחושת עליונות מוסרית, לומר ראו מה יפיתי,
חלקם מתוך עיוורון פוליטי, 
וחלקם מתוך איבה עמוקה למדינתם (מן אנומליה הקיימת רק במדינת ישראל)
במאבק להחרבת המדינה הזה פועלת גם תעשיית תעמולה ודה לגיטימציה הנהנית ממימון זר והפועלים על ה״מכונות״ השקר הם יהודים מתוכנו.

ויש לי משימה קטנה לכל אותם מטיפי מוסר.

מצאו לי פוליטיקאי, קולנוען, סופר או עיתונאי פלסטיני שגינה בפה מלא, ללא ״אבל״, ללא הסתייגויות וללא הצדקות, את טבח היהודים בשבעה באוקטובר.

המציאות שאין חיה כזו.

לאחר שואת יהודי אירופה זכה העם היהודי לכמה שנים של אמפתיה עולמית, שלא האריכה ימים. 

לאחר טבח המזוויע של השבעה באוקטובר, האמפתיה נמשכה בקושי ימים ספורים, בטרם התחלפו גילויי הזעזוע בהאשמות כלפי הקורבנות.

וכאן מתעוררת שאלה איומה, אך בלתי נמנעת.

כמה ימי אמפתיה יעניק לנו העולם אם ארגוני הטרור הפלסטיניים יצליחו יום אחד לממש את חזונם ולבצע טבח המוני בתושבי ישראל?

יום? 
יומיים? 
שבוע?

או שאולי עוד בטרם ייקברו המתים כבר יתייצבו אותם ״בעלי מוסר״ היהודים שמתוכנו ויסבירו לעולם מה עשינו כדי להביא את האסון על עצמנו.
ועד כמה הטבח היה מוצדק.

עגנון הבין דבר שאנו מסרבים ללמוד.
לא תמיד צריך האויב לחפש את הסכין. לעיתים היהודי כבר עומד מולו, משתחווה בנימוס ומציע לו לבחור אחת מתוך הקופה.

והטרגדיה הגדולה היא שגם היום, כשהסכין כבר מונפת, יש בינינו מי שעדיין עסוקים בלהשתחוות.

text:
A commendable example of inter-state coordination and collective commitment to wildlife conservation! 

BT1, the tigress from West Bengal’s Buxa Tiger Reserve, has been safely captured in Assam following a coordinated operation involving forest teams from West Bengal and BTR, with support from the district administration, police and local communities.

Released into the wild at Buxa on 2 October 2026, BT1 travelled over 100 km into Assam, eventually reaching Raimona National Park in the Bodoland Territorial Region. From 23 October, she continued moving through forested landscapes before approaching human settlements in Kokrajhar, making timely intervention essential for the safety of both the tigress and nearby residents.

What followed was a carefully coordinated effort across state boundaries. Forest officials from West Bengal and Assam worked together to track her movements, assess the situation and ensure her safe capture.

Wildlife does not recognise administrative boundaries, and incidents like these remind us why cooperation between states is so important for conservation, particularly in landscapes where animal movement extends across protected areas and human settlements.

My heartiest congratulations to the forest teams of West Bengal and Assam, the district administration, police personnel and local communities whose cooperation made this operation possible.

BT1 is safe, and that is what matters most.

An important example of how inter-state coordination can deliver meaningful outcomes for wildlife conservation.

text:
Today feels different.

As I reflect on the election results in the United States, I am hopeful about the possibilities ahead for a kinder, more just, inclusive, and compassionate world. Democracy is never perfect, and progress is never guaranteed, but moments like this remind us that people can choose hope over fear, solidarity over division, and evidence over misinformation.

Canada has been my home since 1989, but I spent six formative years in Ann Arbor, Michigan, where I studied, worked as a registered nurse, and deepened many of the values that continue to guide my professional and public life. Like many Canadians, I have followed U.S. public life closely for decades because what happens there often reverberates far beyond its borders.

What particularly encourages me is the engagement of younger generations and the emergence of bold, progressive leaders, and the millions alongside them, who are helping reshape the public conversation. Together, they are bringing equity, diversity, inclusion, accessibility, climate action, and social justice back into the mainstream, not as political slogans, but as essential principles for building stronger communities, healthier societies, and more responsive democracies.

The challenges before us remain significant: growing inequality, threats to democracy, climate change, attacks on human rights, rising intolerance, and the urgent need to strengthen public services, including health care. Yet this moment offers renewed confidence that these challenges can be met through collective action, respect for one another, and a commitment to the common good.

For me, the lesson is clear. Progress is neither automatic nor permanent. It requires courage, engagement, and leadership. It requires people who are willing to build bridges rather than deepen divisions, and who believe that our common humanity matters more than our differences.

Whether we are advancing democracy, tackling climate change, strengthening health care, or building more equitable societies, the path forward depends on our willingness to lead with inclusion, compassion, and hope.

Today, I am choosing hope. And I am inspired by a new generation of leaders, and by millions of people working alongside them, who are helping build a more equitable, peaceful, and sustainable future for all.

#Democracy #Equity #EDIA #SocialJustice #ClimateAction #Hope #Leadership

text:
The political rise of Abdul El-Sayed represents a significant development in the American political landscape, highlighting the growing importance of inclusive leadership, grassroots mobilization and policy-driven campaigning. His journey from a public health professional to a prominent political figure reflects the potential of leadership rooted in social equity, healthcare accessibility and economic justice.

Before entering politics, El-Sayed served as Detroit’s health director, where he focused on public health challenges, including lead contamination, asthma and healthcare access for vulnerable communities. His professional experience strengthened his credibility and enabled him to address public concerns through practical policy solutions. His earlier gubernatorial campaign in Michigan in 2018 also helped establish a grassroots network of young activists, working-class families and community supporters.

Throughout his political journey, El-Sayed faced criticism and identity-based rhetoric. However, his strategy emphasized substantive issues such as universal healthcare, fair wages, environmental protection and social welfare. By shifting the debate from personal identity to public policy, he sought to build a broad coalition across ethnic, religious and economic groups.

His campaign reportedly relied on decentralized volunteer networks, community engagement and digital outreach rather than extensive traditional advertising. This approach highlighted the growing influence of grassroots participation in contemporary electoral politics. His policy agenda, including proposals for expanded healthcare coverage and environmental reform, also generated discussion about public investment, economic development and regulatory priorities.

The significance of El-Sayed’s political emergence extends beyond Michigan. It reflects the evolving nature of American democracy and the increasing participation of diverse communities in public leadership. His journey challenges traditional barriers and emphasizes the importance of representation, dignity and belonging.

Ultimately, Abdul El-Sayed’s political narrative underscores the value of inclusive governance, evidence-based policymaking and community-driven leadership. His experience offers important lessons for future political candidates, demonstrating that addressing public concerns through a clear policy vision and sustained grassroots engagement can contribute to a more participatory and equitable democratic system.

text:
Laura, you have the ear of the president. This is a brilliant strategy to stop the Democrats in their tracks. Read this from Nana Crass -

"The clock nobody’s showing you.Republicans run both chambers until noon on January 3rd.

That’s about 55 days. Maybe less once people start skipping town.

The government runs out of money December 11th. The stopgap Trump signed September 2nd ends that night. Everybody knows this. Half of them are already acting like it doesn’t matter.

The debt limit, $41.1 trillion, gets hit around May. Drop-dead date around February 2028.

And here’s the part they really don’t want you thinking about.

ICE and Border Patrol are already funded through September 30th, 2029. The big bill last year. The second reconciliation bill this June. Somewhere around $215 billion, already law. Sitting there.

Jeffries can hold a hearing every day for two years. He can yell. He can’t un-sign a single dollar of it.

That’s the model. Everything else in this piece is about putting more of the board in that same box.

Can we nuke the filibuster and fund this thing through 2028?

Everyone’s asking. Here’s the real answer. Not the fantasy one.

Is it legal? Yes.

The Constitution says money gets spent by appropriations made by law. Article I, Section 9. Nowhere does it say one year at a time. Congress has passed full-year funding bills before. VA medical gets funded a year ahead. The ICE money runs five fiscal years. That’s not theory. That’s already done.

Once it’s signed, the only way to undo it is a new law. Trump has to sign that law, or they need two-thirds of both chambers. Fifty-four senators isn’t 67. Not close. Not even in the same neighborhood.

One catch nobody else will tell you about. Article I, Section 8 says Congress can’t appropriate money for the Army for more than two years. December 2026 to December 31, 2028 is more than two years. Write the Army piece to end sooner. The rest is fair game. Don’t get cute with the Army account and the whole thing gets messy.

Are the votes there? No.

Not today. The nuclear option takes 50 Republicans plus Vance. Thune says they aren’t anywhere close. A dozen-plus GOP senators went on record against it during last year’s shutdown. Some of them just lost on Tuesday. Lame ducks with nothing to lose aren’t easier to whip. They’re harder. Some of them are already checked out. Some of them are pissed. Good luck with that.

Would it even do what you want? Only half.

A two-year freeze freezes everything. Every NGO grant. Every program you’re sick of paying for. Freezing isn’t cutting. You’re just locking the current mess in place and hoping they can’t touch it. That’s not the same as taking a knife to it.

So the nuke is the wrong tool even if you had it. And you don’t.

Here’s the right one.

The 50-vote door

Three plays. None of them needs a single Democrat. None of them needs the nuke.

Reconciliation. Can’t be filibustered. Fifty plus Vance.

The House already passed the first step in July, 216 to 214. Defense, intelligence, farmers, elections. It’s been rotting in the Senate. Just sitting there.

Pull it out. Make it bigger. Put defense and munitions money on the same clock as ICE: good through September 2029. And raise the debt limit inside it, big enough to last through the end of the term. That kills their best 2027 hostage before they can grab it. Do it now while you still can.

Rescissions. This is the one that actually goes after the NGO money.

Under the 1974 impoundment law, the President sends Congress a list of money he wants cancelled. Fast track. No filibuster. Fifty-one votes.

We did it last summer. About $9 billion in foreign aid and public broadcasting, gone. Not theory. Done.

That list should hit the Hill Monday, November 9th. Grant by grant. Name them. And it has to pass before January 3rd, because the new Congress will just let it rot on the floor. They won’t even bring it up.

Judges. Every one confirmed in the next 55 days sits for life. Run the floor every night. Don’t stop. Some of these guys aren’t going to show up if you give them an excuse.

Here’s the whole strategy in one sentence.

Don’t fund the whole government for two years. Fund what you care about for three, at 50 votes, and leave the rest on a short leash.

Then when they threaten a shutdown in October 2027, they’re holding their own programs hostage. Not yours.

What they’re going to do to stop it

One word. Clock.

They’ll refuse a long funding deal. They want a short one into January so their majority writes the bills. That’s the play.

They’ll deny consent on everything. Every nominee gets every minute of debate the rules allow. It’ll be ugly. Slow. They know it.

They’ll run to the parliamentarian on every line of reconciliation that smells like policy. Voter ID is first on the list. Expect it.

They’ll force amendment vote after amendment vote all night and turn every one into a 2028 ad. You already know how that goes.

They’ll work the Republicans who just lost. Some of those guys are already gone in their heads.

And they’ll call it a power grab. Every network. Every hour.

Funny. When Democrats lost the House in 2010, their lame duck repealed Don’t Ask Don’t Tell and ratified a treaty with Russia. Nobody called that a power grab. Different rules, I guess.

What they do after January 3rd

Subpoenas. Robert Garcia is already telling people to lawyer up. Trump’s family business. Immigration enforcement. Epstein. Pardons. The whole list.

Impeachment. Jeffries says he’ll run Hegseth out of town. On Trump, “nothing ruled out.” We’ll see.

Bills. Undo the Medicaid changes. Extend Obamacare subsidies. Take tariff power back. End the Iran war. They’ll try.

Blocking. No judges. No nominees. A Supreme Court seat held open until 2029 if one comes up. They can do that.

Now what they can’t do.

They can’t remove him. That’s 67 senators. They don’t have it.

They can’t pass a law without his signature.

They can’t un-spend money already locked through 2029. That’s already done.

Their only real weapons are the next funding fight and the debt limit. So take both off the table now. That’s the whole game. Don’t leave them sitting there.

We’ve seen this exact movie

Go back to 1801. Federalists lose. Their lame duck creates sixteen federal judgeships and Adams fills them on the way out the door. Midnight judges.

Jefferson’s Congress repealed it a year later.

Why could they? Because they had the White House. Simple as that.

Democrats don’t. The veto is the wall. That’s why this works. Don’t forget it.

And 2018. I need everybody to remember 2018.

We lost the House. Trump forced a shutdown over the wall on December 22nd. It ran 35 days straight into Pelosi’s majority. It ended with no wall money. They got to play the heroes who turned the lights back on.

Don’t do that again. Don’t hand them a Christmas shutdown and let them open their majority looking like the adults. Fund our priorities first. Through the 50-vote door. Then the shutdown card is theirs to lose.

The calendar

November 9: Rescission list goes up. Senate starts the budget resolution. Has to happen that week.

Week of November 16: House adopts it. Committees write over Thanksgiving. A lot of people won’t be around. Plan for that.

Every spare hour: judges. Don’t waste the nights.

Early December: Rescissions pass. Get it done.

December 1-11: Reconciliation passes both chambers. Tight.

By December 11: Offer a full-year funding bill with three grant riders. If they won’t take it, short CR. No Christmas shutdown. Don’t give them that.

What to watch

One vote. The Senate budget resolution, the week of November 9th.

If Thune can’t get 50 on that, none of this happens and you’ll know exactly who to call. Don’t sugarcoat it.

If he gets it, the next two years look a hell of a lot different than the people celebrating last night think they do.

They won the votes.

They don’t get the board."
Nana Crass - The Right Way

text:
Swindled 1.7 million after feeding patties and yogurt for an illicit affair. 

A news report from Boralesgamuwa, Neelammahara area states that a chance encounter at the Pettah bus stand on October 25 last year turned into a robbery of property worth over 1.7 million rupees within a few days.

An elderly woman, sixty-four years old, had gone to Pettah for a personal need that day and was waiting for a bus to return home. There, she met a 52-year-old man who claimed to be a Navy officer residing in the Kalutara area. After a brief conversation, an informal acquaintance began between the two. Preliminary police investigations revealed that her phone number had been exchanged with him.

Over the next few days, they exchanged messages over the phone. Based on this acquaintance, at the woman's invitation, the man arrived at her residence in Neelammahara by a hired three-wheeler around 10:45 AM on November 02. At that time, no one else was at home.

Upon arriving at the house, he had brought short eats including cakes, rolls, and patties, as well as a yogurt drink. During a friendly conversation, the woman consumed the yogurt drink he offered. According to a senior police officer, she fell asleep a short while after consuming the drink and only woke up around 5:30 PM that day.

Upon waking, the woman, still in a dazed state, began wandering inside and outside the house, telling various things to neighbors. Meanwhile, a close relative of hers, who also lived in the same house, returned home from work and, thinking that thieves had entered the house, complained to the police via the 119 emergency hotline.

Accordingly, during investigations conducted by Boralesgamuwa Police officers, it was confirmed that this was not an act by external thieves but a robbery committed by the person who had arrived at the invitation of the homeowner.

Police state that during the time the woman was unconscious, he stole her two-sovereign gold necklace and half-sovereign pendant, two half-sovereign rings, a one-and-a-half-sovereign bangle, and a quarter-sovereign ring that were in the wardrobe, as well as her smartphone. The total value of the stolen property exceeds 1.7 million rupees.

Under the instructions of Boralesgamuwa Police Station OIC, Inspector Ruwan Palihawadana, a team including Crime Investigation Division OIC, Sub-Inspector Dimuthu Rathnayake, is conducting further investigations regarding the suspect.

text:
The Script Is a Hostage Note. Netanyahu Is Not Warning About Israel's Survival. He Is Negotiating His Own.

The Prime Minister of the entity stepped before the cameras and warned that a government relying on Arab parties would "dismantle Israel from within." He called the Arab-led factions "Islamist parties of terror supporters." He demanded a "broad national government" led by Likud, under his leadership, excluding the parties that represent a fifth of the citizenry.

Read the statement as a political document, not a security assessment. The man speaking is a defendant in an active criminal trial, the head of a bloc that lost its majority, and the leader of a party whose own coalition partners are the reason the Knesset is deadlocked. Every sentence is addressed to one audience: the members of his own bloc he needs to keep in line.

The arithmetic is the first lie.

The election was held on 27 October. Likud emerged as the largest single party with 27 seats. The pro-Netanyahu bloc secured only 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, short of the 61 needed for a majority. The opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot secured 48, and the Arab-led parties, Ra'am with eight seats and the Joint List with eleven, won a record 19 seats.

The math does not give Netanyahu a path to 61 without the Arab parties. He cannot form a government without them. He has therefore declared them illegitimate. The declaration is not a strategic choice. It is the only move available to a man whose coalition arithmetic has failed and whose opponents are already talking to the parties he has spent a decade demonizing.

The second lie is the "external threat."

Netanyahu told the public before the election that the entity faced an imminent attack. The army contradicted him. Haaretz reported, citing Israeli military sources, that no concrete preparations or operational movements indicating an attack on the entity had been detected. The security establishment had not raised alert levels, called up reservists, or activated emergency personnel. Security officials could not identify which front the Prime Minister was referring to or what intelligence his warning was based on. Opposition parties called it a "political maneuver".

He used the threat of an external war to campaign. The army said the threat was not there.

The third lie is "national unity."

Netanyahu's offer of a "broad national government" is not an offer of unity. It is an offer to keep his outgoing coalition intact. He said explicitly that the arrangement "would not mean dropping the far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties" that were part of his outgoing government. The "unity" government he proposes is the same government that lost the election, with a new label. The four Zionist opposition parties, Yashar, B'Yachad, The Democrats, and Yisrael Beytenu  have all ruled out joining a government led by him.

There is no unity government available to him. There is only the coalition he already had, which the electorate rejected.

The fourth lie is the Arab parties as a "fifth column."

The Joint List is a coalition of Ta'al, Balad, and Hadash an Arab nationalist party, a Palestinian nationalist party, and a left-wing Arab-Jewish communist party. Its leader, Ahmad Tibi, said the Joint List had blocked Netanyahu from forming a government and was ready to help the change bloc replace him. Yousef Jabareen, the Joint List chairman, said: "Anyone who wants to offer a real alternative to Netanyahu's bloodstained government will have to talk to us. We are ready to pave the way for Netanyahu's removal".

These are not terror supporters. They are elected legislators negotiating the terms of their participation in the political system. The "terror supporter" label is the mechanism Netanyahu has used for a decade to exclude them. In 2019, the Joint List accused him of "dangerous and wild incitement" and "spreading lies" by calling its members terror supporters. In 2015, he warned that Arab voters were "heading to the polling stations in droves" and threatened to place cameras at polling places in Arab communities. The label is not an analysis. It is a get-out-the-vote tool for his base and a disqualification mechanism for his opponents.

The fifth lie is the "existential" framing.

Netanyahu said a government backed by Arab parties "will not fight our enemies" and will "simply dismantle us from the inside". The record of the past year contradicts this. The entity's own security establishment has been at war with his government's judicial overhaul, not with the Arab parties. Hundreds of Air Force officers announced they would stop reserve service in protest at the judicial legislation. The former IDF chief of staff, Herzi Halevi, said Netanyahu rejected a proposal to dismiss the reservists who halted duty. President Isaac Herzog sent a warning letter to Netanyahu, the Defense Minister, and the National Security Advisor, stating the entity was "one step away from disaster" because of the wave of nationalist crime in the West Bank, and warning that the use of firearms against Israeli citizens could lead to "civil war".

The threat to the entity's internal cohesion is not the Arab parties. It is the settler violence, the judicial crisis, and the reservist revolt that Netanyahu's own government has produced.

The real file is the trial.

Netanyahu is the first sitting Israeli prime minister to stand a corruption trial. He concluded his own testimony in June 2026 after 98 hearings spread over roughly 18 months. The trial has moved to a five-day weekly schedule as the judges push through the remaining testimony before the presiding judge's planned retirement. He has called the proceedings "10 years of hell".

A prime minister facing a potential conviction cannot afford to lose office. The immunity that comes with the premiership is the only thing standing between him and a verdict. The "broad national government" is not a governing proposal. It is a legal shield. The "Arab terror supporters" are not a security threat. They are the parties that would give Eisenkot the votes to replace him. The "external threat" is not a military reality. It is a campaign device.

The bill.

Likud: 27 seats. Pro-Netanyahu bloc: 53. Opposition bloc: 48. Arab parties: 19. The four Zionist opposition parties have ruled out joining him. The army says the external threat is not there. The President says the entity is one step from civil war. The reservists are refusing service. The trial is running five days a week.

Netanyahu has no path to 61 without the parties he has declared illegitimate. He has no path to legitimacy without the office he is using to delay a verdict. He has no path to "unity" without the coalition that lost the election.

The speech was not a warning about Israel's survival. It was a hostage note from a man whose own survival is on the line. The bill is being paid by the entity's political system, one deadlocked Knesset at a time.
