text:
Americans No Longer Celebrate Mid-Term Landslides the Way They Once Did

The wave of hope and euphoria that once accompanied Democratic victories in the Obama years is nowhere to be seen after the party’s landslide in the recent United States mid-term elections. 

There are no spontaneous overnight parties in the streets, no community-driven campaign fundraisers, and no volunteer parades organised by ordinary citizens. 

Americans have spent enough time examining the machinery of their politics to recognise controlled opposition when they see it. They understand that the two major parties do not offer genuine alternatives so much as they offer alternating sets of actors who ultimately serve the same corporate interests.

It would therefore be a mistake for Democrats to treat the result as a lasting popular mandate. Most observers already know that the party remains capable of launching another overseas war or of staging a fresh campaign against immigrants the moment it needs to divert attention from its failure to deliver free healthcare, free education, or any meaningful reduction in the cost of living. 

The mid-terms functioned more as a referendum against the Trump family, and especially against his degenerate son-in-law Jared Kushner, than as an endorsement of misguided Democratic policy. Kushner’s role in the disastrous Middle East adventurism that produced the Iran war remains fresh in public memory, and voters appear to have punished that record without necessarily embracing the opposition as a solution.

The Democrats remain inside the same system and continue to rely on low-level psychological operations to secure re-election. 

Minnesota congresswoman Ilhan Omar, for example, generated her own surrounding narrative about arrests linked to her immigration status. The episode placed her back in the news cycle and allowed her to solicit sympathy at the precise moment it was useful for her campaign. After four terms in office she has little of substance to point to beyond the increase in her own net worth and that of her husband. The exercise manufactured a sense of camaraderie while steering attention away from the absence of measurable legislative achievement.

Kenya is one of the few countries that still has a realistic chance of stepping outside this pattern. The electorate is not permanently bound to the long list of briefcase parties that circulate before every election. That distance creates the possibility of rejecting both the status quo and the controlled opposition that is presented as its only alternative. 

Citizens can, for instance, set aside the latest World Bank statement claiming that the Standard Gauge Railway was inflated by 117 billion shillings. The figure is offered as if it were new information, yet the same institution has continued to transact with the regime after successive scandals of the same kind. 

The performance changes little about the underlying relationship.

The same scepticism applies to the theatre produced by commercial activists like Boniface Mwangi, Hanifa Adan, Hussein Khalid, and the corrupt mainstream (githeri) media. Their interventions have repeatedly functioned as accessories to the very oppression they claim to expose and oppose, and they can be given a wide berth without any loss of political clarity. 

The mid-term result in the United States shows what happens when a public finally treats both sides of a manufactured contest as part of the same arrangement. Kenya still has the option of refusing that arrangement altogether.

text:
THE MONTGOMERY BUS BOYCOTT: HOW A FEW PEOPLE CHANGED HISTORY

Montgomery, Alabama, United States | 1946–1956

In 1946, a group of African-American women established the Women's Political Council (WPC) in Montgomery, Alabama. Among its founders was Mary Fair Burks, while Jo Ann Robinson later emerged as one of its most influential leaders.

Their concern was simple but significant: the everyday discrimination Black people experienced on public buses. Rather than simply complain about their experiences, these women decided to organise, engage public authorities and demand change.

They held meetings, wrote letters to government officials, educated their communities and consistently challenged discriminatory practices. In 1954, Jo Ann Robinson wrote to Montgomery's mayor, outlining specific complaints about the treatment of Black passengers. Their demands were largely ignored, but they continued organising.

On December 1, 1955, Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to surrender her seat to a white passenger on a public bus. For many, this became the defining moment of a struggle that had been developing for years.

Jo Ann Robinson and other organisers quickly mobilised. They produced and distributed approximately 52,500 leaflets calling on Black residents to boycott the city's buses on December 5. What was initially planned as a one-day protest received overwhelming support. Approximately 90% of Montgomery's Black residents stayed off the buses.

At a subsequent mass meeting, community leaders established the Montgomery Improvement Association, with a young minister, Martin Luther King Jr., elected as its president. The community decided to sustain the boycott.

But they did not stop at making declarations. They organised transportation networks, coordinated volunteers, established communication channels, mobilised churches and raised funds to support the effort. People who owned vehicles offered rides to those who needed them. Others volunteered their time, coordinated meeting points and encouraged their neighbours to remain committed.

For 381 days, thousands of people walked, shared rides and supported one another despite intimidation, arrests and other difficulties.

On November 13, 1956, the United States Supreme Court upheld the ruling that segregation on Montgomery's public buses was unconstitutional. The boycott officially ended on December 20, 1956.

What began with a relatively small group of organised individuals and years of consistent community engagement became a defining moment in America's civil rights movement.

There is something important to learn from this history.

The transformation did not happen because a few people suddenly performed extraordinary acts. It happened because ordinary people committed themselves to doing necessary things consistently. Some organised, some communicated, some mobilised, some provided transportation, some raised funds, and others simply encouraged their neighbours not to give up.

Not everyone was at the forefront. Not everyone had a title. Not everyone was visible. But everyone who contributed to the collective effort played a part in the outcome.

This is the power of sustainable leadership. It is the understanding that meaningful transformation is not always built through grand gestures or extraordinary interventions. Sometimes, it is built through small actions, repeated consistently, by people who share a common vision and are willing to take responsibility.

A handful of committed people can initiate a transformation, but it takes discipline, organisation, shared values and sustained collective effort to make that transformation last.

We may not change everything in one day, but we can change something every day. And when people commit to doing the right things consistently, those small actions can become the foundation of national transformation.

text:
WHAT I'M WATCHING TODAY— THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 5, 2026
Another major earnings session ahead, with AI infrastructure, power, networking, software, insurance and monetary policy all in focus.
For me, the biggest question remains whether strong demand is translating into sustainable revenue growth, free cash flow and attractive returns on invested capital.
MACRO — UK (GMT)
🔹 10:30 AM — UK Construction PMI: 46.1 expected
🔹 1:00 PM — Bank of England Rate Decision
🔹 1:00 PM — BoE Monetary Policy Report and voting breakdown
The Bank of England decision matters for borrowing costs, mortgage affordability and capital-intensive businesses. I'll be watching the voting split and updated inflation and growth forecasts.
MACRO — U.S. (ET)
🔹 6:30 AM — Challenger Job Cuts
🔹 8:30 AM — Initial Jobless Claims: 196K expected
🔹 8:30 AM — Continuing Claims: 1.710M expected
🔹 8:30 AM — Nonfarm Productivity: +2.8% expected
🔹 8:30 AM — Unit Labour Costs: +0.6% expected
🔹 9:50 AM — Fed Hammack Speech
🔹 10:10 AM — Fed Barkin Speech
The productivity and labour-cost numbers interest me most. Stronger productivity with slower labour-cost growth would support corporate margins without necessarily adding inflation pressure.
EUROPE & ASIA
🔹 Japan — BoJ Meeting Minutes and Services PMI
🔹 8:00 AM GMT — Germany Factory Orders
🔹 8:45 AM GMT — France Industrial Production
🔹 11:00 AM GMT — Eurozone PPI
🔹 4:00 PM GMT — ECB President Lagarde Speech
EARNINGS — BEFORE THE BELL
🔹 $CORZ — Core Scientific: AI data-centre contracts, capacity and financing
🔹 $EOSE — Eos Energy: Battery storage, manufacturing scale and cash requirements
🔹 $FOUR — Shift4: Payment volumes, margins and free cash flow
🔹 $OSCR — Oscar Health: Membership growth, medical costs and profitability
🔹 $LMND — Lemonade: Insurance growth and underwriting discipline
🔹 $CMI — Cummins: Power generation and data-centre demand
🔹 $SO — Southern Company: Electricity demand and grid investment
🔹 $DUK — Duke Energy: Utility capital spending and regulated returns
🔹 $APD — Air Products: Industrial gases, capital allocation and returns
🔹 $ACMR — ACM Research: Semiconductor equipment demand
EARNINGS — AFTER THE BELL
🔹 $IREN — AI Cloud revenue, GPU deployment and financing
🔹 $IONQ — Quantum bookings, commercialisation and cash burn
🔹 $NET — Cloudflare: AI traffic, enterprise adoption and margins
🔹 $AAOI — Applied Optoelectronics: Optical networking demand and profitability
🔹 $SMR — NuScale: Nuclear project development and commercial agreements
🔹 $PSIX — Power Solutions International: Data-centre power demand
🔹 $INOD — Innodata: AI data services, growth and customer concentration
🔹 $SOUN — SoundHound AI: Revenue growth and monetisation
🔹 $TEAM — Atlassian: Enterprise software and AI adoption
🔹 $AXON — Axon: Public safety technology and recurring revenue
🔹 $KTOS — Kratos: Defence technology and contract execution
🔹 $OPEN — Opendoor: Housing activity, inventory and liquidity
🔹 $AFRM — Affirm: Consumer credit, transaction growth and profitability
MY MAIN FOCUS
1. $IREN — AI CLOUD ECONOMICS
This is my biggest earnings focus.
I'll be watching AI Cloud revenue, GPU deployment, utilisation, contracted capacity, financing and cash flow.
Rapid infrastructure expansion means little if it cannot eventually generate attractive returns.
2. $CORZ — DATA-CENTRE CONTRACTS AND FINANCING
Contracted power and capacity are important, but so are development timelines, financing costs and the conversion of infrastructure into revenue.
3. $NET + $AAOI — AI NETWORKING
Cloudflare and Applied Optoelectronics offer different exposures to the AI networking opportunity.
I'm watching demand, customer adoption, pricing, margins and whether AI-related growth is becoming financially meaningful.
4. $IONQ — QUANTUM COMPUTING
The long-term opportunity is substantial, but commercial economics remain early.
Bookings, revenue conversion, customer adoption and cash burn matter more to me than announcements alone.
5. $EOSE + $SMR + $PSIX + $CMI — POWER FOR AI
Power availability is becoming a critical constraint on AI infrastructure development.
I'll be watching manufacturing capacity, project execution, financing and how quickly demand converts into profitable revenue.
6. $FOUR — PAYMENTS AND VALUATION
Shift4 remains interesting to me.
Processing volumes, gross revenue less network fees, integration execution, margins and free cash flow will help determine whether the valuation deserves a re-rating.
7. $INOD + $SOUN + $TEAM — AI SOFTWARE MONETISATION
AI adoption is one thing. Profitable monetisation is another.
I'm focused on revenue quality, customer concentration, recurring revenue and operating leverage.
8. $AXON + $KTOS — DEFENCE TECHNOLOGY
Demand for public safety and defence technology remains an important investment theme, but backlog conversion, execution and valuation still matter.
9. $SO + $DUK + $APD — UTILITIES AND INDUSTRIAL INFRASTRUCTURE
Growing electricity demand is encouraging, but I want to see how capital spending translates into regulated or contracted returns.
10. $OSCR + $LMND — INSURANCE ECONOMICS
Growth needs to be supported by disciplined underwriting.
I'll be watching medical costs, loss ratios, customer economics and profitability.
MY TAKE
Tomorrow brings another important test of the investment themes I've been following.
AI demand remains strong, but demand alone doesn't guarantee attractive shareholder returns.
The framework I'm watching remains:
Capital → Power → Data centres → Compute → Networking → Utilisation → Revenue → Free cash flow → ROIC
And with central bank policy, labour-market data and productivity figures also in focus, the cost of financing remains part of that equation.
AI demand creates the opportunity. Execution, cash flow and returns determine who ultimately benefits.

text:
Staff engineer comp breakdown (rough ranges, not exact, varies a lot by company/stage):

1) Base (US): $210k–$320k
   - Tier 1 cities often +10–25%
   - Remote from lower-cost regions can be -10–30%
   - Some orgs compress Staff vs Senior base and push upside into equity

2) Bonus: 10–25% target
   - Cash-heavy companies: higher target, stricter payout bands
   - Often tied to company scorecard, not just your perf

3) Equity (annualized grant value): $150k–$600k+
   - Public: more predictable, refreshers matter
   - Private: paper math, ask about dilution, strike, and secondary options
   - Equity usually scales hardest with scope, not years

4) Total comp: $350k–$900k+ common band for Staff in big tech / top public
   - Late-stage private can match on paper, but risk profile is different

5) Scope expectations that map to higher bands:
   - Own a multi-service area: reliability + cost + delivery, not just code
   - Lead 1–3 quarters of roadmap across 2–6 teams
   - Set standards: incident process, SLOs, on-call load, tooling, migrations
   - Move hard numbers: p99 latency, error rate, infra spend, deploy frequency

6) Negotiation inputs companies actually use:
   - Level (Staff vs Sr Staff): 1 step can be +$100k–$300k TC
   - Location band + competing offers
   - Criticality: payments/auth/infra tends to price higher than internal tools
   - On-call expectations (frequency, pages/week, incident ownership)

If they're lucky enough to get somebody out of the Air Force, sure.

That's not the reality.  And they need pilots.

"In the United States, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) mandates a minimum of 1,500 flight hours to obtain an unrestricted Airline Transport Pilot (ATP) certificate, which is required to serve as a pilot in Part 121 airline operations.  This rule, enacted in 2013 following the Colgan Air crash, applies to both captains and first officers at major U.S. airlines.
However, the FAA offers a Restricted ATP (R-ATP) certificate for eligible pilots, allowing them to fly as first officers with fewer hours:

750 hours for eligible military pilots.

1,000 hours for graduates of an FAA-approved four-year aviation degree program.

1,250 hours for graduates of an FAA-approved two-year aviation degree program.

While 1,500 hours is the federal minimum, major carriers like Delta, United, and American Airlines often prefer or require 2,000 to 2,500+ hours for competitive hiring, whereas regional carriers may accept candidates closer to the 1,250–1,500 hour threshold.  Globally, most other countries require only 250 hours for a commercial pilot license, making the U.S. requirement significantly higher."

text:
During a recent visit to China's Hangzhou Green and Low-Carbon Digital Energy Port, Parth Kumar of CSE explored how a 30-year-old industrial area is being transformed into a digitally integrated, low-carbon industrial ecosystem.

His article in @down2earthindia highlights some distinctive features of the industrial park in China that offer interesting insights for India's existing industrial clusters and upcoming industrial parks/cities:

🔹 Retrofitting without expanding: The project transformed an existing 0.61 sq km industrial estate, home to over 1,000 enterprises, without acquiring a single inch of land.

🔹 Measurable park-level climate targets: By 2030, the park aims to reduce annual emissions by 8,717 tonnes, lower carbon-emission intensity by 45.9% and generate over 12.15 million kWh of solar electricity annually.

🔹 From energy consumer to energy prosumer: The park integrated solar, wind, multiple battery storage technologies, bidirectional EV charging (used as storage during peak) and a 31.9 MW virtual power plant to generate, store and manage energy within the park.

🔹 Digitalization and real-time intelligence: A central digital platform connects over 3,000 pieces of equipment, with live dashboards displaying and tracking energy generation, consumption, storage, power demand and carbon emissions. This enables continuous monitoring and data-driven management of the entire industrial park.

🔹 A living laboratory for clean-tech innovation: Sixteen enterprises based in the park contribute to an ecosystem of around 200 technologies and solutions spanning advanced solar cells, battery storage, smart grids and virtual power plants. The Park also showcases emerging technologies such as direct air carbon capture (DAC), microbial carbon capture and industrial waste-gas utilization.

text:
📜 THIS DAY IN DIPLOMATIC HISTORY
        November 5, 1779

The King of England wrote to the Empress of Russia, called her "Sister," and begged for her help. George III was losing his war in America, now that France and Spain had joined it against him, and he wanted Catherine the Great to throw her fleet onto his side. She did send her fleet to sea. But not to his side. She sent it to defend the sea trade of the northern neutral states against his own navy.

On November 5, 1779, George III addressed a flattering and anxious letter to Catherine II. He praised her genius and the breadth of her vision, warned that his enemies were openly boasting of plans to turn all Europe upside down, and pleaded that even a show of Russian naval force might scatter the league forming against him and restore the balance of Europe. He wanted peace, he wrote, but only a peace that preserved the rights of his crown. He signed himself her affectionate brother.

Catherine had no wish to rescue George. Worse for Britain, she had a grievance of her own. British warships, enforcing the blockade of France and Spain, were stopping and seizing neutral merchant ships, Russia's among them, on London's claim that Britain alone might search any vessel and decide what counted as contraband. Catherine an opportunity far greater than anything George was offering.

Instead of lending Britain her fleet, she turned the neutral powers against it. On February 28, 1780, she issued a declaration of armed neutrality whose principles struck at the root of British sea power. A neutral ship, it held, might sail freely between the ports of warring states and carry their goods, save only true war material such as arms and munitions. And a blockade was binding only where warships actually stood to enforce it, not a paper blockade of whole coastlines proclaimed from a desk in London. To give the words teeth, Catherine sent squadrons of the Russian navy to sea.

Denmark and Sweden joined that same year, and the League of Armed Neutrality took shape. Over the next three years Prussia, Austria, Portugal and the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies added their names to it. The Dutch Republic, the great shipper and banker of the age, was about to join when Britain, to prevent it, declared war on the Dutch first. Britain now found nearly every maritime neutral in Europe ranged against its claim to rule the seas as it pleased.

By defending neutral trade, Catherine undercut Britain’s blockade of its enemies and indirectly helped the US. The Americans understood it at once. In October 1780 the president of the Continental Congress, Samuel Huntington, wrote to St. Petersburg that Congress was instructing its warships and its envoys to respect the principles of the armed neutrality, and asked that its thanks be carried to its "great and good" friend as soon as could be. The United States, itself a belligerent and no neutral at all, embraced the neutrals' rules because they weakened the enemy.

The League never fought a battle. The Royal Navy outmatched all its fleets combined, and Catherine herself privately mocked her own creation as an "armed nullity." Its strength lay not in its guns but in its diplomacy. It isolated Britain, stripped away the free hand it had claimed on the oceans, and planted in international law the principle that free ships make free goods, which would echo through the whole century that followed.

Britain kept trying to win Catherine over. In 1781, as Russia and Austria jointly offered to mediate a peace, George III offered to hand her the Mediterranean island of Minorca if only she would use that mediation in Britain's favour. Catherine kept the role of mediator and declined the gift. The mediation came to nothing in the end, because Britain and France chose to settle directly with each other.

👉Meetings with companies such as Snowflake and PayPal offered further insights into innovative technology solutions and how these could help support the growth of our ecosystem.

I would like to personally thank Saeed Amidi for his warm welcome in Sunnyvale and for his genuine interest in helping us build stronger bridges between Cyprus and the world.

ethereum:0x57e114b691db790c35207b2e685d4a43181e6061 — ETHENA
⠀
A $2.45 BILLION cryptocurrency.
⠀
A synthetic dollar protocol managing approximately $4.6 BILLION in assets.
⠀
More than $17 MILLION in fees over the last 30 days.
⠀
And a proposed mechanism designed to convert protocol economics into ENA buybacks.
⠀
But here's the contradiction.
⠀
Ethena has built one of DeFi's largest synthetic dollar ecosystems.
⠀
Yet ENA holders don't automatically receive the income generated by USDe.
⠀
And the protocol's most important revenue-sharing mechanism depends on supply milestones.
⠀
Is ethereum:0x57e114b691db790c35207b2e685d4a43181e6061  an undervalued bet on the future of crypto-native dollars?
⠀
Or is the market overestimating how much Ethena's success will benefit its governance token?
⠀
Let's examine the numbers. 👇
⠀
01 | WHAT IS ETHENA?
⠀
Ethena is a synthetic dollar protocol built on Ethereum.
⠀
Its flagship product is USDe, a crypto-native dollar designed to maintain a value near $1.
⠀
The ecosystem includes:
⠀
• USDe — Synthetic dollar
• sUSDe — Staked, yield-bearing USDe
• ENA — Governance token
• sENA — Staked ENA
• Delta-hedged collateral strategies
• Stablecoin integrations
• DeFi lending markets
• Institutional distribution partnerships
⠀
Unlike conventional fiat-backed stablecoins, USDe uses a combination of collateral, hedging strategies, and other approved backing assets.
⠀
Its design aims to create dollar exposure without relying exclusively on traditional bank deposits.
⠀
But USDe is not risk-free cash.
⠀
02 | HOW DOES ETHENA GENERATE YIELD?
⠀
Ethena's economics are built around multiple income sources.
⠀
STAKING YIELD — Returns from eligible staked collateral.
⠀
FUNDING PAYMENTS — Income that can arise from short perpetual futures positions.
⠀
BASIS TRADING — Returns from differences between spot and derivatives prices.
⠀
OTHER RESERVE INCOME — Returns from eligible backing assets and approved strategies.
⠀
The basic concept is delta hedging.
⠀
Ethena can hold crypto collateral while using short derivatives positions to offset directional price exposure.
⠀
But here's the critical distinction.
⠀
Delta-neutral doesn't mean risk-neutral.
⠀
Funding rates can turn negative.
⠀
Exchange counterparties can fail.
⠀
Liquidity can deteriorate.
⠀
And hedges can become less effective during extreme market conditions.
⠀
03 | THE BIG NARRATIVE
⠀
Three narratives define Ethena.
⠀
CRYPTO-NATIVE DOLLARS
⠀
Building dollar-denominated assets for blockchain financial markets.
⠀
ON-CHAIN SAVINGS
⠀
Providing yield exposure through sUSDe.
⠀
PROTOCOL VALUE CAPTURE
⠀
Exploring mechanisms that connect Ethena's economic performance to ENA.
⠀
The opportunity is substantial.
⠀
Stablecoins are among crypto's clearest real-world use cases.
⠀
But the investment thesis for ENA is different from the adoption thesis for USDe.
⠀
USDe can succeed as a financial product without automatically making ENA a superior investment.
⠀
04 | THE COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE
⠀
Ethena has several meaningful strengths.
⠀
• A large synthetic dollar ecosystem
• Established DeFi integrations
• Multiple potential yield sources
• Significant institutional backing
• An existing distribution network
• A dedicated reserve framework
• Expanding stablecoin infrastructure
⠀
Against $USDT and $USDC, Ethena offers a different reserve and yield model.
⠀
Against $DAI and $USDS, it competes for decentralized dollar liquidity and savings demand.
⠀
Against other basis-trading protocols, it benefits from established scale and integrations.
⠀
But yield isn't a permanent competitive advantage.
⠀
When funding opportunities decline, competitors with different reserve structures may offer more attractive returns.
⠀
05 | THE NUMBERS THAT MATTER
⠀
November 5, 2026 snapshot:
⠀
ENA Price: ~$0.183
⠀
Market Cap: ~$2.46B
⠀
FDV: ~$2.75B
⠀
Circulating Supply: ~13.4B ENA
⠀
Maximum Supply: 15B ENA
⠀
Circulating Ratio: ~89.4%
⠀
24H Trading Volume: ~$531M
⠀
All-Time High: ~$1.52
⠀
Decline From ATH: ~88%
⠀
ETHENA USDE:
⠀
Protocol TVL: ~$4.6B
⠀
30D Fees: ~$17.25M
⠀
30D Tracked Protocol Revenue: ~$93K
⠀
Cumulative Fees: ~$1.07B
⠀
Cumulative Tracked Revenue: ~$333M
⠀
Tracked sUSDe Supply APY: ~5.2%
⠀
The valuation question is interesting.
⠀
ENA's market capitalization is roughly 53% of Ethena USDe's TVL.
⠀
But TVL is not shareholder equity.
⠀
And protocol assets are not profits belonging to ENA holders.
⠀
06 | THE REVENUE QUESTION
⠀
This is where the numbers require careful interpretation.
⠀
Ethena generated approximately $17.25 million in tracked fees over 30 days.
⠀
But DefiLlama reports only around $93,000 in protocol revenue under its current methodology.
⠀
Why the difference?
⠀
Its fee metric includes staking returns, yield distributions, mint fees, and other qualifying income.
⠀
Its narrower revenue metric includes mint fees and amounts allocated to the reserve fund.
⠀
Neither figure should automatically be treated as distributable income for ENA holders.
⠀
The protocol has meaningful economic activity.
⠀
But the central question is how much of that activity becomes sustainable net value available for ENA buybacks.
⠀
Gross yield isn't tokenholder profit.
⠀
07 | THE ENA FEE SWITCH
⠀
This is potentially ENA's most important fundamental catalyst.
⠀
In August 2026, Ethena proposed a milestone-based fee switch.
⠀
Under the proposed framework, revenue allocation toward ENA buybacks would increase as USDe supply reaches higher thresholds.
⠀
The proposed thresholds include:
⠀
$7.5B USDe Supply — 5% Gross Revenue Allocation
⠀
$10B — 10%
⠀
$15B — 15%
⠀
$20B — 20%
⠀
The proposal also outlines directing 95% of qualifying net revenue received by the Ethena Foundation toward ENA buybacks once the first milestone is reached.
⠀
But here's the distinction.
⠀
These are proposed economic mechanisms, not evidence of currently active buybacks at every threshold.
⠀
With Ethena USDe TVL around $4.6 billion, the first $7.5 billion supply threshold is not currently met.
⠀
Investors should verify governance approval, actual USDe circulating supply, executed purchases, and how purchased ENA is handled.
⠀
A buyback proposal isn't equivalent to a completed buyback.
⠀
08 | THE TOKENOMICS QUESTION
⠀
ENA has a fixed maximum supply of 15 billion tokens.
⠀
Approximately 13.4 billion are reported circulating.
⠀
That leaves roughly 1.6 billion outside reported circulation.
⠀
But tokenomics are more complicated than subtracting circulating supply from maximum supply.
⠀
Ethena announced changes to its investor unlock arrangements in August 2026, including purchases of certain locked investor allocations and accelerated release arrangements.
⠀
As a result, older vesting schedules may not accurately reflect current liquid supply.
⠀
Different tracking providers also report materially different unlocked percentages.
⠀
This creates an important analytical requirement.
⠀
Investors must distinguish:
⠀
• Tokens vested
• Tokens unlocked
• Tokens circulating
• Tokens held by strategic entities
• Tokens actually available for sale
⠀
An unlock doesn't guarantee immediate selling.
⠀
But a high reported circulating percentage doesn't eliminate concentration or distribution risk.
⠀
09 | THE USDE RISK QUESTION
⠀
Ethena's strongest business opportunity also creates its most important risks.
⠀
USDe depends on effective reserve management, hedging, liquidity, and counterparty arrangements.
⠀
Potential vulnerabilities include:
⠀
• Negative perpetual funding
• Derivatives exchange failures
• Custodial or settlement disruptions
• Stablecoin depegging
• Smart-contract exploits
• Liquidity shortages
• Regulatory restrictions
⠀
The reserve fund is designed to help absorb certain losses.
⠀
But no reserve structure can guarantee protection against every extreme scenario.
⠀
There's another important tradeoff.
⠀
If more revenue is redirected toward ENA buybacks, less may be available for user yields or ecosystem incentives.
⠀
That could weaken the competitiveness of sUSDe.
⠀
A sustainable fee switch must balance tokenholder value capture with product growth.
⠀
10 | THE FINAL VERDICT
⠀
Ethena has built a substantial crypto-native dollar business.
⠀
Its strengths include:
⠀
• Approximately $4.6B in tracked TVL
• Significant historical fee generation
• Established stablecoin distribution
• Multiple income strategies
• DeFi integrations
• A proposed ENA value-capture framework
⠀
But the risks are significant.
⠀
THE BULL CASE:
⠀
USDe supply expands.
⠀
Ethena maintains attractive risk-adjusted yields.
⠀
Institutional adoption increases.
⠀
The fee switch reaches its activation thresholds.
⠀
Verified ENA buybacks begin.
⠀
And token demand grows faster than liquid supply.
⠀
THE BEAR CASE:
⠀
USDe growth stalls.
⠀
Funding yields compress.
⠀
Competing stablecoins attract deposits.
⠀
Counterparty risks increase.
⠀
ENA buybacks remain inactive or economically modest.
⠀
And token distributions outweigh new investment demand.
⠀
What would strengthen my conviction?
⠀
• Sustained USDe supply growth
• Transparent net revenue reporting
• Verified ENA buybacks
• Strong reserve coverage
• Stable peg performance
• Improved tokenholder value capture
• Lower uncertainty around liquid supply
⠀
THE BOTTOM LINE
⠀
ethereum:0x57e114b691db790c35207b2e685d4a43181e6061 is not simply another DeFi governance token.
⠀
It's a potential investment in the economics of a multibillion-dollar synthetic dollar ecosystem.
⠀
Approximately $2.46 billion in market capitalization.
⠀
Around $4.6 billion in protocol TVL.
⠀
More than $17 million in monthly tracked fees.
⠀
And a proposed framework for directing future revenue toward ENA purchases.
⠀
But here's the contradiction.
⠀
Ethena has already demonstrated substantial product demand.
⠀
ENA has not yet demonstrated equally strong, consistent value capture from that demand.
⠀
The next major catalyst isn't another USDe integration.
⠀
It's evidence that growing stablecoin adoption can translate into sustainable net revenue and executed ENA buybacks.
⠀
Bookmark this analysis before the next DeFi rotation.
⠀

⠀

litecoin:native — LITECOIN
⠀
A $4.2 BILLION cryptocurrency.
⠀
More than 154,000 daily transactions.
⠀
Average transaction fees below ONE CENT.
⠀
And a maximum supply of just 84 MILLION coins.
⠀
But here's the contradiction.
⠀
Litecoin has operated since 2011, survived multiple market cycles, and maintained an established global payment network.
⠀
Yet LTC trades around $54, nearly 87% below its all-time high.
⠀
With the next halving approaching in 2027, is litecoin:native  an overlooked Proof-of-Work asset?
⠀
Or has Bitcoin captured the scarcity narrative while stablecoins capture payment demand?
⠀
Let's examine the numbers. 👇
⠀
01 | WHAT IS LITECOIN?
⠀
Litecoin is a decentralized Proof-of-Work cryptocurrency launched in October 2011.
⠀
Created by Charlie Lee, it was designed to support faster and less expensive transactions than Bitcoin.
⠀
Its ecosystem includes:
⠀
• Peer-to-peer payments
• Merchant transactions
• Scrypt Proof-of-Work mining
• Segregated Witness
• Lightning Network compatibility
• MimbleWimble Extension Blocks
• Noncustodial wallets
• Exchange settlement
⠀
Litecoin targets approximately 2.5-minute block times, compared with Bitcoin's 10-minute target.
⠀
But faster confirmations don't automatically make LTC a superior monetary investment.
⠀
02 | WHERE DOES DEMAND COME FROM?
⠀
LTC has three primary demand drivers.
⠀
PAYMENTS — Users acquire LTC to transfer value at relatively low cost.
⠀
MONETARY DEMAND — Investors hold LTC as a scarce, independently operated cryptocurrency.
⠀
NETWORK UTILITY — Transactions, wallet transfers, and optional MWEB activity create blockchain usage.
⠀
But here's the distinction.
⠀
LTC doesn't offer native staking yields.
⠀
It doesn't distribute corporate profits.
⠀
And low transaction fees mean miners currently receive relatively little revenue from fees.
⠀
Its long-term value depends primarily on sustained demand for the asset itself.
⠀
03 | THE BIG NARRATIVE
⠀
Three narratives define Litecoin.
⠀
DIGITAL PAYMENTS
⠀
Supporting inexpensive, permissionless transfers.
⠀
FIXED-SUPPLY MONEY
⠀
Maintaining a predetermined maximum supply of 84 million LTC.
⠀
PRIVACY-ENHANCED TRANSACTIONS
⠀
Providing optional confidential transaction amounts through MWEB.
⠀
The opportunity is meaningful.
⠀
But Litecoin competes with Bitcoin, stablecoins, and newer payment networks.
⠀
Low fees are useful.
⠀
They aren't sufficient to guarantee market-share growth.
⠀
04 | THE COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE
⠀
Litecoin has several established strengths.
⠀
• Approximately 15 years of operating history
• Fixed maximum supply
• Low transaction fees
• Faster target blocks than Bitcoin
• Established exchange liquidity
• Scrypt mining infrastructure
• Dogecoin merged mining
• Optional MWEB functionality
⠀
Against $BTC, Litecoin emphasizes faster base-layer confirmations and inexpensive payments.
⠀
Against bitcoin-cash:native, it competes as an established Proof-of-Work payment network.
⠀
Against dogecoin:native, it offers a fixed maximum supply rather than perpetual fixed-amount issuance.
⠀
But its biggest weakness is differentiation.
⠀
Bitcoin dominates the digital scarcity narrative.
⠀
Stablecoins offer price stability for payments.
⠀
Litecoin must demonstrate why users should choose LTC over both.
⠀
05 | THE NUMBERS THAT MATTER
⠀
November 5, 2026 snapshot:
⠀
Price: ~$54.33
⠀
Market Cap: ~$4.23B
⠀
Circulating Supply: ~77.79M LTC
⠀
Maximum Supply: 84M LTC
⠀
Circulating Ratio: ~92.6%
⠀
24H Trading Volume: ~$192M
⠀
All-Time High: ~$410.26
⠀
Decline From ATH: ~86.8%
⠀
LITECOIN NETWORK:
⠀
Daily Transactions: ~154,306
⠀
Daily Active Addresses: ~212,637
⠀
Average Transaction Fee: ~$0.0028
⠀
Average Block Time: ~2.6 Minutes
⠀
Network Hashrate: ~2.7 PH/s
⠀
Block Reward: 6.25 LTC
⠀
Daily Miner Fees: ~8.65 LTC
⠀
Daily Block Subsidies: ~3,569 LTC
⠀
MWEB Holdings: ~519,500 LTC
⠀
Next Halving: Approximately July 2027
⠀
Now consider the valuation.
⠀
Litecoin processes more than 150,000 transactions per day.
⠀
That's meaningful network activity.
⠀
But transaction counts alone don't reveal unique users, merchant adoption, or economic settlement demand.
⠀
The important question is whether that activity creates sustained reasons to acquire and hold LTC.
⠀
06 | THE TOKENOMICS QUESTION
⠀
Litecoin follows a Bitcoin-like monetary schedule.
⠀
Maximum Supply: 84M LTC
⠀
Current Block Reward: 6.25 LTC
⠀
Halving Interval: 840,000 Blocks
⠀
Next Halving Block: 3,360,000
⠀
Expected Next Halving: July 2027
⠀
At the next halving, the block reward falls to 3.125 LTC.
⠀
At the target block interval, daily issuance would decline from approximately 3,600 LTC to 1,800 LTC.
⠀
That's a reduction of approximately 657,000 LTC in annualized issuance.
⠀
But here's the distinction.
⠀
Lower issuance doesn't guarantee higher prices.
⠀
A halving reduces newly created supply.
⠀
It doesn't automatically increase demand.
⠀
The bullish case requires demand to remain stable or grow while new issuance declines.
⠀
07 | THE MINING SECURITY QUESTION
⠀
Litecoin uses the Scrypt mining algorithm.
⠀
Its network currently operates around 2.7 PH/s of estimated hashrate.
⠀
Litecoin also supports merged mining with Dogecoin.
⠀
Compatible miners can help secure both blockchains through auxiliary Proof of Work.
⠀
That creates an important security relationship between the two networks.
⠀
But here's the risk.
⠀
Mining profitability depends on block rewards, transaction fees, asset prices, and operating costs.
⠀
After the 2027 halving, LTC block subsidies decline by 50%.
⠀
Dogecoin rewards may help support combined mining economics.
⠀
But merged mining doesn't eliminate concentration or security risks.
⠀
Investors should monitor mining pool concentration, hashrate, profitability, and network reliability.
⠀
08 | THE MWEB OPPORTUNITY
⠀
Litecoin activated MimbleWimble Extension Blocks in 2022.
⠀
MWEB provides optional confidential transaction amounts and additional privacy functionality.
⠀
Recent blockchain data indicates approximately 519,500 LTC held within MWEB.
⠀
At the current LTC price, that represents roughly $28 million.
⠀
But here's the distinction.
⠀
MWEB balances don't directly measure payment adoption.
⠀
And privacy features can create regulatory and exchange-listing challenges.
⠀
The strongest bullish evidence would be sustained MWEB usage alongside broader Litecoin payment adoption.
⠀
Privacy is a meaningful product feature.
⠀
But its economic contribution must be demonstrated.
⠀
09 | THE MINER REVENUE QUESTION
⠀
Litecoin's low transaction fees are attractive to users.
⠀
But they create a long-term security-budget challenge.
⠀
Recent network data shows approximately 8.65 LTC in daily transaction fees.
⠀
During the same period, miners received roughly 3,569 LTC in block subsidies.
⠀
Transaction fees therefore accounted for only about 0.24% of combined mining rewards.
⠀
That's an important distinction.
⠀
Most direct Litecoin mining compensation currently comes from newly issued LTC.
⠀
As halvings continue, the network will increasingly depend on LTC's price, transaction fees, and the economics of merged mining.
⠀
The challenge is maintaining strong security while preserving inexpensive payments.
⠀
10 | THE FINAL VERDICT
⠀
Litecoin has one of crypto's longest operating histories.
⠀
Its strengths include:
⠀
• Established Proof-of-Work security
• A fixed maximum supply
• Low-cost transactions
• Broad exchange accessibility
• Optional privacy functionality
• Dogecoin merged mining
• A predictable halving schedule
⠀
But its risks remain significant.
⠀
THE BULL CASE:
⠀
Payment adoption expands.
⠀
LTC maintains strong liquidity.
⠀
The 2027 halving reduces new issuance.
⠀
MWEB adoption increases.
⠀
And sustained demand strengthens LTC's scarcity premium.
⠀
THE BEAR CASE:
⠀
Bitcoin continues dominating monetary demand.
⠀
Stablecoins capture payment activity.
⠀
LTC struggles to attract new users.
⠀
Mining economics weaken after the halving.
⠀
And LTC continues underperforming competing monetary assets.
⠀
What would strengthen my conviction?
⠀
• Sustained growth in genuine payment activity
• Higher economically meaningful transaction volume
• Increasing merchant adoption
• Stable mining security after the halving
• Greater MWEB usage
• Stronger LTC performance relative to BTC
⠀
THE BOTTOM LINE
⠀
litecoin:native is one of the most established cryptocurrencies still operating today.
⠀
Approximately $4.2 billion in market capitalization.
⠀
More than 154,000 daily transactions.
⠀
Over 92% of maximum supply already circulating.
⠀
And another halving approaching in 2027.
⠀
But here's the contradiction.
⠀
Litecoin has demonstrated durability.
⠀
Its network is inexpensive to use.
⠀
And its monetary supply is predictable.
⠀
Yet it remains nearly 87% below its historical peak.
⠀
The next major catalyst isn't simply the halving itself.
⠀
It's evidence that reduced issuance can meet sustained payment and investment demand.
⠀
A scarce asset without growing demand can remain cheap for years.
⠀
Bookmark this analysis before the next Proof-of-Work rotation.
⠀
Which has the strongest long-term monetary thesis?
⠀
litecoin:native, bitcoin-cash:native, or $BTC?
⠀
And can Litecoin convert its long operating history into renewed adoption?
⠀
Or will Bitcoin and stablecoins continue capturing most of the market?
⠀
Drop your pick below. 👇
⠀

ethereum:0x1f9840a85d5af5bf1d1762f925bdaddc4201f984  — UNISWAP
⠀
A $4.7 BILLION cryptocurrency.
⠀
Over $64 BILLION in monthly DEX trading volume.
⠀
Approximately $83 MILLION in monthly trading fees.
⠀
And more than $8 MILLION in monthly protocol revenue.
⠀
But here's what changed.
⠀
After years of functioning primarily as a governance token, UNI now has an active mechanism connecting protocol fees to token burns.
⠀
Uniswap is no longer just a successful decentralized exchange with a governance token.
⠀
Its trading activity can now directly reduce UNI supply.
⠀
Is ethereum:0x1f9840a85d5af5bf1d1762f925bdaddc4201f984 becoming one of DeFi's strongest value-accrual assets?
⠀
Or is the market overestimating how much trading revenue UNI can actually capture?
⠀
Let's examine the numbers. 👇
⠀
01 | WHAT IS UNISWAP?
⠀
Uniswap is a decentralized exchange protocol that allows users to trade cryptocurrencies through automated market makers.
⠀
Instead of relying on traditional centralized order books, Uniswap uses liquidity pools supplied by market participants.
⠀
Its ecosystem includes:
⠀
• Uniswap V2, V3, and V4
• Concentrated liquidity
• Automated market makers
• UniswapX
• Unichain
• Cross-chain liquidity infrastructure
• Governance
• Protocol fee collection
• UNI token burns
⠀
Uniswap operates across approximately 50 blockchain networks.
⠀
UNI is its governance token, with an additional economic role through the protocol's fee-to-burn mechanism.
⠀
But owning UNI doesn't represent conventional equity ownership in Uniswap Labs.
⠀
02 | WHERE DOES DEMAND COME FROM?
⠀
UNI has two major sources of utility.
⠀
GOVERNANCE — Holders can delegate voting power and participate in protocol decisions.
⠀
PROTOCOL FEE BURNS — Eligible protocol fees are converted into permanent UNI supply reductions.
⠀
This second mechanism is particularly important.
⠀
Under the current architecture, collected fees accumulate in on-chain contracts.
⠀
Independent participants can claim those assets by burning the required amount of UNI.
⠀
That creates an economic connection between trading activity and token supply.
⠀
But here's the distinction.
⠀
UNI holders don't receive automatic dividends.
⠀
And every dollar of trading fees doesn't become a dollar of UNI burns.
⠀
The relevant metric is protocol revenue actually captured and converted into token destruction.
⠀
03 | THE BIG NARRATIVE
⠀
Three narratives define Uniswap.
⠀
DECENTRALIZED EXCHANGE INFRASTRUCTURE
⠀
Providing permissionless token trading across multiple blockchains.
⠀
TOKEN VALUE ACCRUAL
⠀
Connecting protocol revenue to UNI burns.
⠀
ON-CHAIN FINANCIAL MARKETS
⠀
Expanding into tokenized assets, advanced liquidity infrastructure, and cross-chain execution.
⠀
The opportunity is substantial.
⠀
As more assets move on-chain, decentralized trading infrastructure could capture growing financial activity.
⠀
But Uniswap faces competition from $CAKE, $RAY, solana:JUPyiwrYJFskUPiHa7hkeR8VUtAeFoSYbKedZNsDvCN, and other trading ecosystems.
⠀
The strongest protocol won't necessarily be the one with the highest historical trading volume.
⠀
It will be the one that retains liquidity while generating sustainable revenue.
⠀
04 | THE COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE
⠀
Uniswap has several established strengths.
⠀
• One of DeFi's most recognized brands
• Deep liquidity across major networks
• Extensive developer integrations
• Concentrated liquidity technology

⠀
01 | WHAT IS DOGECOIN?

⠀

⠀
• Peer-to-peer payments
• Digital tipping
• Merchant payments
• Proof-of-Work mining
• Community-driven adoption
• Exchange trading
• Wallet infrastructure

⠀
But its biggest advantage isn't technological complexity.
⠀
It's global recognition.
⠀
02 | WHERE DOES DEMAND COME FROM?
⠀

⠀
PAYMENTS — Users transfer DOGE between wallets and payment recipients.

SPECULATION — Traders buy DOGE based on market cycles and sentiment.
⠀
COMMUNITY — A globally recognized brand supports awareness and adoption.
⠀
EXCHANGE LIQUIDITY — DOGE is widely available across major trading platforms.
⠀
CULTURAL RELEVANCE — Social media attention can attract new market participants.
⠀
But here's the critical distinction.
⠀
Dogecoin doesn't offer native staking yields.
⠀
It doesn't have a protocol revenue-sharing mechanism.
⠀

⠀
Its valuation depends primarily on market demand for the asset itself.
⠀

THE ORIGINAL MEMECOIN

DIGITAL PAYMENTS

Dogecoin's global recognition creates a powerful distribution advantage.

A cryptocurrency can dominate social media while generating relatively little on-chain economic activity.
⠀
The strongest long-term DOGE thesis requires cultural relevance to evolve into sustained demand.

Investors should distinguish exchange custody transfers from actual whale accumulation or distribution.

• Growing wallet adoption
• Sustainable network activity

• Long operating history

More than 156 billion coins in circulation.

binancecoin:native — BNB CHAIN

A $92 BILLION cryptocurrency.

More than 2 MILLION active addresses in a single day.

Over 15 MILLION daily transactions.

Approximately $5.3 BILLION locked in DeFi.

And nearly $1.2 BILLION worth of BNB destroyed in its latest quarterly burn.

Yet BNB is trading around $702.

Almost 49% below its all-time high.

Here's the contradiction.

BNB Chain is processing millions of transactions.

Its token supply continues shrinking.

But the market is still valuing BNB far below its historical peak.

Is binancecoin:native one of crypto's strongest established infrastructure assets?

Or is its valuation already too large to offer attractive long-term returns?

Let's examine the numbers. 👇

**01 | WHAT IS BNB?**

BNB is the native cryptocurrency of the BNB Chain ecosystem.

Originally launched in 2017 as Binance's exchange token, BNB evolved into the foundational asset of a broader blockchain network.

Today, the ecosystem includes:

• BNB Smart Chain
• opBNB
• BNB Greenfield
• Decentralized exchanges
• Lending protocols
• Stablecoin infrastructure
• Tokenized assets
• Gaming and consumer applications
• Staking and governance

Unlike many tokens built around future promises, BNB already supports an operating blockchain ecosystem.

But there's an important distinction.

BNB Chain activity is not the same as Binance exchange revenue.

And owning BNB does not mean owning equity in Binance.

Those are separate economic relationships.

**02 | WHERE DOES DEMAND COME FROM?**

BNB has several established demand drivers.

GAS FEES

Users need BNB to pay transaction fees on BNB Smart Chain.

STAKING

BNB participates in the network's validator and delegation system.

GOVERNANCE

BNB holders can participate in supported network governance processes.

ECOSYSTEM ACTIVITY

Applications, traders, and infrastructure providers use BNB throughout the network.

BINANCE UTILITIES

BNB also retains exchange-related utilities, including eligible trading fee discounts and participation programs.

TOKEN BURNING

BNB's supply reduction mechanisms permanently remove tokens from circulation.

The economic structure is relatively straightforward.

Network activity creates demand for blockspace.

BNB is required to pay for that blockspace.

And part of the network's fee mechanism destroys BNB.

But transaction growth doesn't automatically translate into proportional token price appreciation.

That depends on fee levels, token demand, staking behavior, and broader market conditions.

**03 | THE BIG NARRATIVE**

Three narratives define BNB.

HIGH-VOLUME BLOCKCHAIN INFRASTRUCTURE

Supporting millions of daily transactions at relatively low costs.

EXCHANGE-CONNECTED ECOSYSTEM

Benefiting from brand recognition, distribution, and infrastructure associated with the broader Binance ecosystem.

DEFLATIONARY TOKEN ECONOMICS

Reducing the outstanding BNB supply through scheduled and activity-linked burns.

The combination is unusual.

Many blockchain tokens have significant inflation.

BNB instead has an established supply reduction framework.

But scarcity alone doesn't create value.

Demand must remain strong.

A shrinking supply can support price appreciation when demand is stable or increasing.

It cannot prevent losses when demand falls.

**04 | THE REAL COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE**

BNB Chain has several important strengths.

• Large existing user base
• High transaction throughput
• Low transaction costs
• Established DeFi applications
• Significant stablecoin liquidity
• EVM compatibility
• Broad exchange support
• An established validator network
• A long operating history

Against $ETH, BNB Chain competes through cost, accessibility, and transaction capacity.

Against $SOL, it competes for high-frequency trading activity, consumer applications, and speculative liquidity.

Against $TRX, it competes for stablecoin transfers and payments.

But here's the challenge.

Low fees attract users.

They can also limit revenue generated per transaction.

And EVM compatibility makes it easier for applications to migrate between competing chains.

The real competitive advantage must come from sustained users, liquidity, and developer activity.

**05 | THE NUMBERS THAT MATTER**

November 5, 2026 snapshot:

Token: BNB

Price: ~$702

Market Cap: ~$92.3B

Circulating Supply: ~131.51M BNB

Current Total Supply: ~131.51M BNB

24H Trading Volume: ~$1.44B

All-Time High: $1,370.55

ATH Date: October 13, 2025

Decline From ATH: ~48.8%

BNB CHAIN ACTIVITY:

DeFi TVL: ~$5.33B

Stablecoin Market Cap: ~$13.2B

Daily Active Addresses: ~2.09M

Daily Transactions: ~15.49M

Daily DEX Volume: ~$895M

7D DEX Volume: ~$5.45B

Daily Chain Fees: ~$305K

Daily Chain Revenue: ~$30.5K

Daily Application Revenue: ~$604K

Now consider the valuation.

BNB has a market capitalization above $90 billion.

Its tracked DeFi TVL is approximately $5.3 billion.

That creates a market-cap-to-DeFi-TVL ratio above 17x.

But that isn't a conventional earnings multiple.

TVL measures deposited assets, not company revenue.

And BNB's value depends on more than DeFi deposits.

The important question is whether the broader network can continue supporting a valuation of this magnitude.

**06 | THE TOKENOMICS ADVANTAGE**

BNB has one of the more established supply-reduction mechanisms among major cryptocurrencies.

Its initial supply was approximately 200 million tokens.

The long-term Auto-Burn target is 100 million BNB.

Current outstanding supply is approximately 131.51 million.

That means the network has already removed a substantial portion of its original supply.

And approximately 31.5 million additional BNB would need to be eliminated to reach the 100 million target, assuming no other supply changes.

But here's the important distinction.

The 100 million figure is a burn target.

It is not a future token unlock.

And BNB's current supply isn't expected to expand through a conventional large venture-capital vesting schedule.

That differentiates BNB from many newer Layer 1 tokens.

However, supply reduction doesn't eliminate market risk.

**07 | THE $1.2 BILLION BURN**

On October 19, 2026, BNB Chain completed its 37th quarterly burn.

Total BNB Burned:

1,646,196.44 BNB.

Approximate Value at Burn:

$1.197 BILLION.

Remaining Supply at Announcement:

131,512,085 BNB.

That's approximately 1.24% of the pre-burn supply removed in a single quarterly event.

The network uses two important burn mechanisms.

AUTO-BURN

A quarterly mechanism based on BNB's price and blockchain production parameters.

REAL-TIME BURN

A portion of transaction gas fees is burned through BEP-95.

These mechanisms operate differently.

The quarterly Auto-Burn isn't simply a distribution of Binance exchange profits.

And the real-time burn links part of the supply reduction to blockchain activity.

But investors should avoid a common mistake.

A $1.2 billion burn doesn't mean $1.2 billion of new buying pressure entered the market.

Burning existing tokens reduces supply.

It isn't economically identical to purchasing that amount of BNB on an exchange.

The distinction matters.

**08 | THE REVENUE QUESTION**

BNB Chain has substantial economic activity.

But network activity and token-holder revenue are not interchangeable.

DefiLlama recently reported approximately:

$305K in daily chain fees.

$30.5K in daily chain revenue.

$604K in daily application revenue.

These metrics describe different economic flows.

Chain fees represent payments associated with network usage.

Chain revenue measures a narrower portion retained under the data provider's methodology.

Application revenue belongs to applications operating on the network.

It does not automatically accrue to BNB holders.

That means the entire economic output of BNB Chain should not be treated as BNB token-holder earnings.

The most direct token-economic mechanisms remain gas demand, staking, and burning.

For investors, the critical question is whether these mechanisms generate sufficient value relative to BNB's market capitalization.

**09 | THE BIGGEST RISKS**

BNB has an established ecosystem.

But that doesn't make it risk-free.

CENTRALIZATION

BNB Chain's validator structure is more concentrated than some competing blockchain networks.

That creates governance and censorship-resistance tradeoffs.

REGULATORY EXPOSURE

BNB's historical relationship with Binance creates potential exposure to regulatory and reputational developments.

COMPETITION

Ethereum, Solana, Tron, and other networks compete for developers, users, and liquidity.

LOW-FEE ECONOMICS

High transaction volume doesn't necessarily produce high network revenue when fees remain extremely low.

VALUATION

At approximately $92 billion in market capitalization, BNB requires substantial economic relevance to support further appreciation.

ECOSYSTEM QUALITY

High transaction counts can include bots, speculative activity, and automated trading.

Not every transaction represents a unique human user.

And the most important risk?

A strong blockchain can continue growing while its token underperforms.

Technology adoption and investment returns aren't the same thing.

**10 | THE FINAL VERDICT**

BNB has several characteristics that distinguish it from smaller speculative Layer 1 tokens.

It has:

• An established operating blockchain
• Millions of daily active addresses
• Significant stablecoin liquidity
• Billions in DeFi deposits
• Broad trading accessibility
• Established token utility
• A transparent burn framework
• A shrinking outstanding supply

But the investment case must be evaluated against its existing valuation.

**THE BULL CASE:**

BNB Chain maintains strong user growth.

Stablecoin and DeFi activity expands.

Applications attract more sustainable demand.

BNB remains essential for network fees and staking.

And continued burns reduce outstanding supply.

That combination could support long-term token demand.

**THE BEAR CASE:**

Competing chains capture market share.

Transaction activity becomes increasingly dominated by low-value automation.

Network fee generation remains modest.

Regulatory or governance concerns intensify.

And the market assigns a lower valuation to BNB despite continued ecosystem activity.

What would strengthen my conviction?

• Sustained growth in economically meaningful transactions
• Increasing stablecoin settlement activity
• Higher organic application revenue
• Strong developer retention
• Transparent validator decentralization
• Continued burn execution
• Durable demand beyond speculative trading

Because the strongest blockchain investment isn't necessarily the one with the most transactions.

It's the one where sustained economic activity creates durable demand for its native asset.
⠀
**THE BOTTOM LINE**

binancecoin:native is no longer simply an exchange token.

It's a major blockchain asset supporting a large ecosystem.

Approximately $92 billion in market capitalization.

More than 15 million daily transactions.

Around $13 billion in stablecoins.

Over $5 billion in DeFi TVL.

And an established mechanism designed to reduce supply toward 100 million BNB.

But here's the contradiction.

BNB has significant adoption.

Yet the token remains almost 49% below its historical peak.

Its supply continues shrinking.

But the network's direct fee revenue remains relatively modest compared with its valuation.

The investment thesis is stronger than a simple burn narrative.

BNB's long-term value depends on whether its ecosystem continues attracting real users, liquidity, and economically meaningful activity.

The next major catalyst isn't just another quarterly burn.

It's evidence that network growth translates into durable BNB demand.

Bookmark this analysis before the next Layer 1 rotation.

Which has the strongest long-term investment thesis?

binancecoin:native , $ETH, or $SOL?

And can BNB's shrinking supply and expanding ecosystem support a return toward its previous highs?

Or is its current valuation already pricing in too much future growth?

Drop your pick below. 👇

text:
Beijing released Jilin-1 satellite images of Taiwan on 25 October that it claimed showed every single street in Taipei. Ten days later, on 4 November, America's vice president blamed the Republicans' loss of Congress on Trump's war with Iran. One event is a welcome delivered via a long lens. The other may dictate what Japanese families pay for fuel this winter.

On 4 November, Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for China's Taiwan Affairs Office, praised these new images from Jilin-1, a commercial Chinese satellite. The pictures captured Sun Moon Lake and every street in Taipei. Zhu said they allow people on both sides of the Strait "clearly see Taiwan's cities, fields, salt pans, wetlands and harbors, and take in the splendor of the mountains and seas of the motherland's treasure island." This relies on the phrase 祖国宝岛 zǔguó bǎodǎo ('the motherland's treasure island'). While it reads like a tourist brochure in English, the Chinese possessive is precise: the island belongs to the motherland, and a camera pointed down from space is the proof.

During that same briefing, Zhu praised Shanghai traffic police for returning a handbag lost by Taiwanese actor Ming Dao at a highway service area on 14 October, just 15 minutes after he left it behind. Zhu then called the mainland "one of the safest regions in the world." From the same podium, she defended coast guard patrols east of Taiwan. For those in Taiwan, the invitation to visit and the reminder that Beijing can see their street have merged into one message.

Meanwhile, Democrats hold at least 228 House seats and 54 Senate seats following the 3 November midterms. Vice President Vance wrote on X, as Yomiuri reports: "The reason we lost is the war." He noted that voters told him they would return if the US ends the war, focuses on the cost of living, and reviews its relationship with Israel. Trump insists the Iran operation was necessary. Looking toward 2028, Vance has broken with Trump's defense of the war, even as both men play down a rift.

Tokyo is watching because Asahi identifies the gasoline price spike from the Iran war as the core of voter anger. Japan imports almost all its crude oil from the Middle East and pays in dollars. If Washington continues fighting, oil prices could remain high, meaning households in Japan may pay more to heat their homes. That pressure could ease if Vance's position wins out.

Beijing may see an opening here. Regarding a possible US-China-Russia summit in Shenzhen, foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning has shifted from saying there is "no information to provide" to stating that China "is maintaining communication with the relevant parties," a phrase that specifies no one. A president trapped by domestic failure wants a foreign victory, and China would be the stage. However, any sanctions relief Trump offers Moscow could face a hostile Congress starting in January. Consequently, photographs may outnumber deals.

⛽ The Adevărul opinion piece says this could include 𝐚𝐝𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐟𝐮𝐞𝐥 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐦𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐝 𝐥𝐨𝐠𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐥 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬, although no precise sum has been made public.

🗓️ A decision on the future U.S. force posture in Europe is expected in 𝐃𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐦𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔, although the exact content and timing of the announcement remain uncertain.

🌊 Nicușor Dan told Colby that the 𝐁𝐥𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐒𝐞𝐚 𝐢𝐬 𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐦𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐠𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐮𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐠𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 and argued that a stronger American military and economic presence in Romania has strategic value.

🛡️ MApN says the talks also covered 𝐚𝐢𝐫 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐦𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐥𝐞 𝐝𝐞𝐟𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞, 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫-𝐝𝐫𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐚𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬, critical infrastructure protection and improvements to facilities used by U.S. forces.

🏭 Romania also expressed interest in deeper cooperation with the United States in 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧, 𝐦𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐥𝐨𝐠𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐥 𝐬𝐮𝐩𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭, not only troop deployment.

🇵🇱 The article compares Bucharest’s approach with the 𝐏𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐬𝐡 𝐦𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥, where host-country financial support is combined with infrastructure investment, national military capacity and industrial cooperation.

💡 𝐖𝐇𝐀𝐓 𝐈𝐒 𝐑𝐎𝐌𝐀𝐍𝐈𝐀 𝐀𝐂𝐓𝐔𝐀𝐋𝐋𝐘 𝐓𝐑𝐘𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐓𝐎 𝐁𝐔𝐘 𝐖𝐈𝐓𝐇 𝐓𝐇𝐈𝐒 𝐎𝐅𝐅𝐄𝐑?

text:
🚨 TED BUNDY'S FINAL HOURS: THE LAST NIGHT OF A SERIAL KILLER

Ted Bundy had spent years deceiving people with his charm, intelligence and seemingly respectable personality. But as January 24, 1989, approached, even he couldn't hide his fear of death.

Bundy was one of America's most notorious serial killers, suspected of murdering dozens of women and girls across several states. He was 42 years old and had spent nearly a decade on death row.

What happened during his final 24 hours is particularly disturbing.

On January 23, just hours before his scheduled execution, Bundy gave his final recorded interview to psychologist and religious broadcaster James Dobson.

During the interview, he spoke about his childhood exposure to pornography and claimed that violent pornography had contributed to his murderous urges.

He repeatedly discussed how his obsession had developed over the years. Although he said he accepted responsibility, he also spent considerable time directing attention towards pornography and society.

At one point, when asked whether he was afraid of dying, Bundy admitted:

"I don't want to die, I'm not going to kid you."

He also spoke about drawing strength from his religious beliefs, saying that millions of people had experienced death before him.

But behind those words, his fear was becoming increasingly difficult to conceal.

THE FINAL NIGHT

Bundy reportedly wept several times during his final interview.

When the US Supreme Court rejected his last appeals around midnight, his remaining hope of escaping execution disappeared.

Prison officials described him as visibly shaken and emotional.

He spent his final hours praying with Methodist minister Fred Lawrence. He also made two final telephone calls to his mother in Washington to say goodbye.

He was offered a traditional last meal of steak, eggs, hash browns, toast and coffee.

He refused to eat.

THE EXECUTION

On the morning of January 24, 1989, Bundy was escorted to Florida State Prison's execution chamber.

The electric chair was nicknamed "Old Sparky."

Around 42 witnesses watched as the execution took place.

When asked whether he had any final words, Bundy turned towards his lawyer, Jim Coleman, and minister Fred Lawrence.

His final words were:

"Jim and Fred, I'd like you to give my love to my family and friends."

At 7:16 AM, Theodore Robert Bundy was pronounced dead.

OUTSIDE THE PRISON

The reaction outside was extraordinary.

Hundreds of people had gathered before sunrise. Some wore T-shirts reading "Burn Bundy" and "Toast Ted."

When news of his execution spread, people cheered, hugged each other and celebrated.

Some had travelled long distances just to witness the moment.

After years of fear, grief and unanswered questions, many felt that justice had finally been served.

The man who had manipulated people for years, escaped custody twice and terrorised countless families had finally run out of chances.

One thing remains particularly striking about his final hours: the confidence and composure he had displayed for years were replaced by fear when he finally faced his own death.

What are your thoughts on Ted Bundy's final interview and his attempt to explain the reasons behind his crimes?

TRUMP VS. IRAN: WHEN THE SHERIFF REALIZES HE’S OUT OF BULLETS
By @BPartisans 

Donald Trump wanted to go down in history as the president who would impose peace by force. Instead, he’s likely to be remembered as the one who managed the feat of losing a war politically without ever winning it militarily. And, as the icing on the electoral coffin, to hand both chambers of Congress to the Democrats.

According to Axios, the billionaire now faces three options. Three doors, three dead ends. Welcome to Donald Trump’s geopolitical casino, where the house loses, but it’s always the taxpayers who foot the bill.

Option one: bomb more. The preferred method of strategists who confuse military might with political acumen. Eight months of war haven’t brought Tehran to its knees? So what! All it would take is to start over, harder, longer, and more expensively. A brilliant strategy consisting of treating a hemorrhage with a chainsaw.

Second option: negotiate. But here’s the thing, the Iranians have fully understood that Trump has just taken an electoral beating. Why offer him today the concessions he failed to secure through bombing? In Tehran, they could now present him with the bill, with interest.

Third option: economically strangle Iran. Naval blockade, sanctions, financial pressure. In short, indefinitely prolonging a war that we claim to want to end immediately. A marvel of Trumpian logic: since we can’t win, let’s orchestrate a slow-motion defeat.

And while Washington searches for the emergency exit, Netanyahu continues to demand airstrikes. He wants to continue his standoff with Tehran, but with American planes, American billions, and, if necessary, American coffins. Proxy patriotism, a particularly cost-effective specialty when you’re not footing the bill yourself.

Even JD Vance is starting to find the bill hard to swallow. The vice president openly attributes the Republican rout to this war and is questioning the relationship with Israel. When the sheriff’s own lieutenants start counting the electoral casualties, it usually means the triumphant ride looks more like a headlong rush.

The most grotesque figure remains Trump himself. He acknowledges that the war contributed to his defeat, but insists he would do it all over again. Here, then, is a man capable of identifying his mistake while claiming the right to repeat it.

The real trap is no longer Iranian. It is narcissistic. Making peace would amount to acknowledging the limits of his power. Resuming the bombings could turn his electoral setback into a strategic disaster.

Trump wanted to bring Iran to its knees. He is discovering that reality does not negotiate with oversized egos.

And now, his most dangerous adversary may no longer be in Tehran, but in his own mirror.

text:
The Quiet Hour 🍿 🎥 💥 
 
The city of Oakhaven has a single, absolute rule. From 8:00 PM to 8:00 AM, the streets must be empty. All lights must be extinguished. All sound must cease. For 12 hours, the only authorized activity is silence. This is the premise of The Quiet Hour, an understated, intense indie thriller that explores acoustic surveillance, obedience, and the sound of fear itself.
The film follows Clara (played with quiet intensity by a newcomer), an archivist who manages the digital remnants of "the loud time" before the Event. The movie never explicitly states what the Event was, but its consequences define the very architecture of the city, which is covered in massive, acoustic dampening panels. Every movement, every breath, and every creaking floorboard is a potential death sentence. The entities that hunt the sound are never seen, but their presence is felt in the agonizing stillness they enforce.
The suspense is derived not from sudden scares, but from the prolonged, excruciating anticipation of volume. The most dramatic scenes involve simple tasks: navigating a apartment floor known for its loose planks, trying to open a jar, or, in one masterfully constructed sequence, dealing with an unexpected cough.
What makes The Quiet Hour interesting is how it forces the audience into a state of heightened sensory awareness. It has been described as an exercise in "forced empathy." As Clara moves through her environment, the viewer mimics her behavior, becoming hyper-aware of their own surroundings the rustle of a program, the crunch of a piece of popcorn. When a sound is inevitably made, it crashes into the silence with the force of an explosion, making every mistake feel like a monumental failure.
It is a film that demands total attention and offers a profound, unsettling reflection on what we lose when we trade our voices for safety. In a media landscape dominated by maximalism and noise, The Quiet Hour proves that sometimes, the most powerful stories are the ones you can barely hear.

text:
🚨FORENSIC REPORT PGP TELEGRAM PGP SIGNED #URUGUAYO1337 🇺🇾

Section one, purpose. This document accompanies a PGP-signed Telegram export deposited at archive dot org slash details slash result underscore two zero two six one one zero five. 

It contains first-hand messages from the account uruguayo1337 spanning May twentieth through May twenty-ninth, twenty twenty-six, including self-identification, an offer to provide a declaration before arrest, and real-time reaction to media reports of an impending detention. 

The purpose is to place this material before @CERTuy, the Dirección General de Cibercrimen, and URCDP with a clear chain of custody, so that any institutional response is documented rather than silent.Section two, material description. 

The export is a standard Telegram JSON export of a personal chat named Aaaa, chat ID eight six one three six one eight nine one zero. Sender ID for the other party is user eight six one three six one eight nine one zero. 

Alberto Daniel Hill's sender ID is user five five zero four zero one one four three. The file is ninety-one thousand nine hundred eighty-nine bytes. It was exported from Telegram Desktop, hashed, and signed with a PGP key using SHA-five-twelve. Two signature files were generated. The signed JSON and signatures were packaged into a zip archive of ten thousand three hundred ninety-four bytes and uploaded to Internet Archive on November fifth, twenty twenty-six.Section three, timeline. 

May twentieth, six forty in the morning: the other party opens with "Buenas Alberto, qué tal?" At five thirty-eight in the afternoon they write "Tengo informacion," "lamentablemente," "de primera mano," "sobre todo el caso pampaleaks." At five forty-one they add "(mi declaracion)" and "ejem." At five forty-two they state "vladimir hizo parte de lo que se lo acuso, no tendra conocimiento tecnico, pero si fue participe del deface a buquebus y alguna cosa mas," and "siendo ya mayor de edad." 

At five forty-three: "sabes quien soy yo?" At five forty-four: "la prensa acaba de decir que en unas horas yo iba a estar detenido y estoy aca en mi casa tranquilo." At five forty-six they write a long message alleging that Mauro Eldritch behaves similarly to ExPresidents and that in a direct attack on ExPresidents, Mauro appears insulting him privately — "a no ser que sean la misma persona." At five forty-seven: "yo no participe en ningun hackeo luego del 15 de abril del 2025," and "fecha de mi mayoria de edad." At five forty-nine: "Pampa sigue operando, yo le tendria mas miedo a el." At five fifty: "si amenazas de esas recivi, fotos en la puerta de casa." At five fifty-one through five fifty-four: "pampa no es un grupo, es una persona," "a mi actualmente se me acusa de ser pampa," "lo cual no es verdad." At six twelve: "estan hace años persiguiendo a un uruguayo en el cual encarcelaron a 1 persona y esperan a otra mas con el deseo de agarrarlo pero no lo atrapan, no saben ni su nombre," and "esto le va a pegar a juan pablo de marco, que fue el que lo subio." At six fourteen: "habla por hablar, sin chequear nada," "intenta conseguir la primicia, asi sea sin verificar nada." At six nineteen: "es un hijo de mil puta." At six twenty: "concentrando en encontrar alguna manera de trabajar de todo lo que se, pero no encuentro nada," "18 años," "terminando el liceo," "no lo termine," "desde mi mayoria de edad no" — referring to selling bases. At seven twelve: "yo quiero laburar remoto para irme del pais." At ten nineteen: "no consigo donde entrar," "todos piden demasiada cosa," "carrera en ingenieria," "años de experiencia." May twenty-first, twelve nineteen: 

Alberto shares his telegram link t dot me slash cybermidnight and says "pero si queres que publique algo tuyo, decime que no hay drama y vos no te comprometes." May twenty-first, ten fifty-one at night: "che," "curioso esto," "fuiste vos el hijo de mil puta que dijo mentiras mias," "y de santiu?" May twenty-eighth, eleven fifty-six: Alberto writes "si ya pampa me conto todo," "no hay codigos," "commo andas?" At twelve oh eight he sends the PDF "Análisis Ciberseguridad La Verdad sobre PampaLeaks y BCA LTD." May twenty-ninth, twelve ten: two X post links about the TuID case and the hacker's story.Section four, what it proves. One: the account holder self-identified as uruguayo1337 in a private message to Alberto Daniel Hill on May twentieth, twenty twenty-six, timestamped and logged by Telegram. Two: he offered a declaration — "(mi declaracion)" — before any arrest occurred. Three: he described receiving threats including photos at his door. Four: he stated he was eighteen, had not finished liceo, and had stopped selling bases since reaching majority age. Five: he named Juan Pablo De Marco as the person who uploaded material. Six: he claimed Pampa is a person, not a group, and denied being that person. Seven: he said he did not participate in any hacking after April fifteenth, twenty twenty-five, the date of his majority.Section five, what it does not prove. It does not prove who created or operated the ExPresidents accounts. It does not prove BCA fabricated them. It does not prove Mauro Cáceres and Mauro Eldritch are the same person. It does not prove any specific individual committed the TuID breach. It is one party's account of events, contemporaneous but unverified by independent forensics.Section six, corroborating public context. PampaLeaks' own May twentieth statement, reported by Eduardo Preve, called uruguayo1337 an ex-collaborator used as a prestanombre for payments and Bitcoin mixing, and explicitly said he was "their decoy and nothing more." Spear dot cx's thread from the group says the same. Wikipedia, El Observador, and LARED21 confirm BCA identified him via a Telegram-to-phone link and that his channels continued operating after arrest. Antel's filing to URCDP admits the TuID breach originated from automated cédula queries against an exposed API. DataBreaches independently documented the ExPresidents red flags — one-hour BCA response lag, thirty-nine point six kilobyte samples, zero cross-forum reputation — and stopped at correlation. BCA's Mauro Eldritch then contacted DataBreaches demanding the company name be removed from their article.Section seven, chain of custody. Telegram Desktop export, JSON, ninety-one thousand nine hundred eighty-nine bytes. SHA-five-twelve hash generated and recorded. PGP signature with SHA-five-twelve applied by Alberto Daniel Hill. Two signature files produced. Zipped with signatures into a ten thousand three hundred ninety-four byte archive. Uploaded to Internet Archive November fifth, twenty twenty-six, item result underscore two zero two six one one zero five.
