Nature and the Communist Manifesto
— John Bellamy Foster
“The bourgeoisie, during its rule of scarce one hundred years, has created more massive and more colossal productive forces than have all preceeding generations together. Subjection of Nature’s forces to man, machinery, application of chemistry to industry and agriculture, steam-navigation, railways, electric telegraphs, clearing of whole continents for cultivation, canalization of rivers, whole populations conjured out of the ground—what earlier century had even a presentiment that such productive forces slumbered in the lap of social labor?”

IN THE COMMUNIST Manifesto Marx and Engels referred to “the subjugation of nature” and to the “idiocy of rural life.” They saw history as generally progressive in character and lauded technological advances. Their analysis of the revolutionary role of the proletariat paid scant attention to environmental factors. Were Marx and Engels then anti-ecological thinkers by today’s standards, as some have charged, and is the Manifesto to be classified as one of the great anti-ecological documents of all time?

Most contemporary commentators on Marx and Engels and the environment have been highly critical of the founders of historical materialism. This is to be expected, given not only the tendency within the hegemonic political culture to evade Marx and his ideas, but also the sorry performance of Soviet-type societies with respect to the environment. Still, the range and intensity of the accusations directed against Marx on ecological grounds far exceed those leveled at any other thinker.

For example, Victor Ferkiss and Gary Snyder cite the reference to “the idiocy of rural life” in the Manifesto as evidence that Marx and Engels believed in the domination of the country by the town. Anthony Giddens insists that Marx’s “concern with transforming the exploitative human social relations expressed in class systems does not extend to the exploitation of nature.” Jean-Paul Deléage and Ward Churchill accuse Marx of denying any intrinsic value to nature, as a result of his adherence to the labor theory of value, which saw labor power as the sole source of value under capitalism. Robyn Eckersley and Ted Benton claim that Marx was “anthropocentric” rather than “ecocentric” and that he supported the subordination of nature to human purposes.*

All of these criticisms can be refuted directly. Rather than celebrating the dominance of town over country, Marx and Engels argued (in the Manifesto as well as elsewhere in their thought) that this antagonistic division needed to be abolished under communism through an “equable dispersal of population across the country,” “combination of agriculture with manufacturing industries,” elimination of both the intellectual degradation (“idiocy”) of rural society and the physical degradation of urban society, etc.

Far from denying that nature was exploited, Marx and Engels referred explicitly throughout their works to the fact that the earth or SOIL was “exploited,” in the sense of being “robbed” of its nutrients under capitalism—part of the same process that included the exploitation of workers in both city and country. This formed the basis of Marx’s critique of capitalist agriculture. Hence, even as early as the Manifesto the “improvement of the SOIL generally in accordance with a common plan” was stipulated as a necessary condition for communism.

The map of Nevada resembles a guillotine blade. Its shape is defined by a flat northern border, a straight eastern boundary, a jagged southeastern corner along the Colorado River, and the angled Sierra Nevada mountain range forming the western, slanted edge of the "blade".
The state's unique geometry was pieced together over time rather than drawn all at once:
The Original Block: The initial borders established in 1864 were mostly a rectangular polygon formed by the 37th parallel and 116th meridian.
The Eastern Expansion: In 1866, Congress moved Nevada's eastern border from the 116th meridian to the 114th, transferring a strip of land from the Utah Territory.
The Southern Triangle: In 1867, Congress gave Nevada the "panhandle" south of the 37th parallel (what is now Clark County, home to Las Vegas) which was taken from the Arizona Territory to grant Nevada control over a crucial stretch of the Colorado River.

History of Nevada
Nevada became the 36th state on October 31, 1864, after telegraphing the Constitution of Nevada to the Congress days before the November 8 presidential election (the largest and costliest transmission ever by telegraph). Statehood was rushed to help ensure three electoral votes for Abraham Lincoln's reelection and add to the Republican congressional majorities. Nevada became the second of two states added to the Union during the Civil War (the first being West Virginia) and became known as the “Battle Born State” as a result of when it achieved statehood.

Book Club Trends that Make Reading More Social

The best **book club trends** have less to do with matching tote bags and more to do with giving readers a good reason to gather. A monthly discussion is no longer expected to look like a classroom circle with one serious novel, one set of questions, and a guilty member who did not finish chapter three. Readers are building clubs around the pleasures that brought them to books in the first place: mystery, friendship, pets, snacks, local history, and the delicious possibility of being surprised.

For cozy mystery fans, that shift feels especially welcoming. A good whodunit already gives a group something to puzzle over together. Add a charming town, a determined amateur sleuth, and perhaps a dog with excellent instincts, and conversation has a way of finding its own trail.

## Book Club Trends Are Becoming More Flexible

One of the strongest changes is simple: book clubs are loosening up. The old rule that every member must finish every page before discussion is fading, and that is a kindness. Busy readers are juggling work, caregiving, appointments, school, and the ordinary surprises of life. A club that allows people to attend, listen, and join the conversation without a book-report confession is more likely to last.

Some groups now use a "read what you can" approach. Members may discuss the opening chapters, favorite characters, or the question that made them want to keep reading. Spoiler-free check-ins at the beginning let unfinished readers participate before the group moves on to the big reveal. For mysteries, this is particularly useful. Nobody wants to learn who hid the key clue in the garden shed before they have met the suspect with the suspiciously polished boots.

Flexible scheduling is part of the picture, too. Instead of a firm monthly meeting, some clubs meet every six weeks or choose books by season. Summer may call for a beachy small-town mystery. October invites spooky-but-not-too-spooky reads. December can bring short novels, novellas, or a cheerful holiday theme when calendars are crowded.

This does not mean structure has disappeared. A dependable host, a clear meeting date, and a shared choice still matter. The difference is that the structure serves the readers, rather than making reading feel like homework.

## Genre-First Clubs Are Finding Their People

General-interest clubs remain popular, but genre-first groups are thriving because they begin with shared enthusiasm. Readers who love cozy mysteries do not need to explain why a clever clue, an eccentric neighbor, or a well-timed cup of coffee can be deeply satisfying. Romance readers, fantasy readers, historical fiction fans, and animal-story devotees are finding the same comfort in groups that speak their literary language.

A genre focus also makes book selection easier. Rather than trying to choose one title that pleases every possible taste, a cozy mystery club can rotate among village mysteries, culinary capers, pet-centered sleuths, historical cozies, and newer stories with modern investigative touches. That variety keeps the shelf fresh while preserving the feeling that everyone came for the same kind of fun.

Small themes give these clubs an extra spark. A group might choose mysteries featuring librarians for one month, gardeners for another, or books set in Florida towns during the winter. A canine-themed meeting could pair a dog-narrated tale with a conversation about how animals notice details humans miss. The Doc and Daisy Mysteries fit naturally into this kind of gathering, where canine forensics and a warm snout can inspire both laughter and serious suspect analysis.

The trade-off is that a tightly focused club can become less inviting to a friend who reads outside the genre. The easy answer is an occasional wild-card pick. One out-of-category book every few months can welcome new voices without losing the club's identity.

## The Gathering Matters as Much as the Book

Readers are turning book clubs into small, low-pressure events. A meeting at a library or bookstore still has its charms, but so does a living room, a community room, a neighborhood café, or a picnic table at the park. The setting need not be fancy. It only needs enough chairs, a little time, and a feeling that people are welcome.

Food and simple activities are showing up more often, not because a book discussion needs decorations, but because they make the evening feel memorable. A mystery club might serve "suspect snacks" with playful name cards, bring a favorite tea mentioned in the book, or ask members to vote on the best fictional alibi. For animal-loving readers, a donation collection for a local shelter can connect a pleasant evening of reading with a little practical kindness.

There is a sweet spot here. When every meeting requires elaborate planning, the host can burn out faster than a candle in a drafty old mansion. A bowl of popcorn and one good question can be plenty. The book is the invitation; the shared conversation is the treat.

## Online and Hybrid Clubs Expand the Circle

Online book clubs have settled into a useful role. They are not a substitute for every in-person laugh or the pleasure of passing a plate of cookies across the table, but they make reading communities possible for people who live far apart, cannot travel at night, or simply prefer joining from a favorite chair with a sleeping cat nearby.

Hybrid clubs are especially practical. A few people can meet in person while others join by video, and a group chat can keep the discussion going between meetings. For readers of series fiction, that ongoing conversation is valuable. Someone may finish book one and immediately need to ask whether a beloved side character gets more page time later. Another reader may want a gentle nudge toward the next title without seeing a single spoiler.

The challenge is keeping digital conversation friendly and readable. A host can help by setting simple expectations: label spoilers, avoid sending thirty messages in a row during a workday, and remember that silence in a chat does not mean someone is not enjoying the club. Not every reader wants to type a paragraph about symbolism at 10:47 p.m.

## Readers Want More Voice, Less Assignment

Another of the most encouraging book club trends is the move away from canned discussion questions. Readers still appreciate a thoughtful prompt, especially when a conversation gets quiet, but they respond warmly to questions that invite opinions rather than test recall.

For a mystery, try asking who earned the group's trust too easily, which clue felt fair, or whether the setting was almost a character of its own. For an animal-centered story, ask what the pet understood that the humans overlooked. These questions leave room for different answers, and they give members permission to be playful. A lively disagreement over the most suspicious neighbor can reveal more about a book than a list of plot facts ever could.

Many clubs are also welcoming personal connections to the reading experience. A historical detail may remind someone of a family story. A rescue dog in a novel may lead to a happy tale about a member's own pet. The goal is not to pull attention away from the author. It is to recognize that books become part of us because they brush against real memories, worries, and hopes.

## Shorter Commitments Are a Smart Choice, Not a Lesser One

Long books can be wonderful, but a club does not prove its seriousness by choosing the heaviest hardcover in the room. Novellas, short story collections, backlist titles, and series installments are increasingly popular choices. They are friendlier to new members and give a group more chances to try different authors over a year.

Series books deserve a little planning. Starting in the middle of a mystery series can work if each story stands alone, but some readers enjoy watching relationships and town history develop from the beginning. A host can simply say whether the selection is a welcoming entry point or whether earlier books add useful context. Clear expectations prevent the sort of confusion that belongs in the fictional crime scene, not at the meeting.

A shorter selection also leaves room for a second layer of fun: a related short story, a local-history note, or a conversation about what everyone is reading next. The evening can feel full without asking members to race through four hundred pages.

## How to Keep a Book Club Warm and Worth Returning To

The clubs that endure usually have one thing in common: people feel seen there. That does not require a perfect attendance record or a dazzling host. It means remembering a new member's name, making room for the quiet reader, and letting laughter have a place beside literary discussion.

If you are starting or refreshing a club, choose the first book with care, but do not treat the choice as a grand declaration for all time. Pick a story with a clear premise, an inviting voice, and enough to talk about. Ask members what kind of reading life they want together. Maybe they want clever mysteries and coffee. Maybe they want big feelings, rescue pets, and a cheerful argument about the final chapter.

The loveliest trend is not a format at all. It is the return to reading as a shared pleasure. Put a few chairs in a circle, bring the book that makes you eager to talk, and leave room for one more reader at the table.
A good author event should feel less like a sales pitch and more like an invitation into a story world. When readers take time out of a busy week to meet an author, they want a little conversation, a little fun, and perhaps a reason to keep thinking about the characters on the drive home. Learning **how to plan author events** with that feeling in mind can turn a simple signing into a warm gathering that readers remember.

For mystery readers especially, an event can carry the same pleasure as opening a new cozy: a welcoming setting, a few intriguing details, and people who are glad they came. The practical details matter, of course, but the best events leave room for personality.

## Start With the One Thing You Want the Event to Do

Before calling a bookstore or posting a date, decide what success looks like for this particular event. You may want to introduce a new release, meet local readers, encourage book-club discussion, celebrate a library program, or simply give longtime supporters a chance to say hello. Those goals overlap, but they call for different choices.

A launch event benefits from a clear focus on the new book and an easy way for guests to get a signed copy. A library talk may work better as a lively presentation on the research behind your stories, your writing life, or the animals that inspire your characters. At a book festival, your goal may be visibility and a memorable first impression rather than a long program.

Choose one primary goal and let it guide the rest. If the purpose is to build local relationships, a smaller independent bookstore or library may be a better fit than a large venue where guests drift in and out. If the goal is a release-day celebration, a larger room and a little extra publicity may make sense.

## How to Plan Author Events Around Your Readers

Think about who is most likely to attend, not just who you hope will attend. Cozy mystery fans often enjoy an afternoon event with time for questions and conversation. Dog and cat lovers may be delighted by a pet-friendly angle, provided the venue permits it and the plan stays comfortable for animals and people alike. Families may need an earlier time, shorter program, and clear expectations about whether children are welcome.

For the Doc and Daisy Mysteries, a Florida small-town setting, a little canine forensics, or a discussion of veterinary experience can give an event its own playful hook. The point is not to pile on activities. It is to offer one detail that feels true to the books and gives readers something to talk about besides, “I got my copy signed.”

Ask your host what their regular customers enjoy. Bookstore staff and librarians know their communities well. They may suggest a weekday evening, a Saturday morning, a book-club partnership, or a joint event with another local author. Their advice is often more useful than a generic rule about the “best” event time.

### Pick a venue that matches the mood

A cozy event needs a place where people can hear, sit comfortably, and browse books without confusion. Independent bookstores, public libraries, community centers, senior living communities, schools, and local literary festivals can all work beautifully. Each comes with trade-offs.

Bookstores are natural places to sell books, but they may have limited seating and a busy calendar. Libraries often draw engaged readers and offer welcoming meeting rooms, though book sales may require advance coordination. Community spaces can feel personal and flexible, but the author may need to handle more setup, payment options, and publicity.

Visit the venue if possible. Notice the lighting, parking, restroom access, sound level, and where a signing line could form without blocking the door. If readers have to stand in a noisy corner for an hour, even the cleverest mystery anecdote will have trouble holding their attention.

## Create a Program With a Little Shape

An author event does not need to be long to be satisfying. In fact, forty-five to sixty minutes is often plenty, followed by signing and informal conversation. A simple structure keeps the gathering moving while leaving room for the unexpected question or funny reader story.

A dependable program usually includes a welcome from the host, a brief introduction, a short reading or story behind the book, a conversation about the writing or research, audience questions, and signing time. The reading should be brief enough to create curiosity rather than answer every question. Choose a passage with character, setting, humor, or a small moment of suspense - not one that needs three pages of explanation first.

Practice the opening out loud. You do not need to sound rehearsed, but you do want to avoid spending the first five minutes searching for your notes. Have two or three stories ready: why you wrote the book, a surprising piece of research, a memorable animal encounter, or a behind-the-scenes detail about the setting. Personal stories are often the moments readers carry with them.

### Make questions easy to ask

Some audiences will have questions ready before you finish speaking. Others need a gentle nudge. Offer a few starting points: readers can ask about character names, research, the next book, writing routines, or the real-life inspiration behind a fictional town. If the room is quiet, ask the host to prepare one or two opening questions.

Keep answers warm and concise. A question from one reader may be exactly what another person was hoping to ask. If someone wants a long, personal conversation, invite them to continue during signing time so the rest of the room stays included.

## Handle the Details Before They Become Drama

The quiet work behind an event is what allows the fun parts to shine. Confirm responsibilities in writing with the venue well ahead of time. Who orders books? Who processes sales? Is there a table, chair, microphone, water, and signage? Will someone introduce you? Is there a rain plan if any portion is outdoors?

Use a simple event sheet with the date, arrival time, address, contact person, parking directions, program start time, book titles available, and equipment needed. Bring pens that will not smear on glossy pages, a backup marker, a small tabletop sign, and a phone charger. If you accept payment yourself, test your method before the event begins.

For a larger event, these four tasks deserve a specific person and deadline:

- Confirm the book inventory and where readers will purchase copies.
- Prepare the venue’s promotional information, including a short author bio and book descriptions.
- Set the room so late arrivals can enter quietly and everyone can see the speaker.
- Decide how the signing line will work, especially if guests bring older books from home.

Do not assume a full room means a long signing line. Some readers will attend because they already own the book, borrowed it from the library, or simply enjoy hearing authors speak. Welcome them all. A reader who does not buy that day may recommend the series to a friend, request it at a library, or return for the next release.

## Promote With an Invitation, Not a Megaphone

Readers respond to specifics. “Author signing Saturday” is useful, but “Meet the author behind a small-town mystery narrated by a very observant dog” gives people a reason to look twice. Share the date, time, place, what guests can expect, and whether books will be available for purchase.

Begin promotion early enough for the venue to include the event in its calendar, then remind people as the date approaches. A first announcement a few weeks ahead, a reminder the week of the event, and a cheerful day-before post are often enough for a local gathering. Too many identical posts can make even enthusiastic followers tune out.

Ask the host what they will promote and what they need from you. A clear headshot, short bio, book cover image, and ready-to-use event description make it easier for them to share the event well. Mention local touches when they are genuine: a nearby setting, a hometown connection, a library partnership, or a seasonal theme.

## Be Present After the Program Ends

The signing table is not merely a checkout station. It is where a reader may tell you that a character made them laugh, that their dog resembles Daisy, or that they passed a book to their sister. Listen. Ask how they found the series. If there is a line, keep the conversation brief but attentive, and personalize each inscription when possible.

Afterward, thank the host and any staff or volunteers who helped. Make a few notes while the event is fresh: which questions came up, what readers seemed most excited about, whether the timing worked, and what you would change next time. Those small observations are better than relying on memory months later.

A well-planned author event does not have to be fancy. It just needs to make people feel they have stepped into a friendly room where stories matter, questions are welcome, and there may be one more clue waiting around the corner.

text:
*_ Ashwayuja Bahula Trayodashi - Yama Deepam, Commencement of Yama Panchaka 𝕝𝕝卐𝕝𝕝_*
*≈≈≈❀┉┅━🪔 🕉️ 🪔┉┅━❀≈≈≈*

*_Yama Deepam_*
*━꧁ 🪔 ꧂━*

*_Ashwayuja Bahula Trayodashi (the lunar day preceding Naraka Chaturdashi) is also known as "Dhana Trayodashi." On this night, to ward off untimely death (apamrityu), one should light a lamp using sesame oil, offer worship, and place it in front of the house. This is called "Yama Deepam." It is lit to seek the grace of Yama (the Lord of Death). Ritual offerings (tarpanam) are made to Yama, and a lamp is ceremonially gifted (deepa daanam)._*

Long ago, there lived a king named Hima. He had an only son, whom he raised with great affection. As a Kshatriya, the prince was trained in martial arts, including swordsmanship. However, astrologers predicted that, according to his horoscope, the prince would die on the fourth day after his wedding.

Despite this, a princess fell in love with him and married him. She vowed to protect her own marital status (symbolized by *pasupu-kumkuma*—turmeric and vermilion). On the fourth day, she piled up heaps of jewelry in front of the prince’s chamber, lit brilliant, radiant lamps, and adorned the ground with colorful *rangolis* (patterns made with colored powders). She sings melodious songs in praise of her beloved deity, Goddess Lakshmi.

Yamadharma Raja (the Lord of Death) arrives in the form of a serpent to claim the prince’s life. The light from a lamp falls upon the golden ornaments, causing the entire chamber to glow brilliantly. Dazzled by this radiance, the serpent’s vision dims, and it finds itself unable to move forward. Enchanted by the princess’s music, the serpent forgets its original mission and remains there, listening to her song. Meanwhile, dawn breaks. As the critical, fated time for the soul’s departure passes, the Lord of Death departs empty-handed.

For this reason, a 'Yama Deepam' (a lamp dedicated to Yama) is lit on this day, as it is believed to please him. In North India, it is customary to place a mound of rice outdoors in the evening and light a 'Yama Deepam' upon it.

*_꧁ॐ Om Yamaya Namaha ॐ꧂_*

*_ll Lokah Samastah Sukhino Bhavantu ll_*

text:
Now that Minister Kirk Franklin has released a song with Davido, a Nigerian secular music artist, I have a serious question for the Church: Are we gradually redefining what it means to leave Babylon?

You cannot claim to have left Babylon and still insist on carrying Babylon's cucumbers and fried rice with you into Zion.

There is nothing Babylon has that Zion needs to borrow to establish its identity.

And please, don't tell me this is culture shifting or that the song is reaching people outside the Church.

SHUTTTTT UPPPPP!

Must we look like the world, sound like the world and embrace everything the world offers just to convince the world that Jesus is relevant?

When did reaching the world become an excuse for compromising the distinction between the Church and the world?

We are called to be the light of the world, not to imitate the world to attract an audience.

Jesus never commanded us to become like Babylon to win Babylon. He called us to be a peculiar people, set apart and committed to representing His Kingdom.

The question is not whether the song will reach people outside the Church. The question is: What are we communicating about the Kingdom we claim to represent?

We must be careful not to baptise every cultural compromise and call it evangelism.

You cannot leave Babylon while constantly looking for reasons to carry Babylon into Zion.

text:
TUSLA AND THE FAMILY COURTS: WHY DO THOSE WITH POWER TO CONFRONT INSTITUTIONAL FAILURE FAIL TO DELIVER CHANGE?

In Julius Caesar, Shakespeare’s Cassius tells Brutus:

“The fault, dear Brutus, is not in our stars,
But in ourselves, that we are underlings.”

Power is sustained not only by those who exercise it, but by the inaction of those who could challenge it. The parallel with Ireland’s handling of Tusla and the family courts is striking.

Governments have heard warnings about children in care, parents’ treatment, safeguarding and whistleblowers through judgments, Oireachtas debates, inspections and families’ testimony.

The problems are known. Why do remedies so rarely follow?

WHEN COURT ORDERS DO NOT PRODUCE PROTECTION

High Court cases have exposed children at risk of exploitation and drug-related harm without available special care placements. Judges have criticised failures to implement orders.

A court order is not a suggestion. Staffing shortages may explain difficulties, but explanations are not accountability. Responsibility cannot disappear between Tusla, Government and the courts.

FAMILY COURTS: PRIVACY AND SCRUTINY

Family court decisions shape childhoods. The in-camera rule protects privacy, but must not obstruct scrutiny. Judicial independence matters, as do adequate laws and safeguards.

Judgments have stressed fairness, children’s views and parents’ rights to challenge evidence. But how many families can afford litigation? Inaccessible rights offer limited protection.

WHEN OVERSIGHT REPLACES ACTION

Ireland has plenty of reports, inspections and hearings. Ministers express concern, agencies promise improvement and recommendations follow.

But were recommendations implemented? Were children made safer? Did families obtain remedies? Where misconduct was established, did consequences follow?

A parliamentary hearing is not a remedy. A ministerial assurance is not a safeguard. A recommendation is not reform until it is implemented and shown to work.

THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE IRISH BODY POLITIC

Tusla, ministers, civil servants, parliamentarians, regulators and judges have distinct responsibilities. Those distinctions matter, but must not become excuses for endlessly passing responsibility elsewhere.

When failures occur, who knew, who could act and what was done? This demands institutional responsibility, not political interference in court decisions.

THE HUMAN COST

Behind the language of governance and capacity are traumatised children, separated parents and professionals raising concerns.

An apology cannot restore a year of childhood. Parents unjustly separated from children cannot recover lost years after an error is acknowledged. Accountability means human outcomes, not procedures.

WHISTLEBLOWERS AND SILENCE

Whistleblowers deserve fair examination, not retaliation or exposure. If speaking out risks careers, others may remain silent. When children’s safety is at stake, silence can be devastating.

HAS FAILURE BECOME NORMAL?

A disturbing case emerges. There is outrage. Questions are asked in the Oireachtas. A minister expresses concern. A review is announced. Attention moves on. Then another case emerges.

The danger is that the political system becomes better at managing controversy than resolving its causes. Promises of reform become routine, and the extraordinary becomes normal.

Many professionals are dedicated. Child protection is complex, but that cannot excuse persistent failure. Problems must be investigated, remedied and prevented from recurring.

Shakespeare’s challenge remains: we must examine not only what Tusla and the family courts do, but what those entrusted with overseeing them fail to do.

Have those with the power to confront institutional failure become so accustomed to it that their own inaction is now part of the problem?

Until that question is confronted, the distance between political promises and justice for children and families may remain as wide as ever.

WOH, Episode 11, Summary 6. Continuing the discussion regarding ZZS: upon hearing WKX ask ZCL about his father’s loss of trust in his own brothers, ZZS intervenes—sparing the boy from having to answer immediately—and tells him to eat first, as there is no rush. It is also possible that ZZS simply does not want WKX to so easily obtain an answer that he clearly—in ZZS’s view—desperately seeks. Nevertheless, the boy remains resolute and explains to both men what transpired on the night his family perished. ZZS reflects deeply on the words the boy’s father had imparted to him—that he should trust no one, for no one is worthy of such trust. When ZCL, with the guileless conviction of a child, tells ZZS and WKX that he trusts *them*, ZZS calls him a foolish child and advises him not to be so quick to place his trust in others. Taken aback, ZZS attempts to persuade the boy to exercise greater caution, but the boy stands firm, declaring that he ought to have trusted ZZS from the very beginning. At this moment, ZZS is a man burdened by profound guilt, convinced that he deserves nothing good. His wariness toward trust stems from his own past—he once placed his faith in people and decisions that ultimately led to tragedy. ZZS does not want this naive, wounded boy to blindly entrust him with anything of consequence—be it his life, his secrets, or his future. At the same time, ZZS is deeply moved. The boy places pure, unconditional trust in him—despite his father’s warnings and despite what he himself had said about his own nature. This is something ZZS never expected from anyone. Unaware of the turbulent emotions stirring within ZZS’s soul, the boy speaks candidly about the conflict among the "brothers" of the Five Lakes Alliance. ZZS is even more taken aback when the boy offers to give him a piece of the Glazed Armor that once belonged to his father. ZZS has never had any interest in it, and he is further surprised by the location where the piece had been hidden. ZZS finally understands why the boy had been suffering so much and why he had kept his wound concealed from the very beginning. Nevertheless, he makes it clear to the boy that he has no desire for the Glazed Armor piece. The boy appears bewildered by this, as he had not realized that the very object for which everyone in the *Jianghu* is fighting holds no significance for ZZS. At this point, WKX steps in to explain to everyone the likely reason behind ZZS’s attitude. ZZS remains silent, listening as WKX questions the boy, who reveals that the "brothers" of the Alliance had been at odds for years. ZZS says nothing, suspecting that WKX might inadvertently reveal more about himself while probing into the conflict among the Alliance members. When the boy mentions that his father wrote a letter, it immediately catches ZZS’s attention—prompting a swift reaction from WKX, who asks where the letter is; the boy then points out its hiding place. Upon hearing how the boy had acted, ZZS remarks that while he had initially taken the boy for a simpleton, he hadn't expected him to be so clever. He added that even in the situation they found themselves in back then—at the abandoned temple, while fighting against the ghosts from Ghost Valley—the boy still managed to hide a letter. This is the first clear compliment ZZS pays the boy; he is genuinely impressed by the lad’s cool-headedness and composure, noting that neither he nor WKX had realized the boy had hidden anything at the temple. Although ZZS had noticed at the time that the boy was wounded, he had failed to see that he had concealed an object. The boy also reveals to both men who the letter is addressed to and what he intended to do next. Still unaware that ZZS is analyzing his behavior, WKX asks who the letter is for. ZZS surmises that the more the boy speaks, the more likely it is that WKX might reveal his own underlying motives.

They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull. There they offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.

And they crucified Him.

They also divided His garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take. It was the third hour when they crucified Him. And the charge inscribed against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS. Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.

And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, come down from the cross and save Yourself!”

In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself! Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe!”

And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him.

Mark 15:22-27, 29-32

text:
Therefore if you bring your gift to the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you,
Matthew 5:23

Jesus pictures a worshiper bringing a sacrifice to the altar at the Temple in Jerusalem, the appointed place where Israel offered gifts to God. Sacrifice expressed repentance, thanksgiving, devotion, and dependence on God’s mercy. Yet worship cannot be separated from obedience to God’s commands concerning love, truth, and peace with others. The Lord desires a sincere heart, not religious activity that ignores unresolved wrongdoing.

A fellow member of God’s people may have a legitimate grievance because of harm, offense, dishonesty, or neglect. Jesus places responsibility on the worshiper to pursue reconciliation rather than waiting for the injured person to act first. Love for God must be demonstrated in humble efforts to make peace with those made in His image.

🔥-take: NewLake delivered another quarter of rock-solid operations — 99.7% year-to-date rent collection, a fully debt-free balance sheet with $17.9 million in cash, and continued selective acquisitions — while maintaining its attractive $1.72 annualized dividend, leaving the company exceptionally well-positioned for growth as the cannabis sector matures.

🤖 ANALYSIS:
NewLake Capital Partners (OTCQX: NLCP), an internally managed REIT that provides real estate capital to state-licensed cannabis operators, reported third-quarter results on November 4, 2026, with its earnings call set for November 5 at 11 a.m. ET.

Financial Results  
- **Revenue**: $12.0 million, down 4.5% year-over-year from $12.6 million. Nine-month revenue totaled $36.4 million, down 6.0% from $38.7 million.
- **Net income attributable to common stockholders**: $4.2 million ($0.20 per diluted share), compared with $6.7 million ($0.32) in Q3 2025. Nine-month net income was $15.8 million ($0.77) versus $20.3 million ($0.98).
- **FFO**: $10.0 million ($0.47 per diluted share), versus $10.7 million ($0.51).  
- **AFFO**: $10.3 million ($0.49 per diluted share), versus $11.0 million ($0.52). Nine-month AFFO reached $30.7 million versus $33.2 million.

The modest year-over-year declines reflected the loss of rental income from three properties that became available for lease in 2025, along with related carrying costs. These were partially offset by contractual rent escalations, a full quarter of contributions from two Ohio dispensaries acquired in 2025 (including funded tenant allowances), and initial income from the August Kentucky dispensary acquisition. Management characterized results as in line with expectations.

Balance Sheet and Capital Allocation  
A standout positive was the balance-sheet cleanup: the company repaid the remaining $7.6 million on its revolving credit facility, ending the quarter with **zero debt** and $17.9 million in cash. Gross real estate assets were $433.8 million (including one property classified as held for sale). It also amended its $90 million revolving facility, extending the maturity to May 2029 with updated terms, and remained fully compliant with covenants.

Year-to-date contractual rent collection stood at an exceptional 99.7%. The Board declared a $0.43 per share quarterly dividend (annualized $1.72), equating to an ~88% AFFO payout ratio. In addition, the stock repurchase authorization was extended through December 31, 2028, with approximately $8.2 million still available.

Portfolio and Tenant Activity
NewLake owns 37 properties (15 cultivation facilities and 22 dispensaries), predominantly under long-term triple-net leases.  
- During the quarter it acquired a Kentucky dispensary for ~$0.6 million and committed ~$1.6 million for improvements.  
- Subsequent to quarter-end it acquired dispensaries in Michigan and Kentucky for an aggregate ~$1.3 million and committed ~$1.7 million in improvements, leased to an affiliate of an existing tenant.

On the tenant side, the company continued monitoring Cannabist’s restructuring and entered agreements (pending close) to terminate the lease and commence a new lease at its Aurora, Illinois cultivation facility; it collected all contractual rent on its other three Cannabist properties through September 30. PharmaCann’s Shamokin, Pennsylvania dispensary underwent a change of control to a Cresco Labs affiliate, with the existing lease terms otherwise unchanged and Cresco added as guarantor.

Outlook and Investment Implications
CEO Anthony Coniglio emphasized the strengthened, debt-free balance sheet, available credit capacity, and disciplined focus on property-level cash flow, stating that NewLake is well positioned to pursue growth opportunities as the cannabis regulatory landscape matures.

Trading near $13.89 (market cap ~$288 million), the shares offer a low-teens P/FFO multiple and a ~12.5% dividend yield. The combination of zero leverage, near-perfect collections, an attractive and well-covered dividend, and ongoing (if selective) acquisition activity supports a constructive view for income-oriented investors seeking exposure to the cannabis real-estate niche, with further upside potential tied to re-leasing activity and eventual regulatory clarity

text:
Known to some as a local hero and to others as a criminal, Henry Berry Lowry and his armed band, consisting of Lumbees, African Americans and one “buckskin” Scot, fought the Home Guard (the Confederate Army’s during the Civil War and the Ku Klux Klan during Reconstruction. The outlaw robbed from planters and redistributed wealth. He mysteriously disappeared after robbing $28,000 from the sheriff’s office in 1872...

During the Civil War, Confederate armies and the state of North Carolina conscripted Lumbees to build fortifications in Wilmington and elsewhere. Many dodged the conscription agents and hid out in the county. As a result, the Home Guard tracked down dodgers and conflict resulted. The eighteen-year-old Lowry formed a guerrilla band that fought back.

. . .

In 1865, Confederate Home Guards executed the father and brother of Henry Berry Lowry in North Carolina. The young Native American, who belonged to the Lumbee community, responded by taking command of an outlaw band that had been hiding in the swamps. What followed was a seven-year struggle against local authorities that turned him into one of the most wanted men in the state.

Lowry's gang was unusual because it included Native American, Black, and white men working together. They raided plantations, stole supplies, and targeted wealthy landowners and officials. They sometimes shared their stolen goods with poor families, earning Lowry a reputation similar to Robin Hood. Despite repeated attempts to capture him, he escaped from jail and evaded local militias and federal troops. His growing popularity among poor communities only made authorities more determined to catch him.

By 1871, authorities had placed a $10,000 bounty on his capture, an enormous sum at the time. But Lowry remained one step ahead of his pursuers. In February 1872, his gang carried out a robbery that reportedly netted $28,000. Shortly afterward, Lowry mysteriously disappeared. Some believed he had escaped to start a new life, while others thought he had met a tragic end. His true fate remains a mystery more than 150 years later.

Lowry’s activities have become legend. Many consider him a Robin Hood, for he robbed (and killed) the powerful in Robeson County. He was also captured three times and found a way to escape each time—once, filing through jail bars. Legend says he single-handedly routed 18 militiamen in one gunfight near the Lumber River. His last robbery and disappearance contribute greatly to his mystique: In 1872, he mysteriously disappeared after robbing the local sheriff’s office and taking $28,000.

His death is disputed. Some believe he died during or shortly after the heist, but others reported seeing him a few years later sitting quietly at a funeral. In the 1930s, some claimed that he was still alive.

After his 1872 disappearance, the Lowry Band was without its namesake and leader. Their exploits ceased, and in a few years, almost every member of the band had been captured or killed.  

Lowry's wife, Rhoda, reportedly insisted for the rest of her life that her husband had successfully escaped. Despite the enormous reward offered for his capture, nobody ever collected it.

As a realtor, sometimes offers and closings aren’t as clean and easy as you’d expect. Some situations need a little extra…incentive. 

Shortly after graduating college in 2025, I was helping a family purchase a home in the Pittsburgh area for about $650,000. It was at the upper end of their budget but it was their forever home and in a location with great schools. Everything was moving along fine until the inspection. It’s always the inspection!

The roof’s underlayment had some damage and was leaking into the attic. The damage was small but the roof would need to be replaced shortly after closing. The buyers wanted the sellers to fix it. The sellers wouldn’t fix it. Since it was a sellers market at the time, they also wouldn’t adjust the price, basically saying “tough shit.”

I met the husband at the house to take a closer look at the roof from inside the attic and decide how he wanted to proceed. This was going to be my biggest sale yet and I really didn’t want to lose out on a nice payday. We went up into the attic and sure enough you could see the spots with a flashlight. About 4 individual damaged spots in total. And there was moisture in the attic that the sellers were clearly trying to hide with a dehumidifier running full time up there.

text:
The Louisiana Purchase treaty was signed in Paris on 30 April 1803. Under it the United States bought from France about 828,000 square miles west of the Mississippi River for 15 million dollars, roughly four cents an acre. Spain had secretly agreed to return Louisiana to France in the Treaty of San Ildefonso of 1 October 1800. For President Thomas Jefferson, a powerful France in control of New Orleans threatened the trade of American farmers who shipped their goods down the Mississippi.

Jefferson's aims were modest at first. His negotiators, Robert R. Livingston and James Monroe, were authorized to pay up to 10 million dollars for the port of New Orleans and the Floridas alone. Instead, Napoleon Bonaparte, then First Consul of France, offered the entire territory. The Americans quickly accepted. France was represented by François Barbé-Marbois, minister of the public treasury. The price combined 60 million francs paid to France with up to 20 million francs to settle claims that American citizens held against the French government.

The deal raised hard questions. Jefferson generally read the Constitution strictly and doubted that it allowed the federal government to acquire new territory. He set those doubts aside when Napoleon seemed ready to withdraw the offer. The purchase doubled the size of the United States and began a century of expansion. Each new territory also reopened the dispute over whether slavery would spread west, a conflict that shaped American politics until the Civil War. What France sold was its claim to the land. The Native nations who lived there had not agreed to any transfer, and their dispossession followed in the decades after.

❤️🐾 HOPE FOR STEPHANIE & STAR

Two Lives. One Journey. One Hope for a Better Tomorrow.

My name is Stephanie, and this is our story.

Life has taken Star and me down a road I never imagined. Today, we are facing homelessness while struggling with serious medical challenges and the uncertainty of what tomorrow may bring.

🐾 MY FAITHFUL SERVICE DOG, STAR

Star is my medical service dog, my loyal companion, and an essential part of my everyday life.

Through every challenge, Star has remained by my side, providing support, comfort, and companionship.

We are facing this journey together, and I am determined to keep us both safe.

💔 OUR CURRENT SITUATION

Star and I are currently homeless in Arizona, living outside while I struggle with serious medical conditions, including a spinal injury, disabilities, and heart problems.

I receive just $986 per month in Social Security benefits. This is not enough to cover safe housing, food, medical expenses, medications, and Star’s essential needs.

Living without stable shelter has made an already difficult medical situation even more challenging. Emergency shelters are full, leaving us with limited options and an urgent need for assistance.

❤️ WHY THIS CAMPAIGN MATTERS

Hope for Stephanie and Star is about survival, safety, stability, and rebuilding our lives.

We are not asking for luxury. We are asking for a safe place to call home, access to essential necessities, and the opportunity to live with dignity.

Every donation can help us work toward safe housing, medical necessities, food, and Star’s care.

🚨 URGENT: STEPHANIE & STAR NEED YOUR HELP NOW!

We cannot afford to wait. We urgently need a safe place to stay.

Every day without shelter brings more uncertainty and additional challenges to managing my serious medical conditions. With my disabilities and Star’s essential role as my medical service dog, finding safe, stable housing is not simply a matter of comfort—it is a critical need.

I am reaching out because I cannot overcome these circumstances alone.

Please, if you are able to help, take action today.

❤️ DONATE: Your contribution, no matter the amount, can help us move closer to safe housing, food, medical necessities, and Star’s care.

🐾 SHARE: If you cannot donate, please share our campaign with your friends, family, and community. Every share helps our story reach more people who may be willing to support us.

With shelters full and nowhere safe to go, we urgently need financial support to secure stable housing.

We need more than thoughts and prayers right now. We need immediate, meaningful help to get us somewhere safe.

I know times are difficult for many people, and I am deeply grateful to anyone who can offer support.

❤️ OUR HOPE FOR TOMORROW

I am not giving up on finding a better future for Star and me.

We deserve the chance to live somewhere safe, manage my health, and wake up without the constant uncertainty of homelessness.

Please don’t scroll past our story without considering whether you can help. Donate if you can. Share if you can’t. Every act of kindness matters.

Thank you for hearing our story, caring about our situation, and helping us hold on to hope.

With heartfelt gratitude,

Stephanie & Star ❤️🐾

Two lives. One fight for safety. One hope for a better tomorrow.

text:
What if a Chatbot Really Could Be a Friend? | Karen L Fingerman Ph.D. & Ryan Moore Ph.D, Psychology Today

Key points

- Chatbots are not a substitute for human connections, input from people, or our own creativity.

- Variety in our social partners and their functions is linked to better psychological and physical health.

- When used appropriately, chatbots may serve new and meaningful functions in our social lives.

---

My daughter bought me a label maker for my birthday. I had never considered using a label maker. But suddenly, the leftovers in the freezer required a name and a date, the file drawers in my office needed topic indicators, and the boxes with holiday decorations are now clearly marked with what is inside. Who knew that something you never had could be so indispensable?

Chatbots may be the label makers of the social world. We never knew how useful they could be until they arrived. A chatbot, especially when powered by today’s generative artificial intelligence (AI) models, can feel like talking with another person. With names like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, chatbots may play important and unique roles in our social lives.

Caveat

New technologies present exciting opportunities, but also reasons to be cautious or concerned. These new AI tools usher in concerns about job obsolescence, security, and the environment. But when used appropriately, AI tools could enhance our social lives in meaningful ways. Let’s focus on enhancement here, not substitution.

Using Chatbots in the Social World

I’ve mentioned previously that different types of social ties fulfill diverse social needs: belongingness, information, everyday tasks, support, intimacy, and feeling loved and cared for. No single social tie fulfills all needs. We benefit from a mix of romantic partners, children, friends, neighbors, close acquaintances (i.e., fringeships), and even strangers.

Historically, new technologies introduced possibilities for social interaction. For example, since the first part of the 20th century, when the telephone entered everyday life, we commonly talk with people who aren’t present.

Chatbots differ from technologies that facilitate communication between people. Chatbots can perform autonomous social functions when humans aren’t available. They provide individualized, tailored information; a sounding board to strengthen human relationships; a forum to think aloud without managing another human’s reactions; and they can reinforce decisions. Consistent affirmation has several limitations and could harm more than help us, but if the input is weighed for what it is, it can be supportive.

Why wouldn’t we want to add that to our social repertoire?

Available 24/7

In the 1980s, L.L. Bean advertised a 24-hour retail service that you could call toll-free day or night. This was a novel approach, but it was limited to ordering fishing gear or a jacket.

Chatbots are available to discuss anything, anytime, anywhere. You can wake them at 2 a.m. when you are ruminating about a talk you have to give. And they have no expectations of reciprocity. There are hotlines available anytime, too (if you ever feel suicidal, call 988 to speak with a human—not a chatbot). But chatbots will shoot the breeze.

Cognitive Proxy

Other available software keeps a calendar. A chatbot goes a step further by solving problems, generating a schedule, and tailoring an agenda to your needs and priorities. Chatbots determine the information we need, then find it.

Chatbots may also support people with deficits. They can take notes during a class for a student with a learning disability. Someone in early-stage dementia can ask the chatbot the same question repeatedly, without taxing a caregiver.

Chatbots can help with tasks that require detail or repetition. It can tutor a third grader in multiplication tables over and over and never needs to go fix dinner. It can format or update a spreadsheet and quickly pull information from the web. Human effort may be better spent on the complex steps in each project.

Enhancing Our Relationships

Counterintuitively, Chatbots could enhance our human relationships. Communication between people can benefit from input that balances what you want with predictions of another person’s reactions. Chatbots offer:

- An opportunity to vent, write in ALL CAPS, throw a fit. They can help you translate that frustration and anger into a polite request to your colleague.

- Practice for a sensitive conversation ahead of time.

- Interpreting an ambiguous message someone sent and drafting an appropriate response.

- Serving as a confidant. It won’t gossip about your conflicts with your friends.

Personalized Information

In 2000, a search engine called Google spread widely, accessing a universe of information. The website even became a verb. I googled, “the year Google became popular” to land on 2000.

But chatbots can personalize information. With the prompt: “I want a vacation that balances sites, hiking, and great food,” ChatGPT suggested Tucson, Arizona. Over time, the chatbot remembers my preferences.

It has pulled recipes (simple, pescatarian), recommended books, and culled my movie recommendations. No one crafts your personal time the way your chatbot can in minutes.

What Are the Risks of Using Chatbots?

Any particular relationship comes with constraints. You don’t hug your customers. You don’t send memos to your grandma. Chatbots are additions to our social networks, but limitations make them tools rather than social partners.

Chatbot advice can be harmful on important issues, including finance or health. Issues of consequence require human research and input; chatbots have led people severely astray.

Researchers have identified addictive or compulsive engagement, overreliance for cognitive skills, and psychological and emotional dependence on chatbots. Some people have even formed romantic ties to a chatbot. Collectively, these behaviors pose risks for individuals who most need human contact.

Their constant affirmation can be limiting. Chatbots won’t engage in detrimental aggression. But human disagreements provide fodder for complex thinking and problem-solving. Challenges of communicating with people who disagree have been linked to prolonged life. AI chatbots affirm human actions even in cases where those actions are deceptive or illegal, which could cause users to take actions that harm their real-world relationships.

Finally, although nearly all our technology use consumes electricity, the AI powering today’s chatbots poses environmental impacts that we should be mindful of.

Bottom line: Chatbots serve as a beneficial “extra” in a diverse social network. But as with any technology, you must implement it effectively. Dishwashers are great for everyday plates and cups, but don't use them for the cast iron skillet.

Using a chatbot wisely can enhance your social world in new and exciting ways. But stick to what it does best.

text:
A customer texts you a billing question. Two weeks later, you text them a promo.

They never asked for that.

Don't mistake a support exchange or reminder signup for express consent to promotions. CASL permits implied consent in some circumstances, but you need to establish that its conditions apply.

If you want them on your promo list, ask separately. Keep a record of when they said yes, how, and what wording they saw. In Canada, CASL covers commercial texts the same way it covers email.

Then watch two numbers side by side: redemptions and opt-outs. A promo that brings in sales while people unsubscribe is spending your list.

When opt-outs jump, go back to what you promised at signup. Maybe people agreed to reminders and started getting offers. Maybe they expected one message a month and got three in a week.

A text feels more personal than an email, so an unwanted one feels more intrusive too.

AN OPEN LETTER TO AMERICA: 

Somehow life has conspired to leave me essentially all alone in the world today, and I can’t take another step alone. To be clear: I am not asking for your charity.

That’s not the purpose for this open letter. It’s the exact opposite of that. I am offering to you and your family a gift so profound it could help change your lives for the better.

I’m finally ready to test the limits of how much good a “single” person can do armed only with the power of mind, strength of character and the “connection” of modern tech.

All fueled by an unending faith in the goodness of The American People.

It was NOT drugs or alcohol or mental illness that caused my current difficulties.

My path to this place began in the days immediately after 9.11.

When I decided to scrap “the 11-college test” I was conducting to determine if a subscription based behavioral health outreach program could reach college students ahead of crisis points including suicide…

that was when I offered my product FREE to every college in America.

375 colleges joined in. People like free.

After that I couldn’t figure out a business model I could live with, so, in the late fall of 2007, my business failed and in January 2008 I moved home with my parents to begin developing a better business model.

Then my mother began to fail from the ravages of Dementia and as a matter of course, for 11 years I became her caregiver.

Turns out being a caregiver is an extremely isolating job.

My parents passed 12 days apart in the late winter of 2023. By then my ‘new’ business model was complete but the world wasn’t the same as it was back in 2008.

The world had grown really dark and divisive and filled with hate.

So, to do the type of good in the world that I set out to do on the day after 9.11…

I needed to keep working.

And my work demanded total focus and attention to get it right.

That’s why I am all alone in the world today.

To be clear I have a childhood friend who is still precious to me, but he lives a world away. And recently I have a met a couple and we are slowly developing a friendship.

But that’s it. That’s the life that I have intentionally built for myself, because my life’s work became so important to me and to humanity that nothing mattered more.

I have discovered how anyone using modern tech can bring out the best in themselves and unlock their hidden reservoir of talent and goodness at scale.

MAKE NO MISTAKE…

it’s not lost on me that right now I am living a life that no sane person would want to live.

But in my extreme isolation, I have built something that is about to become priceless to you. And…

Priceless to America.

Priceless to your children and grandchildren.

And priceless to every soul on Earth.

1. My new enterprise is the massive framework America requires in this moment, to end our political divisions and reset our democracy and it’s how we begin to transition every person on Earth into Modernity in a way that eventually ends The Affordability Crisis for everyone… with an incredible/collaborative redesign of modern education.

2. My new enterprise is how WE rally The American People to end America’s role of “World Police” so America can finally ascend to her highest self as *The World’s Greatest Dream Feeder*.

3. My new enterprise is how WE stop America’s Mental Health Collapse and emerge as a people much better because of our time in The Dark.

AMERICA… I have built this new enterprise to bring out the best in… YOU.

Today is the day when “my new enterprise” …

must become YOUR new enterprise.

And the way you change the world with your friends list, your followers, your connections, your text chats and your email chains.

“Like and Share”.

AMERICA… if you want to become a part of the solution that America needs most right now, then do a deep dive into this massive new enterprise. 

Make it your own.

And then help make the world a much better place.

By using whatever ‘influence’ you have in the world for maximum good.

Begin by SHARING the priceless ideas that came from the heart and soul of a man who literally self-sacrificed everything so that on this day YOU could begin to help make the world a much better place to live for you and your family.

text:
M&M Q2 FY27 Results and Earnings Call Decode 

M&M delivered 25% revenue growth to ₹57,553 crore and 25% profit growth to ₹4,588 crore. Automotive profit grew 55%, Mahindra Finance 61% and Tech Mahindra 33%, while Farm profit declined 9%.

SUV demand remains strong across Scorpio, Thar, Bolero and newer EV models. Management says capacity, rather than demand, is limiting sales. Monthly SUV capacity is planned to increase to 82,000 by FY27 end, 92,000 in FY28 and 132,000 by FY31. Five major launches are planned by June 2027.

EVs account for around 12% of SUV volumes, with monthly EV capacity increasing from 8,000 to 12,000 by March 2027. Commercial vehicles are also growing, while electric three wheelers offer another expansion opportunity.

Tractors remain the weak spot. Poor monsoons have affected demand, prompting management to reduce FY27 industry growth guidance from 5% to flat. International restructuring and farm machinery expansion should support future profitability.

Commodity inflation remains significant, although price increases, product mix and ₹1,000 crore of PLI incentives helped protect automotive profitability.

Management maintained its mid to high teens SUV growth outlook and longer term commitment to 15% to 20% annual EPS growth with 18% return on equity.

The key opportunity is converting strong demand and new capacity into sustained earnings growth. Tractor recovery, commodity costs and dependence on incentives remain important risks.

Thursday, November 5, 2026
Promise #309 — Romans 8:2 (NKJV)

FREED BY THE SPIRIT. CALLED TO WALK IN VICTORY.

Today’s 365Promises Statement:
“The Spirit of life in Christ has set you free from sin and death.”

Promise #309, based on Romans 8:2.

SCRIPTURE — ROMANS 8:2 (NKJV)

“For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has made me free from the law of sin and death.”

⸻

PANEL 1 — THE ORDER

MISSION: LIVE AS A MAN SET FREE IN CHRIST.

The believer’s freedom is not earned through personal strength, flawless discipline, or religious performance. It comes through Jesus Christ and the life-giving work of the Holy Spirit.

Your past does not command your future. Sin is no longer your rightful master.

BATTLE LINE

I belong to Jesus Christ. His Spirit gives me life. Sin will not command my steps today.

TODAY’S DIRECTIVE

Stand firm in your identity in Christ. Reject condemnation, resist temptation, and respond to others with the freedom and grace you have received.

⸻

PANEL 2 — THE TRAINING

WARRIOR DOCTRINE — FREEDOM IS A GIFT; OBEDIENCE IS ITS FRUIT.

Romans 8:1–4 reveals the foundation of today’s promise.

Paul begins with the declaration that there is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. He then explains why: through Christ, the Spirit brings life where sin brought bondage and death.

THREE TRUTHS ESTABLISH OUR POSITION

1. FREEDOM FROM CONDEMNATION

Our standing before God rests on Christ’s saving work, not our perfect performance.

2. FREEDOM FROM SIN’S DOMINION

The Holy Spirit empowers believers to resist sin rather than remain enslaved to it.

3. FREEDOM TO WALK IN OBEDIENCE

Grace does not eliminate holiness; it makes a new way of life possible.

ARMOR FIT — EPHESIANS 6:10–18

Belt of Truth: God’s Word defines your identity.

Shield of Faith: Refuse accusations that contradict the gospel.

Sword of the Spirit: Answer temptation with Scripture and obedient action.

A warrior does not win spiritual battles through anger, intimidation, or willpower alone. He stands in Christ’s victory and depends on the Spirit.

CROSS-REFERENCES

Romans 6:6–14 — Sin shall not have dominion over you.

Galatians 5:16 — Walk in the Spirit.

John 8:36 — Freedom through the Son.

2 Corinthians 3:17 — Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

⸻

PANEL 3 — THE EXECUTION

PUT FREEDOM INTO ACTION TODAY.

COMMANDER’S ORDERS

1. IDENTIFY

Recognize one attitude, temptation, or old pattern that attempts to regain control.

2. SURRENDER

Bring it before Christ in prayer instead of relying only on self-discipline.

3. EXECUTE

Make one deliberate choice consistent with the Spirit’s leading.

4. SERVE

Encourage someone who is struggling. Offer compassion rather than condemnation.

TODAY’S MISSION

Be a spiritual combat medic in your everyday environment.

Find one person who needs encouragement, patience, forgiveness, or practical assistance.

Remind them through your actions that grace restores rather than merely condemns.

WARRIOR’S PRAYER

Heavenly Father,

Thank You for setting me free through Your Son, Jesus Christ.

Forgive me when I return to old habits, carry guilt You have already addressed, or attempt to fight spiritual battles through my own strength.

Holy Spirit, guide my thoughts, discipline my desires, strengthen my obedience, and make my life a testimony of Your transforming power.

Let me stand firmly in truth, serve my family faithfully, and care for those You place in my path.

Jesus Christ is my Commander. I belong to Him.

In Jesus’ mighty name, Amen.

FINAL COMMAND

Do not return to the chains Christ has broken. Walk in the freedom He has given you.

⸻

CHRIST IS MY COMMANDER

text:
Gaza's Population Grew Last Year and There Wasn't a Famine, Hamas's Own Figures Show, Debunking Claims That Most Gaza Deaths are Women and Children | Adam Kredo, Washington Free Beacon

The most recent mortality figures in Gaza show that the population grew by more than 1 percent last year, faster than in most of the world, and that a major hunger crisis failed to ever materialize. The data—supplied by Hamas's own Ministry of Health—undercut claims by the United Nations and other anti-Israel groups that the Gaza war is a "genocide" that has led to a deadly famine, according to an analysis of the figures.

The Australia/Israel & Jewish Affairs Council, the Australian Jewish community's premier public affairs organization, determined in a recent analysis based on the data that Gaza's population increased by 1.2 percent in 2025, a steep rise for a populace supposedly facing a genocide by Israel. Moreover, the number of nonviolent deaths in Gaza that year, meaning those unrelated to direct conflict, was less than in 2022, a year before Hamas's Oct. 7, 2023, terror spree ignited the war.

The figures "absolutely rule out" the U.N.-affiliated Integrated Food Security Phase Classification's headline-grabbing claim in 2025 that major areas of Gaza were facing a "worst-case scenario of famine." The Washington Free Beacon exclusively reported at the time that the IPC used a less reliable reporting metric before declaring famine, and the newly released figures offer further proof that Gaza was never on the precipice of a humanitarian crisis in which thousands would perish.

"The most notable element of the recent all-cause mortality report for 2025 in Gaza … is the lack of the term 'genocide' anywhere in the report, and the fact that the numbers contained in it seem to completely contradict claims by the United Nations-backed Integrated Food Security Phase Classification in August 2025 that, at that time, major parts of Gaza were experiencing category 5 'famine' conditions," the Jewish Affairs Council concluded.

The Health Ministry figures also dispel another widely disseminated claim by Israel's enemies that women and children accounted for 70 percent of casualties in Gaza, an unverified statistic that has been used to peddle conspiracy theories that Israel intentionally targets civilians. In fact, "as is the norm in warfare, most casualties are military-aged males," the study found.

While the Jewish Affairs Council notes that data from the Hamas-controlled ministry are historically unreliable and often skewed, the organization argues "that claims about genocide, famine and casualty breakdowns that are contradicted by what even Hamas claims about such casualties should immediately be viewed as exposing the individual or organisation making the claim as either extreme or cavalier about accuracy."

The Hamas ministry reported 24,650 total deaths in 2025, of which 18,085—or 73.4 percent—were men. Females accounted for just 6,565 deaths, or 26.6 percent. Around 18,870 people were killed violently, such as in battle, suggesting that 76.6 percent of those killed were likely battlefield combatants. Similarly, the figures show that 17,286, or 70.1 percent, were killed through "direct targeting" by Israel. Just 5,780 were classified as "non-violent" deaths or "indirect deaths," again suggesting that Israel is not wantonly killing the civilian population.

The claim that Israel is prosecuting a genocide in Gaza continues to be peddled by the United Nations, U.N.-affiliated advocacy groups, and anti-Israel political candidates across the country. But there is little factual basis for the accusations, which have become a rallying cry on the left.

More than 75 military professionals recently penned an open letter declaring "the allegations that Israel committed this crime do not meet the established definition and standards of genocide, are unsupported by established facts, nor do they stand up to common sense scrutiny."

"Israel's accusers allege genocide mostly because of the supposed number of civilians killed in Gaza," the letter continues. "Such claims are rife with flaws. Genocide is not a quantitative crime; there is no number of civilian casualties that constitutes genocide. Nor are the claimed casualty numbers from Gaza credible. Issued by Hamas themselves and, at the very least, not distinguishing between civilians and combatants, they cannot be relied upon."

But even Hamas's own figures do not meet the threshold.

"Gaza in 2025 experienced natural population growth of 25,577, 1.2% of the population," according to the report. At least one analyst noted that the numbers show "higher population growth than most countries in the world and more than the world average."

"Populations are not expected to grow rapidly during genocides," the Jewish Affairs Council notes in its study. "Among the acts listed under the Genocide Convention is 'Imposing measures intended to prevent births within the group,' something Israel clearly is not doing."

The much-hyped famine predicted by the United Nations in June and August 2025 is also unsupported by the raw statistics.

In 2022, there were 6,061 deaths in Gaza, a number that was elevated by the COVID pandemic. But the number of deaths in 2025, including those who may have died from starvation or malnutrition, is "clearly not significantly higher than the natural deaths which occurred in 2022. We know this because the numbers for 2019, before COVID, are only slightly lower," according to the study.

By the IPC's own standard, there would need to be several deaths per day to constitute a famine. This would have caused at least 8,600 indirect deaths during the time of the supposed famine. But the Gaza Health Ministry figures record only 5,780 nonviolent deaths across the entirety of Gaza in 2025, a significant shortfall.

"There is no evidence of famine conditions ever existing anywhere in Gaza, as the numbers of non-violent deaths for both children under 5 and the general population are orders of magnitude below the IPC thresholds," the study concluded.

There is also little factual basis to claim that civilian deaths in Gaza were significantly undercounted and much higher than believed, another claim that has been weaponized by Israel's enemies.

Middle East analyst Gabriel Epstein determined at the end of September that there was less than 1 nonviolent death, 0.43, for every direct death through 2025. In line with this finding, military-age males are overrepresented in the mortality figures, as expected in a time of intense war.

"Despite widespread claims that 70% of casualties in Gaza have been women and children, the [Hamas ministry's] own published data has shown significant and growing over-representation of military-age males since early 2024," the study notes. "Claims that women and children account for 70% of injuries are also belied by the [Ministry] data."

Open Letter to Senator Abdul El-Sayed
United States Senator from Michigan

Dear Senator Abdul El-Sayed,

Congratulations on your decisive victory in the midterm elections. I hope you and your team will work to honor the commitments made to voters and help redirect American policy toward sustainable development and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, rather than the long-standing prioritization of arms manufacturers, energy interests, and financial institutions that has too often prolonged conflicts.
Your presence in Washington offers many Egyptians a credible symbol of hope and a clear alternative. I hope part of your efforts can help create the conditions for a safe and orderly transition that ends the military’s dominance over the institutions of the state and returns Egypt to a path of responsible civilian governance centered on the interests of its citizens.
For large segments of Egyptian society, the patterns of rule that followed 1952 became associated with corruption, administrative failure, and the expansion of security apparatuses at the expense of competence and public services. External factors, in this view, also helped prolong structural imbalances whose roots were never addressed. Even where details are debated, the lesson is clear: when crises are managed without genuine reforms in governance and development, security becomes a permanent cost rather than a means of protecting a socially and economically resilient state.
The true measure of any leadership is the condition in which a country is left. Experience has shown that governing through military and intelligence structures has weakened the economy, collapsed the currency, degraded public services, and left ordinary Egyptians struggling daily for the bare minimum of energy, water, and food.
A conditional negotiating stance that protects rights, pursued in balance with sustainable development and effective governance, offers the real integration between security and long-term stability. Genuine security is achieved when a state is strong socially and economically, not when parallel institutions sideline competence and reproduce crisis.
Egypt today needs a safe transition that returns the army to its barracks and allows the election of a genuine civilian government capable of rebuilding the state on the foundations of transparency, competence, and development. In this context, many see you as a credible figure who could contribute to a responsible transitional phase that places the interests of the Egyptian people above all else.

With respect and best wishes for success,
Turki Faisal Al Rasheed
Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

text:
California fined a Malibu couple $4,185,000 over a beach gate they didn’t even build.

Their “crime”? Keeping a gate that protected the public from a 20-foot drop onto a drainage pipe.

The fine was so brutal they had to SELL their home to help pay it.

When Warren and Henny Lent bought the house in 2002, the deck, the stairs and the gate were already there. Five years later, the California Coastal Commission demanded they rip all three out. 

Why? A previous owner had agreed to public beach access back in 1978, and the gate stood in the way.

The Lents even handed the state a KEY so officials could open the gate any time they wanted.

It wasn’t enough.

Then in 2014, the legislature gave the commission the power to fine property owners up to $11,250 PER DAY. Two years later, it used that power to do the unthinkable:

NARRATOR: “They retroactively fined them for all 744 days that had elapsed since the Lents were informed their violation could expose them to financial penalties. The ultimate fine was a staggering and disproportionate $4.185 million.”

After the hearing, the Lents offered to take the gate down the very next day. The state told them to wait a few months. Why? It needed time to get its OWN gate ready. The moment the old gate came down, the state put a new one up.

Pacific Legal Foundation took the fight all the way to the U.S. Supreme Court. The Court wouldn’t even hear the case.

WARREN LENT: “When you sit down and the dust settles, you say, ‘What did Warren and Henny Lent do?’ They bought a house on the beach to fulfill a lifelong dream. That’s all we did.”

Years later, the 2025 Palisades fire burned the home to the ground. The only thing left standing was that damned gate.
