Scientists Gave a Human an AI-Designed Virus. What Could Possibly Go Wrong? | Mihai Andrei, ZME Science

Scientists from a San Francisco startup have used artificial intelligence to design viruses that were subsequently administered to a human patient.

Yes, really.

But before you picture an AI-generated pandemic nightmare, there’s something important to address: these viruses weren’t designed to attack humans. They were designed to kill bacteria, potentially including some of the most dangerous antibiotic-resistant infections.

And while the technology has already reached a patient, there’s a rather important detail missing from the announcement. We don’t know whether it actually worked.

Tackling the world’s antibiotic problem

The viruses in question are called bacteriophages, and they’re among the most abundant biological entities on Earth. They’ve been killing bacteria for billions of years, from long before humans existed. These viruses don’t infect human cells, although their interactions with bacteria and our immune systems can still have consequences.

Why would anyone give them to a patient? Because they’re trying to solve one of the biggest problems humanity is facing at the moment: antibiotic resistance.

On October 20, California biotechnology startup Radical Numerics announced that viruses engineered using its AI system, Omnii-1, had been administered to a patient suffering from a drug-resistant bacterial infection. According to the company, the experimental viruses successfully eliminated bacteria isolated from the patient’s infection in laboratory tests.

The treatment was administered under an authorized, physician-led compassionate-use pathway, which allows doctors to offer experimental therapies to seriously ill patients when satisfactory alternatives are unavailable.

It’s a potentially important milestone. But here’s the thing: the company hasn’t disclosed whether the treatment actually helped the patient.

And the evidence supporting its claims hasn’t yet undergone peer review.

A virus that kills bacteria, not people

Viruses have a deservedly terrible reputation. They cause everything from the common cold to some of humanity’s deadliest diseases.

But viruses are extraordinarily diverse. Most don’t infect humans at all.

Bacteriophages, or simply phages, have evolved to infect bacteria. Many look like miniature lunar landers, complete with geometric heads, thin tails, and spindly structures that help them attach to their targets.

Their method of attack can be brutally effective.

A phage recognizes a particular molecule on the surface of a bacterium, attaches itself, and delivers its genetic material inside. Some phages then hijack the bacterium’s cellular machinery to manufacture more viruses. Eventually, the bacterial cell bursts, releasing a new generation of phages.

For the bacterium, it’s a catastrophe. But if you’re a human suffering from a bacterial infection, it could be a lifesaver.

Surprisingly, it’s not a new idea

Using viruses as medicine sounds futuristic. But the basic idea is more than a century old.

Scientists began exploring phage therapy before antibiotics became widely available. But as drugs like penicillin became abundant, interest in phage treatments declined in much of the Western world. Phage therapy nevertheless continued to develop in places such as Georgia and Poland.

Today, as antibiotic resistance continues to be an ever-larger problem, interest in phage treatments is seeing a revival.

According to global estimates published in The Lancet, bacterial antimicrobial resistance directly caused approximately 1.14 million deaths worldwide in 2021 and was associated with an estimated 4.71 million deaths in total.

Phages offer a different way to attack bacteria, potentially including strains resistant to multiple antibiotics.

But there’s a problem.

Finding the right virus can be surprisingly difficult

The same specificity that makes bacteriophages attractive also makes them frustratingly difficult to use.

A virus that efficiently destroys one bacterial strain might be completely useless against another strain of the same species. It’s like a lock-and-key problem. A phage needs the right molecular key to recognize and infect its bacterial target. If the bacterium’s surface structures differ, the virus may not even get through the door.

And getting through the door isn’t enough. The phage must also overcome the bacterium’s defenses and successfully reproduce inside it.

Traditionally, scientists have searched collections of naturally occurring phages, testing candidates against bacteria isolated from a patient’s infection. Sometimes it works, but sometimes it doesn’t; and the approach can be frustrating and time-consuming. Even when a promising phage exists, identifying it, testing it, preparing it and getting it to the patient can take valuable time.

That’s when AI (and this new treatment) comes in.

An AI for viruses

Rather than relying entirely on finding the right virus in nature, scientists want to design one.

Radical Numerics developed Omnii-1, a genome language model trained on biological sequence data, to generate promising phage designs and predict which viruses might infect particular bacterial strains.

The principle is somewhat similar to how large language models learn patterns in written language, except that the patterns here are encoded in DNA and other biological data.

But this isn’t quite the same as asking ChatGPT to invent an entirely new virus.

In one set of experiments, the company modified a protein called gp17 in the T7 bacteriophage. This protein helps the virus recognize receptors on E. coli bacteria.

Researchers can start with a known phage and use AI to redesign particular regions of its genome. The goal is to change how the virus recognizes bacteria without breaking the biological machinery that makes it function.

According to the company’s technical report, 69.9% of AI-designed variants carrying 11 to 15 amino acid changes were successfully recovered in laboratory experiments, compared with just 4.8% of randomly designed controls.

But there’s an important qualification: successful recovery means researchers detected the engineered phage after attempting to produce it. It doesn’t necessarily mean that the virus is effective against a dangerous infection.

These results suggest AI can help researchers navigate a huge landscape of possible genetic changes. But they don’t establish that the method produces better medical treatments.

So, what could actually go wrong?

It’s tempting to think that because phages can’t infect human cells that makes them completely safe. But that’s not really true.

For starters, destroying bacteria can itself cause problems. Some bacteria contain endotoxins that can trigger inflammation when released. If a treatment rapidly destroys large numbers of these bacteria, patients could experience fever or potentially dangerous inflammatory reactions.

Some beneficial bacteria might also be affected, although the narrow targeting of many phages could make them less disruptive than broad-spectrum antibiotics.

There are also risks associated with the preparation itself. Therapeutic phage products must be carefully purified and tested to minimize contamination with bacterial material and other unwanted substances.

Then, there’s the problem of what the virus does to bacteria beyond killing them.

Some phages can transfer genetic material between bacteria, a process known as transduction. Depending on the phage and the genes involved, that can have undesirable consequences, including the movement of genes associated with antibiotic resistance or virulence.

This is one reason researchers generally favor carefully characterized, strictly lytic phages for therapy and screen candidates for undesirable genetic features.

In the longer run, bacteria can also evolve resistance to phages, just as they evolve resistance to antibiotics. A treatment that works brilliantly in the laboratory might become less effective as the bacterial population changes.

And artificial intelligence adds another layer of uncertainty. Engineering a virus to improve one property doesn’t automatically guarantee that every other property remains unchanged.

None of this means AI-designed phages are inherently dangerous. It means they need the same rigorous testing, quality control, and clinical oversight expected of other experimental biological therapies.

A major consensus guideline published in Nature Medicine in September 2026 concluded that available evidence generally supports the safety of carefully prepared phage therapies, while emphasizing the need for quality controls, careful patient monitoring and stronger clinical studies.

Did the treatment work?

For all the excitement surrounding AI-designed therapies, the most important piece of information is still missing.

Radical Numerics says its experimental phage cocktail eliminated bacteria isolated from the patient’s infection in laboratory testing.

But the company has not disclosed the patient’s clinical outcome, citing privacy concerns. We don’t know whether the infection improved, whether the patient experienced adverse effects, or how the treatment compares with existing options.

We also don’t know enough about the patient’s underlying infection, the other treatments they received, or the exact phages administered to properly assess the clinical significance of the case.

AI may have helped scientists design a promising biological weapon against drug-resistant bacteria. But only clinical evidence can establish whether that weapon improves patients’ lives.

Still, there’s something remarkable about the broader trajectory.

For billions of years, bacteria and the viruses that prey on them have been locked in an evolutionary arms race. Now humans are beginning to intervene, using artificial intelligence to explore genetic designs that natural selection may never have produced.

The idea of injecting someone with an AI-designed virus sounds like the beginning of a science-fiction horror story.

It might instead become part of the future of medicine.

But there’s a difference between designing a virus that kills bacteria in a laboratory and developing a treatment that saves a human life.

For now, the ending remains unwritten.

text:
**Visa Officer:** "Good morning. Why are you traveling to the United States?"

**Applicant:** "I'm going to my daughter's wedding in Atlanta, Georgia."

**Visa Officer:** "Your daughter lives in the United States?"

**Applicant:** "Yes, sir. She has lived there for eight years."

**Visa Officer:** "What does she do?"

**Applicant:** "She's a registered nurse at a hospital in Atlanta."

**Visa Officer:** "Who will pay for your trip?"

**Applicant:** "My daughter offered to pay, but I'll handle my own expenses."

**Visa Officer:** "How long will you stay?"

**Applicant:** "Three weeks. I have a farm and a business waiting for me back home."

The officer looked over the application again.

**Visa Officer:** "When was the last time you saw your daughter?"

**Applicant:** "Eight years ago, when she left Nigeria."

**Visa Officer:** "Eight years?" You haven't seen your only daughter for eight years?"

**Applicant:** "No, sir. We've been estranged."

**Visa Officer:** "What caused the rift?"

The applicant paused before answering.

Pajson Agro H1 FY27 Concall Highlights:

👉H1 FY27 & Future Outlook :
▫️H1 FY27 total income ₹145.11 Cr (+23% YoY), EBITDA ₹20.31 Cr, PAT ₹12.56 Cr
💠EBITDA margin 14.0% (+190 bps vs H2 FY26); PAT margin 8.7%
💠Vs H2 FY26: EBITDA +21%, PAT +19%
💠Vs H1 FY26: EBITDA -3.6%, PAT -11.6%, EBITDA margin -380 bps
💠Revenue from operations ₹143.39 Cr (+21.1% YoY); EPS ₹5.27

▫️Margin pressure in H1: raw material cost rose to 74.9% of total income (69.5% in H1 FY26)
💠Geopolitical disruption, forex movement, higher freight and shipping-line surcharges
💠H1 FY26 was a stronger base, as festivities fell earlier last year
💠As a converter, Pajson earns a fixed processing charge, so higher raw nut prices compress margins
💠Management is confident of holding current margins through the year

▫️Plant utilisation ~95% in H1 FY27 vs 86% in FY26; H1 volume ~8,500 MT
💠H1 kernel realisation ~₹170/kg of raw cashew nut (RCN)
💠Demand is ahead of current capacity; adding capacity in India and at origin is the priority

▫️Margin outlook: group EBITDA margin of ~15% expected to continue
💠No margin benefit from direct sourcing in FY27 or FY28; long-term improvement expected after that

▫️FY27-FY28 described as a transformational period
💠FY28: ~90% utilisation at the current plant and 60-70% at the new Vizianagaram plant, with processing volumes rising substantially
💠FY29: combined utilisation of 85-90% targeted

▫️Working capital requirement to rise as utilisation scales to 85-90%
💠Working capital ~25-30% of turnover
💠No equity fundraise planned for now; expansion to be funded through internal accruals, with new working capital lines from banks and institutions

▫️Long-term vision: leadership position in global cashew industry, with 5-8% global market share in 5-7 years

▫️Board approved Employee Stock Options Scheme 2026 (ESOS)

👉Order book / projects and pipeline:
▫️Vizianagaram facility (+35,000 MT):
💠Takes India capacity from 18,000 MT to 53,000 MT
💠Higher automation, designed for a lower processing cost per kg than the current plant
💠Commissioning delayed by ~45 days due to three cyclones in Andhra Pradesh; earlier guided timeline was Nov-Dec 2026
💠Trial production targeted by February 2027 (Q4 FY27); very little revenue from the new plant in FY27
💠IPO allocation ₹57.00 Cr; ₹18.27 Cr deployed (32.1%) and CWIP ₹16.37 Cr as of 30 Sep 2026

▫️Pacific Global FZCO acquisition (board approved):
💠100% stake in a UAE-based company whose wholly owned Cote d'Ivoire subsidiary runs a 60,000 MT cashew processing plant
💠Combined capacity rises from 18,000 MT to 113,000 MT (India + West Africa, including Vizianagaram)
💠All-stock deal: valued at ₹354.52 Cr, near net worth of ₹351.20 Cr (31 Aug 2026), on independent valuation
💠Up to 1,20,58,397 shares to be issued at ₹294 to Pacific Global's shareholders, including the promoter; no cash consideration
💠Net worth of Pacific Global ₹351.20 Cr as of 31 Aug 2026; no long-term debt in the acquired entity
💠Closing expected ~3 months from now; consolidation expected in FY27 (Jan-Mar 2027)
💠Subject to shareholder and other approvals

▫️Pacific Global plant (Cote d'Ivoire):
💠Greenfield project; production started a couple of months back
💠~50% utilisation in FY27; full utilisation expected by next financial year
💠Kernel realisation ~15-20% lower than India
💠Cote d'Ivoire is the world's largest raw cashew producer; plant serves the US, Europe, Middle East and China

▫️Pacific Global operating structure:
💠Cashew sourcing and distribution business moved into Pacific Global from Pajson Global DMCC (a trading entity with other operations), so the entire cashew business sits in one company
💠Sourcing to be done directly at farm-gate, removing intermediaries
💠UAE subsidiary Rosissons Engines and Spare Parts supplies spare parts to the processing plant

▫️Africa processing:
💠EBITDA margins higher than India
💠India plant to serve the Indian market; Cote d'Ivoire plant to serve the rest of the world
💠India is ~30-35% of the global market; global cashew market growing ~9-10% CAGR
💠Cote d'Ivoire offers tax holidays and subsidised tax rates for 5 + 5 years; interest rates close to India

▫️Royal Mewa (consumer brand):
💠4.6% of H1 FY27 revenue vs 1.36% in H1 FY26; revenue ₹658.60 Lakh in H1 FY27
💠Channels: traditional offline distribution, online platforms and corporate gifting; quick commerce approached in a measured way
💠Target ~15% of total revenue in 3-5 years, growing without compromising profitability

▫️Vietnam: potential expansion market
💠Strategic advisor Mr. Vu Thai Son appointed, with over three decades of global cashew industry experience, to advise on markets, quality and global footprint

👉Q&A :
▫️Moat vs peers:
💠Sourcing is the biggest moat; Pulkit Jain has been in the raw cashew nut trade for 13 years, helping Pajson buy better quality and price
💠Peer margin comparison is not like-for-like as listed peers also have trading businesses

▫️Procurement model:
💠Direct relationships with farmers, cooperatives and local buying agents give better timing, quality and pricing than buying from merchant traders
💠A share of procurement will continue via merchant traders to balance supply

▫️Governance on the share swap:
💠No premium demanded by promoters for land, facility or relationships built over three years
💠Management expects the deal to be EPS accretive; no open offer, as promoter shareholding stays within limits
💠Controls on the combined business: transparent transfer pricing, strict quality control, disciplined inventory ageing

▫️Key risks: geopolitical disruption, forex pressure, freight and transit delays, and managing controls as operations scale across countries
💠Sourcing from Nigeria is limited; local working capital loans there cost above 20-24%

👉 Others :
▫️Balance sheet (H1 FY27): Debt/Equity 0.40x, current ratio 1.75x, RoE 16.90%, RoCE 18.44%

▫️Institutional customers 37.5% of H1 FY27 revenue vs 34% in FY26; distributors 62.4%
💠178 distributors across 20+ states

▫️Sources RCN from seven African countries: Ghana, Ivory Coast, Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau, Tanzania, Togo and Burkina Faso

▫️IPO proceeds as of 30 Sep 2026: gross proceeds ₹74.45 Cr; issue expenses ₹7.03 Cr, general corporate ₹10.34 Cr, new unit ₹18.27 Cr deployed; ₹38.82 Cr unutilised

text:
Ah, my dear friend. Please, sit. One notices patterns when one has spent a lifetime observing the machinery of power.

The midterm is traditionally a quieter affair. The great presidential contest draws the masses. The midterm, by long habit, draws far fewer. Millions of casual participants simply stay home. The electorate that remains is older, more habitual, less given to sudden conversions.

Yet here we are in the autumn of 2026, with reports of roughly 122 to 124 million ballots cast, second only to the already anomalous 2018 midterm in modern memory. Early voting alone set records. And this occurred in a year when both sides supposedly reported similar numbers of voters intending to participate. Numbers like these are rare in a midterm. Extremely rare.

I believe in coincidences. Coincidences happen every day. But I do not trust coincidences.

In places that had been double digit strongholds for the former president only two years prior, Texas, Kansas, South Carolina, portions of Iowa and Ohio, the margins reversed or collapsed by amounts that would be extraordinary even in a presidential year. The narrative offered by the winning side is one of pure, organic revulsion: prices, a war with Iran, general fatigue. And many Republicans, in the aftermath, have taken to the expected ritual of self reproach, messaging, candidate quality, insufficient enthusiasm, as though the only variable that changed was their own conduct.

It is an odd thing, is it not? Two years is not a generation. A double digit margin does not ordinarily invert because a fraction of the same electorate suddenly discovered a new enthusiasm for the opposition while the rest stayed home in precisely the numbers required to produce the result. Turnout that begins to approach presidential levels in a midterm is not impossible, but it is rare enough that one might expect a certain curiosity. Instead, the preferred explanation is that the voters simply changed their minds en masse, and those who lost must therefore examine their own shortcomings.

The Republicans who blame themselves are learning a lesson, certainly. Whether it is the correct lesson is another matter. They are studying the surface of the board while the pieces have already been moved.

Of course, I am only a tailor. I notice patterns in fabric, not in ballots. Still, the cloth never lies about the shape beneath it, if one is willing to look closely enough.

text:
Kenyan politics is a muddy river with its own currents and hidden rocks. The one rule that never changes is this. You cannot plant a harvest from an air conditioned room, and you cannot forget the foot soldiers who dug the trenches and built your army with their own sweat and careers. When Fred Matiang’i first stepped onto the field he arrived with a wave of natural support that felt unstoppable. He was the tough Super CS, the doer that a tired Gen Z crowd and an opposition hungry for something new were ready to lift onto their shoulders.

How did he let a race that looked already won slip through his fingers? Now that same wave is drying up and he stands more alone each day. I once saw him as a real contender. Lately the signs have made me walk away from that hope.

How did so much early wind turn into a slow leak? Gloria Orwoba’s sharp interviews and Facebook notes, the walkouts of his old pillars, and the open complaints from people who used to defend him the loudest all point to the same crack. Grassroots roots were pulled up and the 2027 tree began to lean.

For years Matiang’i lived in a tall government tower where his word was the final brick. Orders went down and people simply carried them. That same tower mindset he carried into the open field.

Yet campaigns grow the opposite way. You do not bark commands and expect a crowd to march. You sit, you hear, you gather hands, and sometimes you lower your own head to ask for the vote.

Orwoba says he turned away from the local veterans and loyal shields who know every corner of Kenyan soil. Instead he closed himself inside a circle of faraway American consultants. Those outsiders kept polishing a shiny online show while the real contest kept moving on the dirt roads.

While Matiang’i and his circle stayed inside rooms talking plans, Edwin Sifuna was out walking the ground, gathering the same natural energy Matiang’i once held. Pieces of Gen Z now drift toward Sifuna and others toward Riggy G.

Here is where the story turns strange. While his loyal fighters stood in the open, taking the blows and risking their own names for him, Orwoba claims late night calls were coming from people tied to President Ruto’s broad government. She calls them watu wa Kasongo. They fed him wrong maps and advice that cut against his own path. He stopped hearing his own people and began treating some of them as hidden enemies. Picture a soldier who bled for the general only to be looked at as a spy. Orwoba herself must feel that sting.

She also says he made another deep cut. Even though he knows Kisii ground well he kept chasing support in places other opposition leaders had already locked, while leaving his own backyard open. Rivals moved in fast. In this country an empty plot does not stay empty.

In one Facebook post Orwoba wrote that his handlers told online voices to hammer Gachagua without mercy, yet the same advisers were quietly searching for her, begging for a way to reach Gachagua. Public war on the front page, private handshake behind the curtain.

She recalled that when he first came back from America his team was full of fire. Strong local minds offered clear paths. He did not take them. He let down the ones who had put everything on the line, and the walkouts followed.

Kisii Senator Richard Onyonka crossed to Sifuna’s side and became National Treasurer under Linda Mwananchi, pointing to disorganization and needless attacks on other opposition figures. Nyaribari Masaba MP Daniel Manduku joined UDA. Danstan Omari, once a strong legal shield, stepped back in public.

Omari now says Matiang’i should set aside 2027 dreams because the numbers and national reach are gone. He has lost key allies and shrunk from a national figure to a local one. Orwoba’s plainest line was that you cannot catch flies with vinegar. Kindness, quiet diplomacy, and a lower voice win more than sharp edges and pride.

The flying instructor of 20-year-old Learjet co-pilot Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, who died in the November 1 crash in Florida, has paid an extraordinary tribute to the young aviator he believed was born to fly.

Chris Kirk, who has spent 40 years teaching people to fly, described Nathalia as “the most naturally gifted pilot I have ever taught.”

He recalled how she consistently impressed examiners throughout her training, including during her qualification to fly the Learjet.

According to Kirk, one examiner was so impressed by her performance that he assumed she had accumulated 5,000 flight hours.

In reality, she had fewer than 1,100 at the time.

“There was not a check ride that the examiner was not blown away!” Kirk wrote.

Nathalia had earned her pilot's licence while still in high school and progressed into commercial aviation at an exceptionally young age.

She was among nine people killed when the Learjet 60 crashed in Florida on November 1.

Her instructor's tribute offers a glimpse of the young woman behind the headlines, someone remembered not simply for her age, but for her remarkable ability and passion for flying.

“That young lady was born to fly!”

text:
Man, the avocado toast and $7 coffees every morning are killing my budget. Or are they? Spoiler alert: I can’t even afford Avocados let alone avocado toast and $7 coffees!

TLDR: a mortgage on my childhood home where we lived comfortably when my dad earned 2/3 of what I do today, would cost me 100% of my take-home pay today, just 26 years later.

One thing we’ve seen clearly this year is that Trump and others are completely disconnected with the American people. I’ve made a few comments here and there about the affordability crisis which have gone semi-viral, and I see hundreds more on X every day from other hurting Americans. And there’s always at least one or two folks posting stupid shit about how we need to manage our money better. Well, here’s a real-life case study for you. I challenge anyoneto read this and tell me affordability is just in our heads or we need to better manage our money.

I grew up as the son of a professor. And not one at a hoity toity ivy-league school. One in Christian higher education. My dad never had a great salary while I was growing up, but we also never worried about bills, always had GOOD food on the table, my mom never had to hold down a job outside raising me and my six siblings, and we had regular opportunities for fun as a family.

When I was 14, we relocated from Tennessee where he taught for a Christian Liberal Arts college, to south Florida when he was hired to teach for a seminary. With a big family we needed a big house, but we bought way out in the suburbs, nearly a 90-minute commute for my dad, because that’s where we could afford. In 2000 he paid $287,000 for our 6 bed 4 bath 3740 square foot house. It wasn’t a custom home—just another home in another massive tract home development that has become a staple of the Florida housing market.

I don’t know what my dad’s salary was in 2000 when we moved. I’ve asked, but he hasn’t told me. I’ll make an educated guess that it was in the $70k range.

My parents sold that house in 2018 for $620,000 and paid cash for a new (bigger!) home on 7 acres in Tennessee. Good for them! That’s not the point of this story.

Zillow’s Zestimate for that house today is $958,100. They’ve got the estimated mortgage payment at $7245/month. Zillow’s price data is usually pretty spot-on, especially in hot suburban markets like south Florida. In 26 years, the value of that home has risen 336%.

I’m a smart guy and I know how to find things—the seminary where my dad used to work is, of course, 501(c)3, and as such, they must file an IRS form 990 which is public record. On that 990 they’re required to report the compensation of their highest earning employees. Unfortunately, the publicly available IRS 990 records don’t go back to 2000, but the oldest I could find was from 2014. In 2014 the seminary president earned $107k and none of the faculty earned enough to be reported. According to the 2025 990 (most recent available), the seminary president earned $158k, and the two highest earning professors earned $126k and $119k, respectively.

I’m a mid-level national manager for a publicly traded company in the reai estate and construction industry. I make right at $120k/year. After paying out just over 10% of my gross pay for health insurance premiums for the cheapest HDHP plan offered by my company, and after not quite hitting the match point for 401k contributions, my take home is just a hair under $7300/month.

If I wanted to buy my childhood home, that was comfortably owned by my dad while he made about 2/3 of my current income, I would need to spend virtually 100% of my take-home pay just for the mortgage payment. That leaves zero dollars for food. Zero dollars for groceries. Zero dollars for transportation. Zero dollars for internet. Zero dollars for anything else.

This isn’t poor money management. This is an affordability crisis driven by inflation, the devaluing of our dollar against real things like gold, and the corrupt and broken structure that our government has become.

Hundreds arrested in massive Florida sex sting — including former Mickey Mouse performer, 13 Disney workers, school deputy | Paul Sacca, Blaze Media

Hundreds were arrested in a recent multi-day undercover operation targeting child predators, prostitution, and human trafficking in Florida. The arrestees included 17 theme park employees, according to law enforcement.

The Polk County Sheriff's Office launched a seven-day joint-agency undercover operation "focusing on those who prey upon and travel to meet children for unlawful sexual activity, and human trafficking."

Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said the sting, named "Polk Around and Find Out II," is the "single largest undercover operation we’ve ever done."

The sheriff's office said in a statement that the undercover sting resulted in 281 arrests, including 239 related to soliciting prostitutes, offering to commit prostitution, and aiding/abetting or transporting prostitutes.

Authorities also arrested 31 suspects in connection with alleged child sex crimes.

Among those arrested were 17 theme park employees, including 13 from Disney and four from Universal Studios. Of the arrested theme park employees, seven were accused of committing child sex crimes, according to the sheriff's office.

WKMG-TV reported that a "former Walt Disney World Mickey Mouse character was among those arrested in the child predator operation."

The sheriff's office stated that 24-year-old Collin Klaco of Clermont "communicated online with an undercover detective posing as the guardian of a 13-year-old boy."

"He said he wanted to do something in a public family restroom," the police statement read. "He drove to the undercover location and was taken into custody; detectives found diapers and wipes in a backpack that he carried into the house."

"He wanted to wear diapers," Sheriff Judd explained. "He wanted to put diapers on the children, and he wanted to do all kinds of nasty stuff."

Judd added, "He had the high squeaky voice, too, by the way."

Police said Klaco was charged with traveling to meet a minor, use of a computer to solicit a guardian, use of a two-way communication device to commit a felony, and attempted lewd/lascivious battery on a minor.

Judd said all of the Disney employees caught in the sting had been fired.

"These predators are out there, online, trying to groom and violate our children," Judd said, adding that "the things that these predators say to children are vile, disgusting, and not fit for anyone except trained detectives to read. And even seasoned, trained detectives are repulsed."

The statement said 40-year-old Orange County Deputy Sheriff Eric Raymond was arrested in the sting.

Raymond, from Winter Garden, also is a school resource deputy at Independence Elementary School in Horizon West.

The statement said of Raymond, "He answered an online ad placed by an undercover detective and agreed to pay her $110.00 to have unprotected sex during a 'quick visit.' He told detectives he is married."

Raymond was charged with one count of solicitation of a prostitute.

Sheriff Judd said Raymond "should have known better."

"His actions demonstrate moral turpitude," Judd stated.

Sheriff Judd continued:

The online prostitution industry enables and empowers human traffickers, allowing them to profit off the people they exploit. Our goal is to identify victims, offer them help, and arrest those who are fueling the exploitation of human beings like Eric Raymond and those profiting from the exploitation of human beings. Prostitution is not a victimless crime — it results in human exploitation, misery, disease, dysfunction, drug and alcohol addiction, violence, and broken families.

Police noted that 32 illegal aliens from nine different countries were arrested.

WTVJ-TV reported that 16 suspects have been turned over to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

WTVJ added that 32 individuals were charged with drug possession, including methamphetamine, cocaine, and fentanyl.

Police said the suspects were charged with a total of 198 felonies and 290 misdemeanors. The statement added that the suspects had previous criminal charges totaling 358 felonies and 440 misdemeanors.

Law enforcement also identified 11 human trafficking victims during the operation.

text:
Cat-sized foxes in Texas are in trouble. Big guard dogs could help. | Laura Baisas, Popular Science

Two guard dogs could be protecting more than just the livestock grazing on the Rita Blanca National Grasslands in the Texas Panhandle. The working canines may be helping increase the odds of survival for the Lone Star State’s smallest fox.

The swift fox (Vulpes velox) is about the size of a house cat. While not federally listed as endangered, conservationists believe there are fewer than 250 left in Texas. They only occupy about 40 percent of their historic range, from Texas north to Alberta, Canada.

“The swift fox relies on the shortgrass prairie ecosystem once found across the Panhandle and into western Texas,” Haley Sloan, a doctoral student at Texas A&M, said in a profile. “Coyotes can take advantage of the cover provided by the taller vegetation that has grown into these areas, resulting in coyote predation being a leading cause of mortality in swift fox populations.”

Sloan is currently studying if livestock guardian dogs paired with a cattle herd can reduce swift fox mortality. The thought is that the dogs will act as a larger predator, and change the way the coyotes behave and use their habitat.

“The hope is that the dogs’ presence will deter coyotes, thereby reducing swift fox mortality and allowing the foxes to start using areas where the coyotes are being excluded,” Sloan said.

The dogs work in northwestern Texas’ Dallam County, the only known county in the state that still has a swift fox population. The swift fox’s small size and diet of insects, plants, and small rodents also means that they don’t pose any threats to cattle, sheep, and goats.

If incorporating these livestock guardian dogs with cattle herds alters the coyotes’ behavior, Sloan said that it offers two potential benefits. It could improve the chances of swift fox survival, while reducing the threat of livestock predation, especially during the vulnerable calving season.

To monitor the animals’ behavior, Sloan and the other researchers put GPS collars on coyotes and swift foxes ahead of this three-year-long project. The livestock guardian dogs were introduced with the cattle herd this summer. While it is too early to report any initial findings, the team has high hopes.

“I’m happy to report right now the dogs are doing great,” Sloan said. “The producer involved in the project hasn’t lost any calves to predation, and I have hope we’ll have similar positive outcomes for swift foxes in the vicinity of the herd.”

text:
This video brings up some good points when it comes to Lamar to the @MiamiDolphins 

Why it makes sense for the @MiamiDolphins to trade for  Lamar Jackson!!    

Lamar Jackson holds all the leverage. He has a no-trade clause, a no-tag clause, and an $84M cap hit. Because of that, Baltimore is facing three choices: trade him to a team of his choice on terms favorable to the acquiring team, cut him and get nothing, or keep him on the roster with an $84M cap hit.

If Lamar wanted Miami, the Dolphins could potentially offer Malik Willis plus a conditional 2028 2nd-round pick that could become a 2029 1st-round pick. From Baltimore's perspective, that's a better return than letting Lamar play out the final year of his contract and potentially ending up with only a 2029 compensatory 3rd-round pick.

Miami is projected to have around $100M in cap space, and trading for a top-5 QB may be a better use of those resources than overspending in free agency, especially when the front office has traditionally preferred to draft and develop talent.

Including Willis would help offset some of the cap concerns, and Lamar's roughly $52M cap hit in 2026 could be lowered through an extension. I could also see Miami using a front-loaded structure, taking advantage of its cap space in 2026 while maintaining flexibility down the road.

The biggest benefit for Miami is that it accelerates the retool. Instead of spending years hoping to find and develop a franchise QB, Miami would already have one in place while still being able to draft and develop a young quarterback such as LaNorris Sellers behind him. That potentially shortens the timeline back to contention while giving the Dolphins both a proven veteran and a long-term plan at the position.

A 49-unit coastal resort offering in Edisto Beach comes with a more interesting question than the nightly room rate: what exactly can the next owner do with it?  

Hilco is marketing the former Club Wyndham Ocean Ridge Sea Oaks and Sea Palms communities, with offers due November 13.  

The broker describes 49 units across 10 buildings, approximately 58,212 square feet on 6.1 acres. The offering is marketed as fee simple, free of Club Wyndham branding and management agreements. Sale remains subject to bankruptcy-court approval.  

My thoughts: The interesting part is the chance to simplify an old ownership structure and give existing buildings a workable next use. That opportunity has to survive title review, local approvals, building-condition work and coastal insurance costs. “Conversion potential” belongs in the diligence list until those answers exist.  No public asking price, occupancy, NOI or cap rate was disclosed in the materials reviewed. text:
November 3rd may mark the start of a new political paradigm. Democrats can build a lasting coalition around individual liberty, economic opportunity, and the American dream.

Much of the discussion about November 3rd will focus on voters turning against Republicans. Trump's unpopular policies drove demands for change. But that misses something important: Democrats' return to big tent politics.

Democrats won Senate races in Texas, Kansas, South Carolina, Iowa, Ohio, North Carolina, and Maine, alongside holds from Georgia to Oregon, with Mississippi and Alaska still being counted. In Kansas, a Democrat won a Senate seat for the first time since 1932, the year FDR was first elected. Across these states, Democrats won with candidates reflecting their communities.

These candidates offered different solutions to their states' challenges but shared the same concern: How do we make the lives of the people in our state better?

As Republicans focused on foreign wars, ballrooms, and self-enrichment, they gave Democrats an opening to return to their roots as a party of the working class, the middle class, and the American dream.

Just as Democrats have welcomed candidates with diverse views, they must welcome independents, former Republicans, and first-time voters who care about their communities but may never have seen themselves as Democrats.

Democrats are strongest when they speak to Americans as individuals as well as communities. Fighting discrimination remains essential. Yet every person has their own concerns, ambitions, and beliefs. A big tent gives them a voice in shaping the party, even when they don't agree with every position.

This is a chance to return to liberalism: individual liberty, equal rights, and the freedom and opportunity to build a better life.

Liberalism, once treated as a dirty word, is worth fighting for again. As MAGA concentrates power and advances the interests of the politically connected, Democrats can organize around protecting individual freedom and expanding opportunity.

The freedom to speak your mind, practice your faith, live according to your beliefs, and participate in public life without fear of political retaliation. The opportunity to afford a home, raise a family, start a business, and build a future.

But lasting political success requires delivery. Democrats must earn these votes again by making people's lives better.

There is a model in the party's history.

During the New Deal era, Franklin Roosevelt and congressional Democrats united Americans with different backgrounds, beliefs, and regional interests. They disagreed on plenty. But enough believed Democrats would improve their economic security and give them an opportunity to get ahead.

Social Security, worker protections, public investment, and financial reforms gave voters concrete reasons to keep supporting Democrats. People could experience what Democratic policies delivered.

That coalition sustained Democratic power for decades, especially in Congress. It also carried profound failures, including racial exclusions that denied many Black Americans the full benefits. A modern big tent can't be held together by excluding people. It must extend the promise of economic security to everyone.

The task now is to rebuild that connection between Democratic government and a better life. When people can afford a home, find a good job, access healthcare, and see a future for their children, they have reasons to keep supporting the party that made it possible.

That is the path for 2028, 2030, 2032, and beyond. Welcome a broader range of people. Protect individual liberty. Deliver greater economic opportunity. Build a coalition that lasts.

Trump helped create the opening. What Democrats build will determine whether this becomes a lasting political realignment.

The American dream needs a party willing to fight for it. Democrats can become that party for a new generation, and if they deliver, for decades to come.

text:
Local opposition stalled nearly $68B of data centers in three months. 

The AI industry thinks voters have a power bill problem. Voters actually have a permission problem.

Voters said no to data centers in 40 of 41 local ballot measures this week, and the industry's answer is to offer to pay for the power.

That fixes the bill. It doesn't fix the no.

The backlash started before anyone voted. 

Between April and June 2026, at least 45 data center projects worth nearly $68 billion were blocked or delayed by local opposition, according to Data Center Watch.

 @Bisnow reported that was more than half of the new large-scale data centers the firm tracked that quarter.

Then the ballots came.

 @CNBC reported 41 local measures in 10 states, and voters sided against the industry in every one except Harwood, North Dakota. In Granville, Ohio, 82.5% voted to prohibit them.

The complaint isn't AI. 

American Sentiment's database of 10,202 public comments at 417 local governments found water use was the top concern. 

73% of meetings had zero data center supporters. More than 90% of the comments were negative, and only 21% mentioned AI at all.

@Reuters/@Ipsos found 77% of Americans worry AI data centers will raise electricity costs. Strains on water and energy supplies topped the list of concerns.

So people are angry about the utility bill, the tap, and the closed-door deal. 

As @axios put it, voters want tech companies to pay for infrastructure, bring their own power, and stop the NDAs and secret deals.

@OpenAI's new "Compute Campus Policy Blueprint," like other developers' proposals, promises to cover power costs. That answers one of three demands.

A pledge to pay the bill doesn't win back a town that already voted not to build.

text:
THE BILLIONAIRE WHO TRIED TO ERASE OUR ENTIRE NEIGHBORHOOD

The eviction notice arrived in an envelope stamped FINAL DEMAND.

At first, I thought it had been delivered to the wrong address.

I had owned my home for twenty-three years.

My wife and I had paid off every cent of the mortgage. We raised two sons there. We buried our golden retriever beneath the maple tree in the backyard. Every crack in those walls had a memory attached to it.

Yet according to the letter, I was now an "unauthorized occupant" on property owned by a private development corporation.

They gave me forty-five days to leave.

My name is Michael Turner. I was sixty-four years old, a retired electrician living in a quiet suburb outside Columbus, Ohio.

The next morning, I found half the street standing outside with identical letters in their hands.

No one understood what was happening.

By lunchtime, three black SUVs rolled into the neighborhood.

A sharply dressed woman introduced herself.

"My name is Victoria Grant. I represent Crescent Horizon Holdings."

She smiled as if she were welcoming us to a neighborhood barbecue.

"Our company recently completed the acquisition of this community."

An elderly veteran laughed.

"You can't buy people who already own their homes."

Victoria didn't react.

"We're offering generous compensation to make relocation easy."

She handed each homeowner a sealed envelope.

Mine contained an offer nearly $250,000 above market value.

It was more money than I'd ever imagined.

I still tore it in half.

Within days strange things began happening.

Construction crews fenced off the empty lot at the end of the block.

Streetlights stopped working.

The city claimed maintenance had been delayed.

Then our water pressure suddenly dropped.

Coincidence?

None of us believed it.

I hired an attorney.

After reviewing my paperwork, she frowned.

"Your deed is valid," she said.

"So why are they acting like it isn't?"

"Because they aren't trying to prove they own your house."

"They're trying to prove your houses were never legally separated from the original land parcel."

That made no sense.

Until an unexpected visitor appeared.

A retired surveyor named Harold Benson knocked on my door carrying a rusted metal tube.

Inside were rolled-up maps dating back almost fifty years.

"I've been waiting for someone to ask the right question," he said.

According to the original subdivision plans, every homeowner legally owned their individual lot.

But beneath those records was another document few people had ever seen.

A permanent neighborhood covenant.

The agreement prevented the land from being sold as one project unless every single property owner agreed in writing.

Every single one.

Not a majority.

Not two-thirds.

Everyone.

Someone had quietly removed that covenant from later public copies decades earlier.

My attorney immediately filed an emergency motion.

The corporation insisted the covenant had never existed.

Then came the trial.

Their legal team presented a polished binder containing certified land records.

Everything appeared perfect.

Until Harold quietly unfolded his original survey map.

Hidden in the lower corner was the county registrar's embossed seal.

The same seal missing from every document the corporation relied on.

The courtroom became silent.

The judge ordered the county archives to produce the original records.

Three days later, they did.

The covenant was real.

Even worse for the corporation, investigators discovered someone had altered digital land records only six years earlier.

The forgery reached far beyond our neighborhood.

State investigators launched a criminal investigation.

The company's redevelopment project collapsed overnight.

Every eviction notice was canceled.

Every homeowner kept their property.

A month later, as life finally returned to normal, a silver limousine pulled up outside my house.

An elderly man stepped out.

He introduced himself as Arthur Holloway.

text:
$WEN Q3 2026 earnings: Wendy's profit falls fast as it rescues troubled franchise stores

Wendy's, the fast-food burger chain, unveiled its new turnaround strategy as falling customer traffic and franchisee distress cut deeply into profit. Sales at U. S. restaurants open at least 15 months fell 6%, while profit per share excluding one-offs dropped 46% to $0.13 on lower store margins and $12 million in consulting bills. Chief executive Bob Wright launched the Dave's Way plan and made breakfast optional for stores, without restoring a full-year outlook.

• U. S. same-restaurant sales: -𝟓.𝟕% (-7.0% last quarter)
• Revenue excluding advertising funds: $𝟒𝟑𝟓.𝟔𝐌 (-1.6% from a year ago)
• Profit per share, excluding one-offs: $𝟎.𝟏𝟑 (-46% from a year ago)
• Full-year 2026 outlook: 𝐖𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐡𝐞𝐥𝐝 (withdrawn last quarter)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🔴 Bearish

The story got worse because financial strain among franchise operators is now forcing Wendy's to step in with its own balance sheet. unpaid franchise bills drove up bad-debt expenses, and the company signed a deal with lenders to buy up to 163 restaurants from troubled operator Meritage Hospitality Group. One bright spot: U. S. net closures slowed to 13 stores, and finance chief Steve Cirulis said letting quiet locations drop breakfast could add up to $200 million in store-level profit.

The question now is whether buying weak franchise stores and cutting morning hours stabilizes the system or drains corporate cash while diners keep leaving. Either optional breakfast lifts franchisee profits enough to stop defaults, or taking over 163 Meritage stores drags down company margins further. Fourth-quarter bad-debt expenses and the final court-approved Meritage terms will show the cost.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢 𝐎𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐁𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐤𝐟𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐂𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐒𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐬 $𝟐𝟎𝟎 𝐌𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧
Morning hours have hurt restaurant profits and reduced sales at stores open at least 15 months. This quarter, the fast-food chain revised its breakfast strategy "to be location specific" after tests showed profit gains when quiet stores dropped the morning meal.

Finance chief Steve Cirulis said the change "could unlock up to $200 million in restaurant-level EBITDA across the system" (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization at individual stores). That relief goes straight to restaurant operators because they stop staffing kitchens during unprofitable morning hours, even though dropping breakfast reduces top-line sales.

What to watch: the fourth-quarter sales drag from stores opting out of breakfast, alongside U. S. restaurant margin. A wider margin on lower morning sales would confirm that cutting hours improves store profits.

🟢 𝐔.𝐒. 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐂𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐒𝐥𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐝 𝐃𝐨𝐰𝐧
Wendy's spent the first half of 2026 shutting weak U. S. locations, which shrank the base of restaurants paying royalties. In the third quarter, net U. S. closures slowed to 13 stores, leaving 5,711 domestic locations at quarter-end.

• U. S. net closures: 13 in Q3, down from 81 in Q2 and 164 in Q1
• U. S. sales at restaurants open at least 15 months: down 5.7%, compared with a 7.0% drop in Q2
• U. S. total systemwide sales: down 7.6% from a year ago, compared with an 8.2% drop in Q2

The slower pace of closures matches chief executive Bob Wright's decision to end broad closure targets. However, the U. S. store base is still 4.5% smaller than a year ago by our math, and customer traffic kept falling.

What to watch: fourth-quarter U. S. sales at established stores, which face an easy comparison against last year's 11.3% drop and include an extra calendar week. Failure to turn positive would show customer demand is still shrinking.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐅𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐧 𝐒𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐚 𝟏𝟔𝟑-𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐭
"We have evaluated the investment needs of Dave's Way and are confident we have the financial capacity to execute the strategy," Cirulis said. Yet franchisee distress is now pulling corporate cash and balance-sheet capacity into restaurant rescues.

Wendy's signed a letter of intent with franchisee Meritage Hospitality Group and its lenders to buy up to 163 restaurants, subject to higher offers and court approval. Meanwhile, franchise support and other costs rose 53.4% from a year ago to $26.9 million, climbing 1.7 percentage points of revenue by our math because of "an increase in the provision for doubtful accounts" on unpaid franchise fees.

Buying troubled stores turns a royalty collector into a store operator just as restaurant margins are shrinking. That is why the burger chain bought back zero shares again this quarter and kept its quarterly dividend at $0.07, half its level two quarters ago.

What to watch: the purchase price and store-level profit of the Meritage restaurants when a final agreement is filed. Taking on up to 163 low-margin stores will increase corporate operating costs and use up cash.

🔴🔴 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐟𝐟𝐢𝐜 𝐃𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐁𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐬 𝐂𝐮𝐭 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭
Fewer customers visited U. S. restaurants, while beef costs, wages and outside consultants drove expenses higher. Operating profit fell 39.3% from a year ago to $55.8 million, and profit per share excluding one-offs dropped 45.8% to $0.13.

• U. S. company-operated restaurant margin: 11.7%, down 1.4 percentage points from a year ago
• Cost of sales (food, paper and store labor): 88.7% of company store sales, up 1.1 percentage points by our math
• General and administrative overhead: $73.1 million, up 26.3% from a year ago (up 2.8 percentage points of total revenue)
• Profit before interest, taxes, depreciation and one-offs (adjusted EBITDA): $113.4 million, down 17.8%

Overhead jumped because Wendy's spent $11.9 million on third-party consultants for its new strategy and executive changes. Even excluding those fees, overhead rose by $3.4 million by our math while franchise royalty revenue shrank 6.6% to $119.4 million.

What to watch: fourth-quarter U. S. company-operated restaurant margin. With beef inflation easing in the second half of the year, another margin drop would prove that lost customer traffic is outrunning lower food inflation.

🔴 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰 𝐎𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝐨𝐧 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬
Wendy's has relied on international expansion to offset its shrinking U. S. business, adding 27 net international locations in the quarter to reach 1,483 stores. That pushed total international sales up 3.5% in constant currency, less than half the 8.6% pace of a year ago.

However, sales at international restaurants open at least 15 months fell 2.2% from a year ago, marking the third negative quarter in the last four. Because existing foreign stores are losing sales, new openings are doing all the work, and the international division remains too small at 16.5% of global sales by our math to make up for U. S. declines.

What to watch: international sales at established stores in the fourth quarter. A fourth decline in five quarters would show that brand weakness abroad is offsetting new store openings.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Three standing risks received no new numbers or updates in the third-quarter earnings release.

• Withheld full-year targets: Wendy's did not restore a 2026 financial outlook after withdrawing it last quarter, and gave no multi-year spending budget for Dave's Way.
• Debt leverage and refinancing: net debt stands at $3.01 billion, or 6.5 times trailing 12-month adjusted EBITDA by our math, with no update in the release on refinancing the $430 million of notes due in March 2028.
• China expansion deal: the release gave no update on the 1,000-store China agreement, which either side can cancel without penalty before December 12, 2026.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐃𝐚𝐯𝐞'𝐬 𝐖𝐚𝐲 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐡 𝐖𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭𝐬
Chief executive Bob Wright replaced last year's turnaround plan with Dave's Way, a strategy aimed at "growing customer traffic and market share while strengthening restaurant profitability". The company hired Chief Marketing and Customer Growth Officer Tariq Hassan, began testing menu upgrades, and planned "transfers of franchised restaurants to well-capitalized, high-performing operators". Wendy's recorded $11.9 million in consulting and reorganization charges this quarter, but published no cost targets or revenue goals.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐝𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐟𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟒𝟑𝟓.𝟔 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Revenue excluding advertising funds — the royalties, store sales and rent Wendy's keeps — fell 1.6% from a year ago. Total revenue dipped only 0.5% to $547.0 million because franchisees shifted local marketing money into the national advertising fund, which adds to reported revenue without adding profit.

𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐟𝐥𝐨𝐰 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟓𝟑.𝟗 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Third-quarter free cash flow fell 37.4% from a year ago by our math, pulling the nine-month total down 10.9% to $174.2 million. Operating cash flow dropped by $36.3 million over the first nine months, which the restaurant group partly cushioned by cutting capital spending and franchise development loans by $23.8 million.

𝐃𝐞𝐟𝐞𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐟𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐟𝐞𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟖𝟎.𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Long-term deferred franchise fees — upfront cash paid by franchisees for future store openings — shrank 2.0% from last quarter and 9.0% since the end of 2025 by our math. The balance has fallen every quarter this year as U. S. store closures accelerate fee recognition while new domestic development slows.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐥𝐲 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐝𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐝: $𝟎.𝟎𝟕 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from $0.07 per share ($0.28 annualized)
Unchanged. The board declared a fourth-quarter dividend of $0.07 per share, matching the annualized $0.28 rate set in August after two cuts in five quarters. With third-quarter profit per share excluding one-offs down to $0.13, the quarterly payout takes 53.8% of earnings by our math, right inside the Ohio company's 50% to 60% target.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐛𝐮𝐲𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝟏𝟔𝟑 𝐌𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐠𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭?
Wendy's signed a letter of intent with Meritage and its lenders for up to 163 stores under court approval. Investors need the purchase price, the stores' current profit margins, and whether other struggling franchisees also require buyouts.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐃𝐚𝐯𝐞'𝐬 𝐖𝐚𝐲 𝐥𝐚𝐮𝐧𝐜𝐡 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭𝐬?
Management withdrew its 2026 outlook last quarter to build a turnaround plan, but unveiled Dave's Way with no multi-year revenue, profit or spending numbers. When will the company restore full-year financial targets?

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐲 𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐝𝐫𝐨𝐩 𝐛𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐤𝐟𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐨 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡 $𝟐𝟎𝟎𝐌?
Finance chief Steve Cirulis said location-specific breakfast could add up to $200 million in store-level profit across the system. How many restaurants must drop morning hours to hit that figure, and how much will that reduce systemwide sales?

𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝟏,𝟎𝟎𝟎-𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐂𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐚 𝐚𝐠𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐩𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐃𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐦𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝟏𝟐?
Last quarter's filing showed either party can cancel the China master franchise deal without penalty before December 12, 2026. The release did not mention China, leaving open whether Wendy's largest international growth pipeline is still intact.

text:
Over Klaver, een verjaardag en mijn eigen voortvarendheid

Waarde Lezer,

Ik heb besloten mijn eerdere stuk over Jesse Klaver en de verjaardag van zijn zoontje geheel offline te halen.

Ook ik ben, zo moet ik tot mijn lichte schaamte bekennen, in de commotie meegegaan. De suggestie dat het verjaardagsverhaal van Klaver niet kon kloppen, blijkt bij nader onderzoek ongegrond.

Uit de parlementaire verslagen van 2013 en 2014 valt namelijk op te maken dat zijn zoon Maurits begin november, misschien zelfs eind oktober 2013 werd geboren. Een verjaardag die op zaterdag 31 oktober 2026 wordt gevierd, is daarmee volstrekt aannemelijk.

Daarmee vervalt de grondslag van mijn eerdere kritiek.

Toch kwam de verwarring niet geheel uit de lucht vallen.

In een interview met The Guardian uit maart 2017 verklaarde Klaver zelf dat zijn oudste zoon slechts enkele weken oud was toen Wilders op 19 maart 2014 zijn beruchte ‘minder, minder’-uitspraak deed.

Ook in een eigen bijdrage aan BNNVARA uit december 2016 sprak Klaver over zijn ‘pasgeboren zoontje’ en dat hij ‘net vader geworden’ was.

De werkelijkheid is dat Maurits toen ongeveer vierenhalve maand oud was.

Nu kan men natuurlijk twisten over de precieze betekenis van ‘pasgeboren’, maar ‘een paar weken oud’ lijkt mij toch een wat creatieve beschrijving van een kind dat zijn vijfde levensmaand nadert.

Dat verklaart de verwarring. Het rechtvaardigt niet mijn eerdere conclusie.

En aangezien ik anderen nogal eens de maat neem over feiten, zorgvuldigheid en het trekken van conclusies, lijkt het mij niet meer dan behoorlijk diezelfde maatstaf ook op mijzelf toe te passen.

De feiten gaan vóór de polemiek. Ook wanneer de polemiek aanzienlijk vermakelijker was.

Wat natuurlijk blijft, is het trillende lipje, de indringende stilte en de nadrukkelijke ontroering waarmee Klaver zijn persoonlijke offer aan het Vaderland presenteerde.

Of wij daar getuige waren van oprechte emotie of van politieke dramaturgie, laat ik, waarde lezer, geheel aan U.

Ik heb immers zojuist geleerd dat een vermoeden, hoe aantrekkelijk ook, nog geen bewijs is.

The next opportunity window may be taking shape. Here’s my 2026 U.S. stock watchlist — and the reasoning behind each name. 

$AVGO — Broadcom
The long-term AI infrastructure story remains intact. I’d rather look for pullbacks toward key support than chase an extended move.

$TSM — TSMC
Its lead in advanced chip manufacturing remains a major competitive advantage. Consolidation is underway, and a deeper retest could offer a better entry.

$ORCL — Oracle
Cloud growth is gaining traction, but the stock has already priced in a lot of optimism. Patience may offer a better risk-reward setup.
$CRM — Salesforce
A leading name in enterprise software, though valuation still matters. Near-term volatility wouldn't surprise me, but the longer-term opportunity is worth tracking.

$SMCI — Super Micro Computer
High exposure to AI server demand comes with high volatility. I'd avoid chasing sharp rallies and wait for a more attractive setup.

$AMAT — Applied Materials
A key player in semiconductor equipment. Improving industry demand could be a tailwind, but I'd keep some buying power available for pullbacks.

$QCOM — Qualcomm
Its exposure to smartphones, automotive, and edge AI gives it multiple growth drivers. The near-term picture may remain range-bound, but the longer-term story is broader than phones.

$ANET — Arista Networks
Data-center networking remains an important part of the AI infrastructure buildout. Pullbacks are worth watching as long as demand and execution stay strong.

$SBUX — Starbucks
The turnaround story depends on a sustained consumer recovery and stronger operating performance. I'd rather see the numbers improve than rely on sentiment alone.

$UNH — UnitedHealth
Healthcare exposure can add diversification beyond high-growth tech. The key is whether operating performance stabilizes and earnings visibility improves.

$DIS — Disney
Streaming and theme parks give Disney two important business engines. The next step is proving that growth can translate into stronger, more consistent profitability.

The best opportunities aren't always the stocks making headlines. Sometimes they're the businesses where the fundamentals improve before sentiment catches up.

A watchlist is a starting point, not a buy list. Entry price, valuation, and risk management still matter.

text:
Clontibret O’Neills Launches Healthy Club Committee

Clontibret O’Neills GAA has established a new Healthy Club Committee to help make health, wellbeing and belonging part of everyday club life.

The committee, formed at the clubhouse on 4 November, brings together Damien McKenna, Fiona Dolan, Eileen Morgan, Maire Meehan and Enda Brennan, working alongside Healthy Club Officer Stephen Dalton and with the support of the club executive.

Its aim is straightforward: to help everyone who engages with the club have a positive, welcoming and health-enhancing experience — whether as a player, coach, volunteer, parent, supporter or member of the wider community.

In practical terms, this means supporting opportunities for people of different ages and abilities to participate, encouraging movement and social contact, and considering how everyday club decisions, communications and practices affect people’s wellbeing. The committee will recognise the good work already happening and listen to the community about where improvements could make a difference.

There is already a strong foundation to build on. Club members accumulated 3,960 km in the Irish Life Steps Challenge, while the St Brigid’s Day Health Reset Walk & Talk brought people together following the winter storms. Thirty participants also completed the six-week Walk to Jog programme, including people who would not usually take part in club activities.

The committee’s next meeting, on 19 November, will focus on developing a practical plan for the year ahead. An early priority is to recruit volunteer walk leaders, with fully funded training available. The aim is to offer regular opportunities to walk together on the club track and in the surrounding area, helping people stay active and connected through the winter months.

These actions will support Clontibret O’Neills’ progress towards Healthy Club accreditation and strengthen the club’s contribution to community life.

Get involved

The committee would like to hear from anyone interested in becoming a walk leader, joining future walks, volunteering or suggesting ways to make the club more welcoming and inclusive.

You do not need to be a player or a regular club participant. Contact Stephen Dalton or any committee member to express your interest, and watch the club notes and club app for updates.

Everyone has something to contribute. A little time, a practical idea or an invitation to someone who might otherwise stay at home can help build a healthier, more connected Clontibret community.

text:
Christ’s Sacrifice Once for All

10 The law is only a shadow of the good things that are coming—not the realities themselves. For this reason it can never, by the same sacrifices repeated endlessly year after year, make perfect those who draw near to worship. 2 Otherwise, would they not have stopped being offered? For the worshipers would have been cleansed once for all, and would no longer have felt guilty for their sins. 3 But those sacrifices are an annual reminder of sins. 4 It is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

5 Therefore, when Christ came into the world, he said:

“Sacrifice and offering you did not desire,
    but a body you prepared for me;
6 with burnt offerings and sin offerings
    you were not pleased.
7 Then I said, ‘Here I am—it is written about me in the scroll—
    I have come to do your will, my God.’”[a]
8 First he said, “Sacrifices and offerings, burnt offerings and sin offerings you did not desire, nor were you pleased with them”—though they were offered in accordance with the law. 9 Then he said, “Here I am, I have come to do your will.” He sets aside the first to establish the second. 10 And by that will, we have been made holy through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

11 Day after day every priest stands and performs his religious duties; again and again he offers the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins. 12 But when this priest had offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, he sat down at the right hand of God, 13 and since that time he waits for his enemies to be made his footstool. 14 For by one sacrifice he has made perfect forever those who are being made holy.

15 The Holy Spirit also testifies to us about this. First he says:

16 “This is the covenant I will make with them
    after that time, says the Lord.
I will put my laws in their hearts,
    and I will write them on their minds.”[b]
17 Then he adds:

“Their sins and lawless acts
    I will remember no more.”[c]
18 And where these have been forgiven, sacrifice for sin is no longer necessary.

A Call to Persevere in Faith
19 Therefore, brothers and sisters, since we have confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus, 20 by a new and living way opened for us through the curtain, that is, his body, 21 and since we have a great priest over the house of God, 22 let us draw near to God with a sincere heart and with the full assurance that faith brings, having our hearts sprinkled to cleanse us from a guilty conscience and having our bodies washed with pure water. 23 Let us hold unswervingly to the hope we profess, for he who promised is faithful. 24 And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds, 25 not giving up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging one another—and all the more as you see the Day approaching.

26 If we deliberately keep on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, no sacrifice for sins is left, 27 but only a fearful expectation of judgment and of raging fire that will consume the enemies of God. 28 Anyone who rejected the law of Moses died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses. 29 How much more severely do you think someone deserves to be punished who has trampled the Son of God underfoot, who has treated as an unholy thing the blood of the covenant that sanctified them, and who has insulted the Spirit of grace? 30 For we know him who said, “It is mine to avenge; I will repay,”[d] and again, “The Lord will judge his people.”[e] 31 It is a dreadful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

🪷 Diwali Lakshmi Puja | A Simple Step-by-Step Guide 🪔
By The Sadhana Movement 

1. Set Up Your Altar

Clean your Puja space and place the Murtis or images of Shri Ganesha, Maa Lakshmi, and Maa Saraswati.

Keep flowers, a diya, dhoop, kumkum, akshata (unbroken rice), sweets, fruits, and other offerings ready.

2. Prepare the Kalash for Maa Lakshmi 🪷

* Take a clean Kalash and apply Haldi and Kumkum to it.
* Tie a sacred red thread (Mouli/Kalava) around its neck.
* Fill the Kalash with clean water.
* Add a coin, turmeric root, and a few grains of Akshata (unbroken rice) to the water.
* Place five mango leaves at the mouth of the Kalash and apply Haldi and Kumkum to the leaves.
* Place a coconut on top, preferably wrapped in a red cloth.
* Keep the Kalash near Maa Lakshmi’s Murti or image preferable on some unbroken rice 

🪔 BEGIN YOUR PUJA

3. Light a Diya

Begin by lighting a ghee or oil diya

दीपज्योतिः परब्रह्म दीपः सर्वतमोपहः ।
Dīpa-jyotiḥ parabrahma dīpaḥ sarva-tamōpahaḥ.

4. Worship Shri Ganesha

Offer flowers to Shri Ganesha and chant 3 times:

ॐ गं गणपतये नमः।
Aum Gam Ganpataye Namah 

5. Worship Maa Lakshmi

Offer flowers, kumkum, and akshata to Maa Lakshmi and the Kalash.

Chant:

ॐ श्रीं महालक्ष्म्यै नमः।
Aum Shreem Mahalakshmyai Namah

Pray for prosperity, nourishment, harmony, and abundance in all aspects of life.

6. Worship Your Dhan (Wealth)

Place coins, gold or silver ornaments, or other symbols of wealth near Maa Lakshmi.

Offer kumkum, akshata, and flowers.

This is an expression of gratitude for the resources we receive and a reminder to use wealth with wisdom, responsibility, and Dharma.

7. Chant Maa Lakshmi’s Names

Recite or listen to any one of the following:

* Sri Lakshmi Ashtottara Shatanamavali (108 Names)
* Sri Mahalakshmi Ashtakam
8. Worship Maa Saraswati

Offer flowers to Maa Saraswati and chant:

ॐ ऐं सरस्वत्यै नमः।

Om Aim Saraswatyai Namah

Place your books, notebooks, or musical instruments near the altar and offer flowers, kumkum, and akshata respectfully.

Seek Her blessings for knowledge, clarity, creativity, and wisdom.

9. Offer Dhoopam & Deepam

Offer incense (Dhoopam), followed by the light of a diya (Deepam), to the Deities.

10. Offer Naivedya

Offer freshly prepared sweets, fruits, or other sattvic food as Naivedya with gratitude.

11. Conclude with Aarti

Perform any Aarti you know, or simply offer a camphor (Karpur) Aarti.

Bow down and offer your gratitude to the Divine.

text:
The origin of Chicken McDo

Chicken McDo is McDonald's Philippines' popular fried-chicken meal, typically served with rice and gravy. It became a familiar Filipino fast-food favorite by combining McDonald's international brand with local preferences for rice-based meals and crispy fried chicken.

How it started
In 1981, Dr. George T. Yang opened the first McDonald's restaurant in the Philippines in Morayta, Manila. Initially, the menu focused on McDonald's international offerings.

Yang recognized that Filipinos loved fried chicken and rice, so he pushed for a menu adapted to local tastes. In 1986, Chicken McDo was introduced alongside McSpaghetti, helping establish McDonald's as a fast-food brand that catered to Filipino preferences. 

Why it became popular?

- Crispy, flavorful fried chicken suited Filipino tastes.
- Rice and gravy made it a satisfying, familiar meal.
- It offered an alternative to burgers and fries.
- Its combination of international branding and local food preferences helped it become a Filipino fast-food staple.

Chicken McDo has continued to evolve, including a major size and crispiness upgrade in 2023. 😉

🪔Yam Deepam Remedy 

Yama Deepam : After Pradosh Kaal (in the southern direction of the main door as the evening deepens) 

Yam Deepam (or Yamraj Diya) is a sacred ritual performed on Dhanteras to honor Lord Yama, the god of death and justice, seeking protection from untimely death (akal mrityu), disease, and negative energy.

🏹The Legend: It is connected to the story of King Hima’s 16-year-old son, whose horoscope predicted death by a snakebite on his fourth wedding day. 

His clever wife did put gold, silver, and sparkling jewelry at the entrance and lit numerous lamps. When Yama arrived disguised as a serpent, the dazzling light blinded him, and he left peacefully without taking the prince's life

🪔Yam Deep / Yama Deepam

Light a lamp outside the house (southern direction) in honor of Yama Dev (Lord of Death). 

This is said to protect the family from untimely death.

📍🚩How to Perform the Yam Deepam Remedy

👉🏻Prepare The Lamp: Use a large, four-faced (Chaumukhi) earthen (mud) diya or an flour (ata) lamp.

👉🏻Wicks and Oil: Place four cotton wicks pointing in all four directions, and fill the lamp with mustard oil or sesame (til) oil.

👉🏻The Seat: Place a small heap of uncooked rice grains or wheat on the ground outside your main entrance to act as a seat for the diya.

👉🏻Direction: Place and light the lamp in the evening at dusk/sunset outside your main door, facing south (the direction of Lord Yama).

👉🏻Offerings: Offer water, vermilion (roli), rice, flowers, and sweets (prasad) to the lamp while offering your prayers

👉🏻Mantra: Chant the mantra "ॐ यमाय नमः" 11 times while mentally offering the lamp to Lord Yama and praying for the health, safety, and longevity of your household.

Let the lamp burn out naturally; do not blow it out.

text:
I worked the polls here in North Carolina, and we need to be honest about where we failed. Voters approved photo ID for all voters, a 3.5% state income tax cap, and requiring limits on local property tax increases. They supported those policies, but we failed to connect that economic message to our candidates.

I kept telling Michael Whatley’s crew to talk about jobs, manufacturing, and helping people afford their lives. Instead, too much messaging leaned on emotional hot-button issues and the same rallying cries aimed at our own base.

Our organization fell short, too. In my county, we scrambled for volunteers at the last minute. Meanwhile, I watched groups supporting Democrats provide coverage, relief, and food for their people. I worked until I couldn’t anymore. Dedicated volunteers cannot compensate for poor planning.

One white woman supporting a write-in candidate told a Black woman distributing Democratic sample ballots that she would vote for anyone whose name “sounded” like a Black woman’s name. I found that deeply racist. A name tells you nothing about someone’s qualifications, and no party owns anyone’s vote.

“You can’t argue with people who have hubris over intellect.”

But Republicans need to examine ourselves, too. An R beside someone’s name does not qualify them to govern, any more than “not Trump” does. Blind loyalty is a problem on either side.

Read Xi Van Fleet’s Mao’s America: A Survivor’s Warning. History offers painful examples of movements turning against their supporters. Loyalty should never replace independent judgment.

I prayed for God’s will, and my trust in Him cannot depend on getting the election results I wanted.

“Let us not be weary in well doing.” Galatians 6:9

I’m continuing the work God called me to do: helping people through addiction and recovery and supporting opportunities to rebuild their lives. Politics matters, but we cannot wait for an election victory to help our neighbors or expect legislation to change a heart.

text:
Bookkeepers and Fractional CFOs: The Property Sale Hit Your Ledger Before It Hit the Tax Plan.

To the Texas bookkeepers, fractional CFOs, and controllers closing out the year for owner-operators: this one is for you.

You see a sale the day it posts. You also see the depreciation schedule, the loan payoff, and the proceeds landing in the bank account. Often you are the first person the owner asks, "How did we do this year?"

Here is a scenario. A business owner (and accredited investor) sells a rental building held for many years. The books show a large gain. The owner assumes the CPA will sort it out in the spring.

Three things are worth noticing early:

1. The gain is not the same as the cash.

Tax on a sale is generally computed on the sale price less the adjusted basis, not on what hit the bank. Years of depreciation lower the basis, which generally raises the gain, and part of that gain can be taxed differently from the rest.

2. Some options have to be in place before closing.

A 1031 exchange generally requires a qualified intermediary engaged before the sale closes, with strict identification and closing windows afterward. If the property has already closed, the set of options is smaller. Whether any option fits is a CPA question.

3. Categories exist for owners who want to stay invested without managing a property.

Delaware Statutory Trusts are one category that can serve as replacement property in an exchange. They carry real risks: loss of principal is possible, interests are illiquid, and nothing is guaranteed. Whether a category fits depends on the owner's full financial picture.

You are not expected to give tax advice, and you should not have to. When a sale shows up in the ledger, one question helps: "Has your CPA seen this yet, and did anyone plan for it before closing?"

That question takes ten seconds. Owners remember the person who asked it.

I work with bookkeepers, CPAs, and real estate professionals across Texas when their clients face a large capital gains event. If a client of yours is in that position, I am glad to be a resource. Reach out anytime, or schedule a conversation. Please review your specific situation with your CPA.
