text:
All right, this is where Yakuza 4 Remastered can either become a fairly manageable trophy cleanup or a much longer attempt to clear absolutely everything. I would decide which one I’m doing before spending an evening trying to master pool.

The platinum/all-achievements route does not require the complete minigame checklist. The in-game checklist has substantially tougher targets, and completing its minigames earns the Golden Pistol from Bob at Naomi’s Palace. Haruka’s Trust is another separate project, available only in Premium Adventure and unnecessary for either the platinum or the game’s 100% completion percentage.

One platform detail matters immediately: pachinko is present on PS4 and Xbox consoles, but absent from the Steam and Windows PC versions. PC players do not have a missing pachinko requirement to fix. The corresponding trophy/achievement is absent there too.

I’d keep a dedicated cleanup save, save after difficult successes, and check the Challenges menu rather than trying to remember what counted. A loaded older save also restores its older completion progress. Save-scumming a casino loss is useful; accidentally erasing a successful arcade run is less useful.

CLUB SEGA: THREE GAMES, NOT JUST TWO

Welcome to SEGA wants participation in UFO Catcher, Boxcelios 2, and the original Boxcelios. Actually finish the arcade attempts instead of entering and immediately quitting.

To unlock the original Boxcelios, use Akiyama at the Theater Square arcade, finish three Boxcelios 2 plays, and follow up with the employee. This is tied to his ally progression. Once the older cabinets are installed, play one of those too.

For full completion, both Boxcelios games require level 50. In both, your target is the glowing core rather than every piece of metal surrounding it. Firing slows your movement, so reposition first, then shoot through a clear line. Holding fire continuously can leave you slowly chewing through the wrong part of the enemy.

Boxcelios 2 gives a short free window at the start of each enemy and rewards sufficiently fast kills with extra time. Build that cushion on early enemies. Original Boxcelios also has a brief free window, but no equivalent quick-kill time bonus. Its apparent 3D shapes can obscure the fact that an intervening piece still blocks the shot. Move close to the core when possible.

For UFO Catcher, full completion means every distinct prize, not a set number of successful grabs. The 23-prize checklist is:

• Piyo-chan, Silkie Piyo-chan, Sky Piyo-chan, Peach Piyo-chan, and Big Piyo-chan.
• AiAi, Manjiro, Golden Manjiro, and Syrup Boy.
• Hito-nyan: Normal, Disappointed, and Happy.
• Pillow Pups in Golden Retriever, Shiba, French Bulldog, and Chihuahua, in both regular and giant sizes.
• Yummy Bar: Spicy Cod Roe, Salami, and Sauce.

Check both arcades and refresh the machines through the attendant or by leaving and returning. Golden Manjiro is worth specifically checking for at Nakamichi. Use the side camera before committing the depth movement. If a toy slips out, change where the claw catches its shape rather than repeating exactly the same grab.

BATTING: LEARN CONTACT FIRST, SCORE SECOND

Captain Two-fer only requires one hit that breaks two panels simultaneously. Aim at a shared border. That is much less demanding than completing the batting checklist, which wants S rank on every course.

The S-rank targets are Easy 2,300, Normal 2,800, Hard 3,000, and Extra Hard 3,500. Extra Hard unlocks after scoring at least 1,800 on Hard.

Watch the batter as well as the pitch. The bat settles when the swing window approaches. The pitch sequence repeats, so a short practice run spent learning the slow curves is more productive than changing your timing randomly every attempt.

Multi-panel shots matter because they multiply the score, including completed lines. On Hard, hit the three single panels of a diagonal, then use corners around the center panel to clear the remaining groups of three. The final group can complete several lines together. On Extra Hard, work in blocks and preserve a central block that can complete several lines at once. Take the bonus bullseye seriously when it appears; you only get one pitch at it.

BOWLING: THREE STRIKES VERSUS A WHOLE SCORECARD

Boiled Turkey means three consecutive strikes. Full completion requires 200 points in one ten-frame game at Mach Bowl.

I’d use a ten-frame game even for the trophy. It gives you room to establish a repeatable delivery and then continue straight into the 200-point target.

Aim for the pocket beside the head pin rather than the head pin’s center. Pick one starting position and power range, then make small angle or spin corrections. A useful starting test is one position to the right of center with an almost straight delivery. If that does not suit your timing, try a wider starting position and a modest inward curve. Neither setup should be treated as a guaranteed strike macro.

Once you find a delivery that works, repeat its actual inputs. Do not change ball, angle, power, and spin simultaneously after one bad result. Spares still matter for the 200-point target, especially when they preserve the bonus from a preceding strike.

DARTS: THE THROW NEEDS TO BE REPEATABLE

Hat Trick wants three bullseyes in the same three-dart turn. At Bantam, use a long 01 game if you want plenty of attempts.

On a controller, aim with the left stick, draw the right stick back smoothly, and release it cleanly. A violent flick or inconsistent pull can change where the dart lands. Start with roughly half a pull and adjust based on the actual result. The hand also moves, so do not assume an aim point stays fixed forever while you hesitate.

Full completion requires beating Beginner, Intermediate, and Advanced opponents in five categories: an 01 game, Standard Cricket, Random Cricket, Hidden Cricket, and Count-Up. That is 15 wins. You do not need separate wins in every 301/501/701/901 length; 301 is the efficient choice for the 01 category.

Count-Up rewards raw scoring. In 01, plan the final exact total before throwing yourself into a bust. In Cricket, watch which scoring areas are still open: hitting a triple can close a number immediately, but scoring repeatedly on a number your opponent already closed accomplishes nothing.

POOL: THE TROPHY IS A SMALL PART OF THE JOB

First Carom asks you to score the first point in Four-Ball at Cuez Bar. Choose Beginner, take the opening turn, and make your cue ball contact two other balls in one shot. A cushion-assisted route is fine. You do not need to win the whole match for that trophy.

Full completion is 16 wins: Nine-Ball, Eight-Ball, Rotation, and Four-Ball against all four difficulty levels.

Use the overhead view, line up carefully, and pull the shot stick straight back. If your shot direction repeatedly disagrees with your aim, check for sideways movement during the stroke before rebuilding your entire strategy.

Nine-Ball requires contacting the lowest-numbered ball first, but a legal combination that pockets the nine wins immediately. Eight-Ball requires clearing your assigned group before legally potting the eight. Rotation also demands lowest-number-first contact, while the pocketed ball’s number supplies its points. Four-Ball rewards caroms rather than pockets.

At higher difficulty, cue-ball position matters as much as making the current pot. Use enough power to finish the shot without sending the cue ball somewhere that ruins the next one. A calm safety is preferable to handing over an easy table after a reckless scratch.

MAHJONG: SEVEN PAIRS IS A SPECIFIC HAND

Seven Pairs wants seven different pairs in a concealed hand. Four copies of one tile do not count as two pairs. Do not call chi, pon, or kan while building this particular hand. Winning with ron on another player’s final discard is valid; you do not have to self-draw with tsumo.

I’d look for a starting hand already containing several pairs. Keep those pairs, discard excess third copies, and compare your remaining singles against the visible discards. A single whose other three copies are already visible cannot become your seventh pair.

At six pairs plus a single, check whether riichi is available. Riichi does not invalidate Seven Pairs. It can add value and automate ordinary discards while you wait, but it also locks your hand, so choose the remaining tile carefully.

Full mahjong completion is different: finish a game with at least 50,000 points before the placement bonus, usually called uma. Merely seeing a post-bonus result above 50,000 is not enough.

For that longer target, do not force Seven Pairs every hand. Build efficient hands, use red dora if enabled, and protect a strong score instead of chasing an unnecessary expensive hand into an opponent’s riichi. A normal four-meld-and-a-pair shape still needs a valid yaku; dora alone does not supply one. Keeping a hand closed makes riichi available once it is ready, which is a straightforward way for beginners to establish a yaku.

SHOGI: PROMOTION DOES NOT MEAN RANKING UP

Shogi Promotion means promoting a piece on the board. It does not require grinding the ranked opponent ladder.

Use Challenge 1 at Shoten Shogi. Clear a route for an eligible piece, move it into the opponent’s promotion zone, and accept the promotion prompt. Dropping a captured piece directly into that zone does not immediately promote it.

For full completion, win five games. Challenge 1 can be repeated for all five. Its limited opposing army makes it a practical place to learn the difference between threatening the king and actually trapping it. Support the attacking piece with a second piece so the king cannot simply capture it or step aside. Remember that captured pieces can return to the board as drops, which changes the mating patterns if you are approaching this like western chess.

KARAOKE: PLAYING THE SONG AND CLEARING IT ARE DIFFERENT

The Human Jukebox requires registering a performance for every song, with no 900-point demand. Full completion wants at least 900 on all 11:

Otomeiro My Life; Machine Gun Kiss; Raindrops; Pure Love in Kamurocho; GET to the Top!; I Wanna Change Myself; Kamurocho Lullaby; Summer Memories; Where Has Your Touch Gone?; Saturday Night Lover; Shooting Star.

Kiryu is convenient for the cleanup because he can sing or provide support for the full selection. You can support the machine’s vocals without arranging a date for every song. Saejima does not participate.

For high scores on support tracks, choose Lively rather than Simple. Read hold and rapid-press prompts properly, and focus on the timing lane rather than the background video. Singing follows the vocal phrasing, which may not match the steady beat you would use while cheering.

Haruka can accompany Kiryu only in Premium Adventure. Her version of GET to the Top! becomes available after scoring at least 900 on Otomeiro My Life. You do not need that particular singer’s version merely to register GET to the Top! for The Human Jukebox.

TABLE TENNIS AND MASSAGE

Table Tennis Pro wants three Heat smashes in one match at Yunosono Hot Springs. I’d fit all three into the same game to avoid any tracking ambiguity. Full completion requires winning on all three difficulties.

Build Heat through good returns and the gaze control, then use the smash when the gauge is ready. Watch for the ball’s timing flash. Keep aiming simple until you can rally reliably. A smash is not always an automatic point, especially late in a harder match, so stay ready to return the ball afterward instead of relaxing during the animation.

VIP Member is the easy half of Love in Heart: take five massages to unlock VIP membership. Full completion requires the top Serene Dragon result on all four courses. Five visits unlock the third course; ten unlock the fourth.

For the massage game, watch the gauge and its momentum. Small corrections are safer than holding an input until the marker rockets to the opposite edge. Higher positions earn points faster, but a failed session is worse than spending part of the course safely in the middle. Learn each course’s sudden changes before trying to keep the marker near the top. Do not assume every pulse behaves identically on the hardest course.

FISHING AND GOLF

Mr. Outdoors asks for five fishing attempts and five golf plays. Use the same character for a clean route. For fishing, actually cast and let the attempt resolve rather than backing out immediately. For golf, five separate practice visits with a stroke followed by quitting are sufficient; five complete nine-hole tournaments are unnecessary. Golf is accessible by taxi during the day.

Fishing completion requires all 18 catches, including junk. The useful targeting list is:

• Day: Great White Shark 50–60 m; Thread-sail Filefish 30–100 m.
• Night: Prawn 0–10 m; Squid 50–80 m.
• Sunset: Conger Eel 0–20 m; Flounder 30–60 m.
• Day or sunset: Sea Bream 70–90 m; Coelacanth 140–150 m.
• Day or night: Japanese Huchen 30–40 m; Goby 30–60 m.
• Sunset or night: Giant Oarfish 130–140 m; Marlin 120–150 m.
• Any time: Devil Scorpionfish 20–90 m; Steel Drum 30–90 m; Briefcase 20–140 m; Umbrella 40–150 m; Giant Crab 100–150 m; Tuna 130–150 m.

Choose bait whose distance window reaches the target. Matching distance and time narrows the possibilities but does not guarantee a species. Re-enter fishing to refresh the available targets. During the fight, follow the fish’s direction with the rod, reel while tension is manageable, and ease off before the line reaches either extreme.

Golf completion requires a tournament result of −5 or better over nine holes. Practice the swing’s power and impact inputs separately. Read the wind relative to the golfer’s current facing, leave room for the ball to roll after landing, and aim for safe fairway positions rather than carrying every hazard at maximum range. On the green, account for slope instead of treating the distance marker as the entire putt.

Five under is easier to plan as several reliable birdies and safe pars than as a demand for a spectacular shot on every hole. If your approach regularly rolls through the green, adjust its landing point and spin before blaming the putting.

THE GAMBLING ROUTE

Dragon Palace has the four Japanese gambling games and a casino. Fukuma Casino in Purgatory provides the higher-stakes casino options. Novice Gambler requires playing Cee-lo, Cho-han, Koi-koi, and Oicho-kabu. Casino Rookie requires Baccarat, Blackjack, Poker, and Roulette. Play a resolved round and leave normally rather than assuming opening a table is sufficient.

For in-game completion, the targets are:

• Baccarat: 20,000 chips won.
• Blackjack: 10,000 chips won in one session.
• Poker: 10,000 chips won in one session.
• Roulette: 20,000 chips won cumulatively.
• Cee-lo: 20,000 tags won.
• Cho-han: 20,000 tags won.
• Koi-koi: 10,000 tags won.
• Oicho-kabu: 10,000 tags won.

Buying currency does not replace winning the relevant completion target. Blackjack and Poker are particularly easy to misread: the target counts winnings during that sitting, not a single giant hand, and losses do not subtract from that running winnings count. Haruka’s requests instead ask for a specified net increase when you finish the session, so track those separately.

Save before using a scarce cheat item. These are consumable in-game items, not external cheats. Bigger stakes make a useful item go further, but keep enough currency to remain at the table and finish normally.

Baccarat is mostly choosing whether Banker, Player, or a tie will win. Card-drawing decisions are automatic. Banker’s Piece and Player’s Piece help the corresponding side; bet on the side matching the item. Tie bets have large payouts because they are much less likely. I would not treat a losing streak as evidence that a tie is now due.

Blackjack has two useful items with different behavior. Blackjack Amulet produces blackjack hands for five deals. Bust Amulet only forces a bust if the dealer has to draw; it does not prevent the dealer from standing on a strong opening hand. Do not bust your own hand while expecting the amulet to rescue it. Use the higher-stakes table when available and watch the betting limit increase rather than spending your best item on tiny bets.

Poker is Texas Hold’em. Fold poor hands rather than paying to see every river. Royal Joker Card affects the next community-card reveal, so use it when that card can complete a strong hand for you. Improving the whole board can also improve your opponents’ hands. Even a huge hand earns little if everyone folds, so the item is not a guaranteed 10,000-chip button.

Roulette’s Zero Jewel restricts the next result to 0 or 00. Betting on one gives a chance at the large straight-up payout; splitting between them trades payout for certainty. With a 1,000-chip straight-up bet, the winning result is enough for the 20,000 target. Red and Black Jewels restrict the next spin to their color, not to one particular number. Save before committing the jewel if you plan to reload an unsuccessful single-number bet.

Cee-lo is strongest when you exploit the banker turn, because you can collect from several opponents. The 1-1-1 Card, Trips Yokan, 1-2-3 Gum, and Piss Mountain Stone manipulate different rolls. Use the appropriate prompt while rolling, and leave/re-enter before expecting to use another item in a fresh game. Watch the bank and bets: a wonderful roll against tiny wagers still produces a tiny return.

Cho-han starts with even/odd bets and opens larger wagers and extra betting options as you keep playing. Leave and re-enter periodically to refresh the available stake ceiling. Even Goro’s Beads guarantee an even next roll. A Lopsided Cigarette changes how the other players distribute their bets; it does not guarantee the less popular side wins. Save the reliable outcome item for a worthwhile wager.

Koi-koi has no cheat item here. Match the month/plant, collect scoring combinations, and examine what the opponent is collecting too. Moon Viewing and Cherry Blossom Viewing are efficient two-card routes involving the sake cup. Calling koi continues the round and risks losing your current opportunity if the opponent scores first. When protecting a lead, taking the points can be better than chasing one more combination. Short three-round games make the overall result easier to manage.

Oicho-kabu also has no cheat item. Your score is the final digit of the card total, with nine the ordinary target. A high-looking sum is not automatically good: 18 counts as eight, while 20 counts as zero. Learn the special hands and remember the dealer wins ties. Keep playing to unlock larger betting levels, then work toward the cumulative winnings target instead of expecting one lucky round to finish everything.

PACHINKO, ON PS4 AND XBOX CONSOLES

At Volcanic Volcano, Way of the Pachinko King requires obtaining the trophy prize, priced at 500 balls in the remaster. Full minigame completion is tougher: finish a play 5,000 balls ahead of where you started.

Save before using a Get-Rich-Quick Card. It guarantees the first slot spin becomes a jackpot, but you still need to launch balls successfully and collect the payout. Adjust launch strength to feed the opening beneath the display. Stop wasting balls while an animation is resolving, then resume when the jackpot payout rounds begin.

Do not leave immediately because the screen celebrates a jackpot. Wait until you have actually collected enough balls. For the trophy, save after earning the balls and before purchasing the prize. Xbox players have reported the achievement failing to trigger on the first purchase; that backup lets you reload and buy it again without repeating the entire win.

RESTAURANTS: COVER THE MENUS THAT ARE EASY TO MISS

text:
Keep on trusting your book of war—a book made for men of war, which treats women and children as spoils of war, and which describes paradise as a post-war respite filled with virgins and wine; a paradise tailored to the tastes of men of war from the year 570 AD.

That’s your problem.

Start here.

A war-band can take a peninsula and still not own its own story. Muhammad died in Medina in June 632. Within a generation his men were not reciting one fixed text. According to the Sunni canon itself—Sahih al-Bukhari 4987 and 5102—Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, campaigning in Armenia and Azerbaijan under the third caliph, Uthman ibn Affan (r. 644–656), heard Syrian and Iraqi soldiers accusing one another over variant readings of the Qur’an and feared schism. Uthman ordered Zayd ibn Thabit and a small committee to produce one official recension from the sheets already gathered under Abu Bakr after the battle of Yamamah (c. 632–633), sent copies to the main garrison cities, and commanded that other written collections be burned. That is not how a father handles truth. That is how a commander handles a riot in camp. The man of the raid had offered fighting men what fighting men already priced—women, spoil, rank, a paradise with the smell of victory on it—and he got his army: Hijrah 622, Badr 624, the taking of Mecca in 630, a community armed enough that, after 632, it walked out of Arabia and broke the near frontiers of Byzantium and Ctesiphon. He did not get control of the wording. The sword can gather a host. It cannot keep ten mouths from rewriting the banner. When the banner starts a fight, the caliph does not repent. He lights a fire under the other pages (Bukhari 4987).

That is the method. Feed the pack. Win the ground. When the story cracks, burn the variants. A hunter plates the hunger. He does not remake it.

Now the other table.

The gospel is still the worst product in the shop. No one designing customers writes it. Someone who wants sons writes it. Soft men swollen with appetite will always walk to the louder stall. That walk is not evidence. It is the x-ray. And it leaves Jesus where He stands: above the stall, the legion, and every cheap replacement—worthy, because He refused to purchase us with our vice. He paid in blood.

God is not recruiting buyers. He is calling children home.

Jesus does not bait Jew or Greek with their favorite dish. He orders both to drop the plate.

The Jew wanted a war-crown: Rome thrown off, Zion armed, a Messiah who wins like Caesar. Jesus answers with timber and nails, under Pontius Pilate, c. 30–33. “My kingdom is not of this world” (John 18:36). Come back to the Father. Receive a name. “To all who received Him, He gave the right to become children of God” (John 1:12).

The Gentile wanted the old night: the body as shrine, the feast that never closes, the rot Paul names in the streets around the churches (Romans 1; 1 Corinthians 5–6). Jesus answers with a cut. Stop staring. Tear out the eye (Matthew 5:27–32). One covenant bed. Rule the flesh. Then live as a son, not as a stomach.

He does not toss steak to the wolf. He puts bread in a mouth that only knew raw meat—and then dies and rises so the mouth can say Abba. No harem as wages. Adoption. The Lamb dies for the enemy. The stone rolls.

Muhammad runs the opposite shop. He wanted a host and he bought one with the inventory the host already priced: raids for caravan wealth after 622, plural marriage written into law, captives as a lawful yield of war. That raises banners. It does not raise sons of God. And when the inventory of words would not sit still, Uthman, about 650–653, burned the extras. Army first. Canon by bonfire second.

Look at what grows, without perfume. Where Christ’s gospel actually entered—not the costume of Christ, the command of Christ—even under crooked kings, a strange orchard appeared: the weak life counts, the child is not a clan chip only, the woman is not a share of loot, letters and universities sprout because a soul is addressed by God and must learn to answer. Cathedral schools and the medieval universitas—Bologna (1088), Paris (c. 1150), Oxford (c. 1096)—did not grow from a tent of captives. They grew from a Cross and from “let the little children come to Me” (Mark 10:14).

A creed built to please the raider will not pause and see woman and child as the image of God. It will see them as cargo—flesh, hush, wall. Useful falsehood, sanctified war, the killing of the holdout, poverty called fate: that is not bad weather on the map. That is what you plant when desire wears a scabbard.

If truth were the average male wish, heaven would be unemployed. We already know the wish: more body, more force, more alibi. That wish is the clay of this century—in the old paganism that still rides under a prophet’s name, and in the new ideologies that spit on the church. Both want a homemade god. One names it caliphate. One names it State. Both say the vote of man is the verdict of right. That sentence is not faith. It is apostasy with a flag.

The hunter blesses the pulse. The Father breaks it and names it child. That is why the gospel still will not sell to synagogue or forum. And that is why Jesus still has no rival: He would rather lose the crowd than nurse the fever. He lost the crowd. He kept the empty tomb. He kept the way back to the Father.

🇮🇳 Born After His Father’s Kargil Martyrdom, He Turned His Dream Into Reality!

He was born just 45 days after his father, Lance Naik Krishnaji Samrit, was martyred in the 1999 Kargil War.

Years later, Prajwal Samrit fulfilled his father's dream of seeing his son become an Army officer. And he did it after nine SSB attempts, multiple setbacks and two prestigious IIM offers!

🎖️ A Dream He Inherited From His Father

Growing up in Pulgaon tehsil of Maharashtra's Wardha district, Prajwal learnt about the father he never got to meet and his wish to see his son serve in the Indian Army.

After Class 12, he took a year off to prepare for the NDA. He cleared his first SSB but could not qualify in the medical examination.

📚 Eight Setbacks, But No Surrender

Prajwal moved to Pune and enrolled in BSc Electronics at Fergusson College.

What followed were seven more SSB interviews. He cleared the screening round every time but was repeatedly conferenced out.

By his eighth setback, he was close to giving up. His neighbour, Nitin Kothe, a teacher at the Indian Military School in Pulgaon, encouraged him to make one more attempt.

🔥 Two IIM Offers, One Unfinished Dream

Knowing it could be his final opportunity, Prajwal also prepared a strong backup.

He cracked CAT with a 97.51 percentile and secured admission offers from IIM Indore and IIM Kozhikode.

But he still had one dream to fulfil.

On his ninth attempt, he cleared both the SSB and medical examinations and earned his place at the Indian Military Academy (IMA), Dehradun.

He chose the uniform over two prestigious management institute offers.

🫡 From a Kargil Martyr’s Son to an Army Lieutenant

In December 2024, Prajwal completed his training at IMA and was commissioned as a Lieutenant in the Indian Army.

His mother, Savita, who lost her husband in the Kargil War, said:

“My husband wanted to see my elder son become an Army officer. After Kunal couldn’t make it, we had hope in Prajwal. I feel very proud.”

❤️ Nine attempts. Two IIM offers. One dream.

Prajwal's journey is a reminder that setbacks do not have to decide the destination. Sometimes, the dream you refuse to give up becomes the legacy you carry forward.

TRUMP WANTED TO BRING ABOUT REGIME CHANGE IN TEHRAN; THE AMERICANS BROUGHT ABOUT REGIME CHANGE IN WASHINGTON
By @BPartisans 

He wanted to make Tehran tremble. He ended up bringing down his own majority. Donald Trump, the man who promised to make America great again, has just pulled off a remarkable diplomatic feat: losing control of the U.S. Congress by waging war on a country located 10,000 kilometers away from his voters.

The Wall Street Journal describes an electoral rout of spectacular proportions. A Democratic wave swept away Republican certainties, even in their strongholds. Of the roughly 3,000 counties analyzed, only about 170 escaped the Republican setback. A national slap in the face for a president who clearly confused popularity with the applause at his rallies.

And what irony! Trump had promised to end the endless wars. He started a new one, with the enthusiasm of an arsonist convinced he was leading the firefighters. The result: a war without a decisive victory, an Iranian regime still standing, and gas prices that have skyrocketed by 40 percent.

Americans were demanding purchasing power. Trump offered them missiles. They wanted to fill their refrigerators. He offered them a view of the ruins of Iran. Clearly, the average voter still prefers to eat three meals a day rather than finance the White House’s geopolitical fantasies.

The most satisfying part remains the collapse of the man himself. The one who claimed to negotiate better than anyone else is discovering that you can’t run a war like a reality TV show. You can fire an advisor, insult a journalist, threaten an ally. But you can’t fire 300 million Americans just because they refuse to applaud.

And now the Democrats are in control of Congress, with investigative committees on the horizon, accountability demands, and backroom deals that may suddenly come to light.

As for Netanyahu, another key architect of this venture, he, too, is taking stock of the political fallout. Two leaders convinced they were reshaping the Middle East may, in the end, have primarily reshaped their own electoral futures. This is a feat that would almost deserve a medal, if it hadn’t cost so many lives and so much money.

The most troubling question remains: What does a humiliated, narcissistic president, who is still commander-in-chief of the world’s leading military power do? Will he accept his defeat, or will he seek a new show of force to mask the previous one?

For Trump retains considerable power, even without a congressional majority. And a wounded ego can sometimes become more dangerous than an enemy army.

History may well remember this tremendous absurdity: Trump went to war to overthrow Iran’s leaders. Eight months later, it was American voters who overthrew his power in Congress.

In Tehran, the regime is still in power. In Washington, it was Trump’s majority that collapsed.

Receive a name. “To all who received Him, He gave the right to become children of God” (John 1:12).

The Gentile wanted the old night: the body as shrine, the feast that never closes, the rot Paul names in the streets around the churches (Romans 1; 1 Corinthians 5–6). Jesus answers with a cut. Stop staring. Tear out the eye (Matthew 5:27–32). One covenant bed. Rule the flesh. Then live as a son, not as a stomach.

He does not toss steak to the wolf. He puts bread in a mouth that only knew raw meat—and then dies and rises so the mouth can say Abba. No harem as wages. Adoption. The Lamb dies for the enemy. The stone rolls.

Muhammad runs the opposite shop. He wanted a host and he bought one with the inventory the host already priced: raids for caravan wealth after 622, plural marriage written into law, captives as a lawful yield of war. That raises banners. It does not raise sons of God. And when the inventory of words would not sit still, Uthman, about 650–653, burned the extras. Army first. Canon by bonfire second.

Look at what grows, without perfume. Where Christ’s gospel actually entered—not the costume of Christ, the command of Christ—even under crooked kings, a strange orchard appeared: the weak life counts, the child is not a clan chip only, the woman is not a share of loot, letters and universities sprout because a soul is addressed by God and must learn to answer. Cathedral schools and the medieval universitas—Bologna (1088), Paris (c. 1150), Oxford (c. 1096)—did not grow from a tent of captives. They grew from a Cross and from “let the little children come to Me” (Mark 10:14).

A creed built to please the raider will not pause and see woman and child as the image of God. It will see them as cargo—flesh, hush, wall. Useful falsehood, sanctified war, the killing of the holdout, poverty called fate: that is not bad weather on the map. That is what you plant when desire wears a scabbard.

If truth were the average male wish, heaven would be unemployed. We already know the wish: more body, more force, more alibi. That wish is the clay of this century—in the old paganism that still rides under a prophet’s name, and in the new ideologies that spit on the church. Both want a homemade god. One names it caliphate. One names it State. Both say the vote of man is the verdict of right. That sentence is not faith. It is apostasy with a flag.

The hunter blesses the pulse. The Father breaks it and names it child. That is why the gospel still will not sell to synagogue or forum. And that is why Jesus still has no rival: He would rather lose the crowd than nurse the fever. He lost the crowd. He kept the empty tomb. He kept the way back to the Father.

text:
One day in the House of Representatives a bill was taken up appropriating money for the benefit of a widow of a distinguished naval officer. Several beautiful speeches had been made in its support. The speaker was just about to put the question when Crockett arose:

"Mr. Speaker--I have as much respect for the memory of the deceased, and as much sympathy for the suffering of the living, if there be, as any man in this House, but we must not permit our respect for the dead or our sympathy for part of the living to lead us into an act of injustice to the balance of the living. I will not go into an argument to prove that Congress has not the power to appropriate this money as an act of charity. Every member on this floor knows it.

We have the right as individuals, to give away as much of our own money as we please in charity; but as members of Congress we have no right to appropriate a dollar of the public money. Some eloquent appeals have been made to us upon the ground that it is a debt due the deceased. Mr. Speaker, the deceased lived long after the close of the war; he was in office to the day of his death, and I ever heard that the government was in arrears to him.

"Every man in this House knows it is not a debt. We cannot without the grossest corruption, appropriate this money as the payment of a debt. We have not the semblance of authority to appropriate it as charity. Mr. Speaker, I have said we have the right to give as much money of our own as we please. I am the poorest man on this floor. I cannot vote for this bill, but I will give one week's pay to the object, and if every member of Congress will do the same, it will amount to more than the bill asks."

He took his seat. Nobody replied. The bill was put upon its passage, and, instead of passing unanimously, as was generally supposed, and as, no doubt, it would, but for that speech, it received but few votes, and, of course, was lost.

Later, when asked by a friend why he had opposed the appropriation, Crockett gave this explanation:

"Several years ago I was one evening standing on the steps of the Capitol with some members of Congress, when our attention was attracted by a great light over in Georgetown. It was evidently a large fire. We jumped into a hack and drove over as fast as we could. In spite of all that could be done, many houses were burned and many families made houseless, and besides, some of them had lost all but the clothes they had on. The weather was very cold, and when I saw so many children suffering, I felt that something ought to be done for them. The next morning a bill was introduced appropriating $20,000 for their relief. We put aside all other business and rushed it through as soon as it could be done.

"The next summer, when it began to be time to think about election, I concluded I would take a scout around among the boys of my district. I had no opposition there but, as the election was some time off, I did not know what might turn up. When riding one day in a part of my district in which I was more of a stranger than any other, I saw a man in a field plowing and coming toward the road. I gauged my gait so that we should meet as he came up, I spoke to the man. He replied politely, but as I thought, rather coldly.

"I began: 'Well friend, I am one of those unfortunate beings called candidates and---

"Yes I know you; you are Colonel Crockett. I have seen you once before, and voted for you the last time you were elected. I suppose you are out electioneering now, but you had better not waste your time or mine, I shall not vote for you again."

"This was a sockdolger...I begged him tell me what was the matter.

"Well Colonel, it is hardly worthwhile to waste time or words upon it. I do not see how it can be mended, but you gave a vote last winter which shows that either you have not capacity to understand the Constitution, or that you are wanting in the honesty and firmness to be guided by it. In either case you are not the man to represent me. But I beg your pardon for expressing it that way. I did not intend to avail myself of the privilege of the constituent to speak plainly to a candidate for the purpose of insulting you or wounding you.'

"I intend by it only to say that your understanding of the constitution is very different from mine; and I will say to you what but for my rudeness, I should not have said, that I believe you to be honest.

But an understanding of the constitution different from mine I cannot overlook, because the Constitution, to be worth anything, must be held sacred, and rigidly observed in all its provisions. The man who wields power and misinterprets it is the more dangerous the honest he is.'

" 'I admit the truth of all you say, but there must be some mistake. Though I live in the backwoods and seldom go from home, I take the papers from Washington and read very carefully all the proceedings of Congress. My papers say you voted for a bill to appropriate $20,000 to some sufferers by fire in Georgetown. Is that true?

"Well my friend; I may as well own up. You have got me there. But certainly nobody will complain that a great and rich country like ours should give the insignificant sum of $20,000 to relieve its suffering women and children, particularly with a full and overflowing treasury, and I am sure, if you had been there, you would have done just the same as I did.'

"It is not the amount, Colonel, that I complain of; it is the principle. In the first place, the government ought to have in the Treasury no more than enough for its legitimate purposes. But that has nothing with the question. The power of collecting and disbursing money at pleasure is the most dangerous power that can be entrusted to man, particularly under our system of collecting revenue by a tariff, which reaches every man in the country, no matter how poor he may be, and the poorer he is the more he pays in proportion to his means.

What is worse, it presses upon him without his knowledge where the weight centers, for there is not a man in the United States who can ever guess how much he pays to the government. So you see, that while you are contributing to relieve one, you are drawing it from thousands who are even worse off than he.

If you had the right to give anything, the amount was simply a matter of discretion with you, and you had as much right to give $20,000,000 as $20,000. If you have the right to give at all; and as the Constitution neither defines charity nor stipulates the amount, you are at liberty to give to any and everything which you may believe, or profess to believe, is a charity and to any amount you may think proper. You will very easily perceive what a wide door this would open for fraud and corruption and favoritism, on the one hand, and for robbing the people on the other. 'No, Colonel, Congress has no right to give charity.'

"'Individual members may give as much of their own money as they please, but they have no right to touch a dollar of the public money for that purpose. If twice as many houses had been burned in this country as in Georgetown, neither you nor any other member of Congress would have Thought of appropriating a dollar for our relief. There are about two hundred and forty members of Congress. If they had shown their sympathy for the sufferers by contributing each one week's pay, it would have made over $13,000. There are plenty of wealthy men around Washington who could have given $20,000 without depriving themselves of even a luxury of life.'

"The congressmen chose to keep their own money, which, if reports be true, some of them spend not very creditably; and the people about Washington, no doubt, applauded you for relieving them from necessity of giving what was not yours to give. The people have delegated to Congress, by the Constitution, the power to do certain things. To do these, it is authorized to collect and pay moneys, and for nothing else. Everything beyond this is usurpation, and a violation of the Constitution.'

"'So you see, Colonel, you have violated the Constitution in what I consider a vital point. It is a precedent fraught with danger to the country, for when Congress once begins to stretch its power beyond the limits of the Constitution, there is no limit to it, and no security for the people. I have no doubt you acted honestly, but that does not make it any better, except as far as you are personally concerned, and you see that I cannot vote for you.'

"I tell you I felt streaked. I saw if I should have opposition, and this man should go to talking and in that district I was a gone fawn-skin. I could not answer him, and the fact is, I was so fully convinced that he was right, I did not want to. But I must satisfy him, and I said to him:

"Well, my friend, you hit the nail upon the head when you said I had not sense enough to understand the Constitution. I intended to be guided by it, and thought I had studied it fully. I have heard many speeches in Congress about the powers of Congress, but what you have said here at your plow has got more hard, sound sense in it than all the fine speeches I ever heard. If I had ever taken the view of it that you have, I would have put my head into the fire before I would have given that vote; and if you will forgive me and vote for me again, if I ever vote for another unconstitutional law I wish I may be shot.'

"He laughingly replied; 'Yes, Colonel, you have sworn to that once before, but I will trust you again upon one condition. You are convinced that your vote was wrong. Your acknowledgment of it will do more good than beating you for it. If, as you go around the district, you will tell people about this vote, and that you are satisfied it was wrong, I will not only vote for you, but will do what I can to keep down opposition, and perhaps, I may exert some little influence in that way.'

"If I don't, said I, 'I wish I may be shot; and to convince you that I am in ernest in what I say I will come back this way in a week or ten days, and if you will get up a gathering of people, I will make a speech to them. Get up a barbecue, and I will pay for it.'

"No, Colonel, we are not rich people in this section but we have plenty of provisions to contribute for a barbecue, and some to spare for those who have none. The push of crops will be over in a few days, and we can then afford a day for a barbecue. 'This Thursday; I will see to getting it up on Saturday week. Come to my house on Friday, and we will go together, and I promise you a very respectable crowd to see and hear you.

"'Well I will be here. But one thing more before I say good-bye. I must know your name."

"'My name is Bunce.'

"'Not Horatio Bunce?'

"'Yes

"'Well, Mr. Bunce, I never saw you before, though you say you have seen me, but I know you very well. I am glad I have met you, and very proud that I may hope to have you for my friend.'

"It was one of the luckiest hits of my life that I met him. He mingled but little with the public, but was widely known for his remarkable intelligence, and for a heart brim-full and running over with kindness and benevolence, which showed themselves not only in words but in acts. He was the oracle of the whole country around him, and his fame had extended far beyond the circle of his immediate acquaintance. Though I had never met him, before, I had heard much of him, and but for this meeting it is very likely I should have had opposition, and had been beaten. One thing is very certain, no man could now stand up in that district under such a vote.

"At the appointed time I was at his house, having told our conversation to every crowd I had met, and to every man I stayed all night with, and I found that it gave the people an interest and confidence in me stronger than I had ever seen manifested before.

"Though I was considerably fatigued when I reached his house, and, under ordinary circumstances, should have gone early to bed, I kept him up until midnight talking about the principles and affairs of government, and got more real, true knowledge of them than I had got all my life before."

"I have known and seen much of him since, for I respect him - no, that is not the word - I reverence and love him more than any living man, and I go to see him two or three times every year; and I will tell you, sir, if every one who professes to be a Christian lived and acted and enjoyed it as he does, the religion of Christ would take the world by storm.

"But to return to my story. The next morning we went to the barbecue and, to my surprise, found about a thousand men there. I met a good many whom I had not known before, and they and my friend introduced me around until I had got pretty well acquainted - at least, they all knew me.

"In due time notice was given that I would speak to them. They gathered up around a stand that had been erected. I opened my speech by saying:

"Fellow-citizens - I present myself before you today feeling like a new man. My eyes have lately been opened to truths which ignorance or prejudice or both, had heretofore hidden from my view. I feel that I can today offer you the ability to render you more valuable service than I have ever been able to render before. I am here today more for the purpose of acknowledging my error than to seek your votes. That I should make this acknowledgment is due to myself as well as to you. Whether you will vote for me is a matter for your consideration only."

"I went on to tell them about the fire and my vote for the appropriation and then told them why I was satisfied it was wrong. I closed by saying:

"And now, fellow-citizens, it remains only for me to tell you that the most of the speech you have listened to with so much interest was simply a repetition of the arguments by which your neighbor, Mr. Bunce, convinced me of my error.

"It is the best speech I ever made in my life, but he is entitled to the credit for it. And now I hope he is satisfied with his convert and that he will get up here and tell you so.'

"He came up to the stand and said:

"Fellow-citizens - it affords me great pleasure to comply with the request of Colonel Crockett. I have always considered him a thoroughly honest man, and I am satisfied that he will faithfully perform all that he has promised you today.'

"He went down, and there went up from that crowd such a shout for Davy Crockett as his name never called forth before.'

"I am not much given to tears, but I was taken with a choking then and felt some big drops rolling down my cheeks. And I tell you now that the remembrance of those few words spoken by such a man, and the honest, hearty shout they produced, is worth more to me than all the honors I have received and all the reputation I have ever made, or ever shall make, as a member of Congress.'

"Now, sir," concluded Crockett, "you know why I made that speech yesterday. "There is one thing which I will call your attention, "you remember that I proposed to give a week's pay. There are in that House many very wealthy men - men who think nothing of spending a week's pay, or a dozen of them, for a dinner or a wine party when they have something to accomplish by it. Some of those same men made beautiful speeches upon the great debt of gratitude which the country owed the deceased--a debt which could not be paid by money--and the insignificance and worthlessness of money, particularly so insignificant a sum as $20,000 when weighed against the honor of the nation. Yet not one of them responded to my proposition. Money with them is nothing but trash when it is to come out of the people. But it is the one great thing for which most of them are striving, and many of them sacrifice honor, integrity, and justice to obtain it."

The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has condemned what it described as a sustained, coordinated and state-sponsored assault on democracy, freedom of association and the constitutional right of Nigerians to political participation under the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

The Council said the unfolding incidents across the country went beyond ordinary political rivalry, alleging that they represented a disturbing pattern of intimidation, harassment and suppression of opposition voices.

These are calculated atrocious actions skewed to scare Nigerians ahead of the general elections.

In a statement signed by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC recalled a series of incidents, including attacks on its leaders and members in Kaduna, the reported assault on its Sokoto State governorship candidate, Alhaji Munir Dan Iya, by operatives of the Sokoto Marshals along Airport Road, Sokoto, and alleged attacks on other opposition figures.

It also cited the reported demolition of its governorship campaign office in Kebbi State and the alleged denial of a campaign venue in Enugu State to the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi.

The Council further referenced the reported attacks on the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, and other opposition voices, describing the incidents as part of what it called an emerging pattern of political intolerance.

According to the ADC-PCC, the alleged attacks, denial of campaign venues, arrests, harassment and intimidation of opposition figures raise serious concerns about the state of democratic freedoms and political pluralism in Nigeria.

The Council maintained that no government, regardless of its political or institutional strength, could successfully suppress the democratic aspirations of Nigerians, recalling that popular resistance contributed to the collapse of former President Olusegun Obasanjo's third-term agenda.

It also argued that President Tinubu and the APC enjoyed the benefits of political participation and opposition politics when they were outside government, insisting that those same democratic freedoms must be guaranteed to all political parties and their members.

The ADC-PCC expressed concern over the continued detention of its Vice Chairman and former Governor of Kaduna State, Mallam Nasir El-Rufai, alleging that he was being unlawfully held and denied his right to bail.

It warned that the circumstances surrounding his detention would not weaken the party, adding that the international community was watching developments in Nigeria.

"The world is watching, and the burden of this illegality rests squarely on those responsible," the Council stated.

The campaign council further alleged that financial inducements were being deployed to compromise individuals and weaken opposition ranks, but insisted that Nigerians would not surrender their constitutional rights for monetary or material benefits.

"President Tinubu is at liberty to corruptly buy a few consciences with money and material inducements. Millions of Naira are being offered to weak individuals to mortgage their rights, but not all Nigerians are for sale," the statement declared.

The ADC-PCC called on Nigerians to remain committed to defending democratic values, freedom of association and the right to political choice, regardless of political affiliation.
Reaffirming its commitment to its political mission, the Council declared that the ADC was determined to provide an alternative political platform and contribute to what it described as the rescue of the country.

"The ADC has come to rescue this country.
"This too shall pass. Nigeria will endure and democracy will prevail," the statement concluded

Signed:
Kola Ologbondiyan
Director, Media and Publicity
ADC Presidential Campaign Council

LAW ON CALL

Innovative, Affordable Law Firm Arrives in Washington State

Nov. 5, 2026

SPOKANE, Wash., Nov. 5, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Law on Call is expanding its practice into Washington, becoming the first entirely nonlawyer-owned law firm to operate in three U.S. states. Since launching in 2021, the firm has removed the most frustrating aspects of hiring a lawyer: long wait times, large retainer fees, excessive billable hours. Recently approved to operate in Washington by the state Supreme Court, Law on Call also practices in Arizona and Utah.

Law on Call is a licensed law firm that gives clients unlimited access to attorney advice, with optional legal work added at discounted rates. As a law firm owned entirely by nonlawyers, it only operates in states that have opened their rules to new ownership models. Its expansion into Washington brings a proven, affordable alternative to traditional legal services for small businesses and people who have often gone without help.

"Law on Call's expansion mirrors my own move to the Pacific Northwest as a young attorney,” said Law on Call attorney Andrew Olmsted. "We were in the middle of a global financial crisis. People were getting laid off and losing homes, small business owners were getting taken advantage of. There was a need for legal services, but people couldn't afford them. Today, things aren’t so different. Except now, we offer an alternative.”

As part of the Washington State Bar Association (WSBA) Entity Regulation Pilot Project, Law on Call is eager to bring its affordable and accessible legal services to the West Coast. The goal has always been simple: to get more people the legal help they need quickly, easily, and at a price they can afford.

"Sadly, it doesn’t really feel like we’ve made a lot of progress [toward access to justice],” says WSBA Executive Director Terra Nevitt. "I see technology and different business models as things that we need to be curious about, because they might be the innovations we need to really make progress.”

The WSBA will collect data to evaluate the success of the Pilot Project and entities operating within the program. The pilot is scheduled to run for at least 10 years (tentatively until in 2036), and more permanent solutions may follow.

"The outdated U.S. legal system doesn’t change before consumers demand it does,” added Olmsted. "Law on Call’s approval in Washington is a market disruptor.”

***

About Law on Call

Law on Call is reinventing the traditional approach to legal services in the United States. The client-centered and nonlawyer-owned law firm focuses on keeping costs low while providing fast turnarounds, client satisfaction, and high quality of work.

text:
On August 5, 2009, a Florida woman came home from the gym to police tape and was told her husband had been murdered.

He hadn't been. The street was a staged crime scene, and a television crew was filming.

Her name was Dalia Dippolito. Five days earlier, her former lover, Mohamed Shihadeh, had gone to Boynton Beach police and said she wanted her husband killed.

Police made him a confidential informant. He set up a meeting at a gas station, with a hidden camera in his car.

Two days later, in a CVS parking lot, she met the "hitman," an undercover detective named Widy Jean. She offered him $7,000 to kill her husband in a staged burglary. He asked if she was sure.

"5,000% sure."

She agreed to leave for the gym at 6 a.m. that Wednesday, with Michael home in bed.

Instead, police woke him, told him what was happening, and moved him out of the house.

In the video below, the recordings and the staged scene play back, including the moment she is shown the "hitman" in an interrogation room.

"I've never seen him before."

Then her husband walked in. She was arrested.

"I didn't do anything."

Her lawyers argued the recordings were written for TV. She testified that she, her husband and Shihadeh had been making a video to pitch a reality show. Michael Dippolito and Shihadeh denied it.

In 2011, a jury convicted her and she was sentenced to 20 years. In 2014, an appeals court threw out the conviction over an error in jury selection. The 2016 retrial ended in a hung jury.

In June 2017, a third jury convicted her. This one took about 90 minutes. She was sentenced to 16 years.

🔎🐍 Some may ask, “Why spend so much time studying Theosophy, the New Age movement, the NAR Movement, and QAnon?”

Well, if you don’t study the ideologies you’re confronting, how can you recognize their influence, understand their objectives, or discern when their teachings begin creeping into Christianity?

⚠️ Why does Theosophy matter? Why should Christians care about the New Age movement?

Because lies are often more convincing when they’re mixed with truth. We see that very tactic in Genesis 3, when the serpent questioned God’s Word and offered Eve the promise of greater knowledge.

🧠 Here’s a prime example of what is called the “next man up” mentality, associated with Theosophical teachings about humanity’s spiritual evolution.

We’re seeing narratives encouraging Americans to rise up, fight evil, reclaim their country, and free themselves from those supposedly “controlling,” “manipulating,” and even “stealing their loosh.” That last term, in particular, circulates in modern esoteric and conspiracy communities.

👁️ And here’s where things get interesting.

Some of these ideas are being wrapped in patriotism, Christianity, and the promise of a coming “Great Awakening.” What appears to be a battle between good and evil may also carry philosophical and spiritual assumptions that Christians should carefully examine.

🚨 I believe the “Great Awakening” narrative deserves serious scrutiny because of its similarities to New Age teachings about spiritual transformation and collective enlightenment. Just take a look at the great awakening map and you will see the fullness of “The Plan.” Anyone pushing that information is now the “next man up.”

🇺🇸 That brings me to General Michael Flynn.

Flynn has been associated with political movements promoting a national awakening, including the ReAwaken America Tour. His public appearances and rhetoric raise questions about the spiritual influences surrounding these movements.

📖 One particularly interesting example occurred when Flynn spoke at Pastor Hank Kunneman’s Lord of Hosts Church in Omaha, Nebraska. A church that supports the NAR movement.

During that appearance, Flynn delivered a prayer containing references to “sevenfold rays” and “legions.” The language drew attention because of its similarities to a prayer associated with famous New Age teacher Elizabeth Clare Prophet, whose teachings incorporated esoteric ideas and claimed spiritual communications involving Archangel Michael.

The language of spiritual rays also appears in the writings of Alice Bailey, whose work promoted the externalization of a spiritual hierarchy and a coming transformation of humanity.

🤔 Now, does similar language automatically prove that everyone involved is knowingly advancing the same spiritual agenda? No. But should Christians examine those similarities and their historical origins? Absolutely.

This is why I keep researching Theosophy, New Age spirituality, and their intersections with modern political and religious movements.

✝️ From my biblical perspective, there’s a serious danger in assuming that every movement promising to defeat evil is automatically aligned with Jesus Christ.

📜 I also believe these developments deserve examination alongside Revelation 17 and its imagery of the harlot and the beast. That’s my prophetic interpretation, not something I claim has been conclusively established.

🐍 Deception doesn’t always present itself as darkness. Sometimes it presents itself as enlightenment, liberation, patriotism, or even a spiritual awakening. Satan likes to mask as the “good” guy. Don’t be fooled.

And that’s precisely why discernment matters.

I’m not interested in concern trolling or endless arguments that distract from the material. I’m asking people to examine the teachings, study the historical sources, and compare what they’re hearing with Scripture.

🔥 The message is simple: Don’t confuse a promised Great Awakening with the truth of Jesus Christ.

Have a blessed day, everyone. Much love, and God bless! ✝️

text:
5 scouting takeaways from Ohio State-BYU:

1) Amare Bynum looked outstanding.

At 6'8, 245 pounds, he has a great combination of length, strength and quickness. He got to the rim easily, finished well and added 2 blocks.

He has a real NBA 4 frame. If the jumper comes along this year, I think there’s starter upside. He's T20 on my board right now. 

2) Robert Wright III was the best player on the floor.

He consistently blew by defenders, hit difficult 3s and passed well.

At 6'1, 183 pounds, the NBA questions are obvious. He’ll be small defensively and doesn’t add much rebounding or event creation.

But the offense is good enough that I can see a backup point guard pathway.

3) Bruce Branch III is still No. 2 on my board.

The 3-ball didn’t fall, but he scored well inside the arc, passed well and was a plus defensively.

His 7'1+ wingspan gives him a huge margin for error. Even when a defender gets by him, he can still recover and make a play.

I still see a second-side creator, floor spacer and plus defender who projects comfortably as a good NBA starter.

4) Anthony Thompson was basically invisible.

He entered the year as a top-10 prospect for me, but went scoreless from the field, missed all 4 of his 3s and didn’t make much of a defensive impact either.

One bad game doesn’t change my grade, but I need to see much more activity when the shot isn’t falling.

5) Both teams looked much better offensively than defensively.

There were too many easy straight-line drives on both sides.

BYU’s rim protection was especially concerning. They finished with zero blocks and didn’t offer much resistance once Ohio State got downhill.

NC - has seen rapid increase in population of Charlotte. RDU has seen rapid increase in their suburban population. Western NC has seen increase of left voting population bc of retirees permanently moving to the Mtn towns from areas like ATL. 

GA - absurd population growth of left voting individuals moving from areas like CA/NY/etc. They liked all the great things GA has to offer but voted like they were still in their old states. ATL has seen an explosion in recent years of population growth. And not just ATL proper but mainly in the surrounding suburbs. And there has been rapid expansion of housing development pushing further out than ever before to increase what was previously not considered a suburb but now is. Coastal towns are becoming hot spots like never seen before. Then there are areas in Augusta, LaGrange, Columbus where the population of left voting has naturally increased plus folks moving there during the COVID years from ATL who vote left. And those left voting folks who left ATL were not just replaced 1 for 1 by people moving to GA from other states but by huge margins.

He put it into his own stomach, had an endoscopy done, and showed the development of gastritis and its cure with antibiotics. That is not proof that “the institutions didn’t get it.” It is proof that the hypothesis could be tested. The same applies to anyone who appeals to him: “Marshall was right even though they didn’t believe him” holds only if you leave behind a test that could have failed. Monster group + materials science + software stack + theology + revival offers no such test—only a package that resists testing by being composed of things that legitimize each other.

👏 Which contemporary Irish design projects will matter in fifty years? 👏

The Irish Design Excellence Awards (IDEA) is a new initiative and collaborative creation of the Design & Crafts Council Ireland (DCCI) and the National Museum of Ireland (NMI). It showcases projects nominated by Ireland's leading design organisations and selected for their design excellence, innovation, impact, and cultural and national significance.

IDEA offers a unique snapshot of contemporary Irish creativity and highlights the contribution design makes to Ireland's cultural, social, and economic life.

Shortlisted projects include:

🐎 EquiMetrics and https://t.co/VNWOdz2kDa’s S-PRO, a wearable technology platform designed to give racehorse trainers insights into performance, fitness and recovery. Nominated by IxDA – Interaction and Digital Design.

💧 Arklow Wastewater Treatment Plant, by Clancy Moore Architects. Nominated by the Royal Institute of the Architects of Ireland (RIAI).

🎬 All Ways Home, a short illustrated film by Alan Dunne, released to mark the launch of EIRSAT-1, Ireland’s first space mission. Nominated by Illustrators Ireland.

“With the introduction of the IDEA award, we hope to encourage designers, makers and creatives to continue pushing boundaries, innovate and challenge the world around us.”
– Mary Blanchfield, CEO of Design & Crafts Council Ireland.

“The Museum’s IDEA acquisitions will grow the national collection as a broader expression of human creativity and as a source of inspiration to future designers.”
– Dónal Maguire, Keeper of the Art and Industrial Division at the National Museum of Ireland.

One of my longtime friends and Boise State alumni, Tim Yates, MBA, is the founder of https://t.co/E38xcrvCPR™, a company that helps families across the country prepare their estate planning documents and protect what matters most.

On Tuesday, November 17th, Tim will be hosting a FREE 30-minute educational webinar covering what living trusts are, how they can help families avoid probate, and some important steps you can take to make things easier for the people you love.

The downside I called back in Aug etc. is here now...
(by the way, my Sunday post predicted the up into Wed and down into Thu)

I remain selectively constructive on equities into EoY, with $SPX confirmation still pending...
The structure I laid out last week still holds. 7700 is the center of the defended book into Nov 20, and the real change toward exposure to rising prices with rising vol only begins above 7723. 
Acceptance above that, and then above the 7919 upside pivot, would open the 8052–8185 zone, that is my 8000 case. 
A pullback into the 7615–7640 brake zone, which is the centroid of the EoY book, still works as long as 7550 holds, bcs that is the strongest brake and the swing low anchoring the zone. 
Losing 7550 would shift my attention to 7443, the lower edge of the positive November payoff, and below that the thesis changes, sustained acceptance below 7371 with failed recoveries makes a bear regime my working assumption, and staying below 7267 proves it by breaking the June base... all of this I wrote few days ago about the levels, linked below in comment... 
The Dow holding up better through rotation adds support while it stays above its 50,906 reaction low.
Pessimistic sentiment helps, bcs of put decay later, and seasonality favors the bulls, although I give it less weight because the post-midterm stimulus was spent pre-vote.

FCIs keep easing with equities higher and bonds bid, helped by the softer USD.
Even a sideways tape can deliver earnings-led multiple compression while leaving household wealth broadly intact.
Credit and money growth still support demand, while USD weakness adds imported inflation to existing supply pressure. With nominal growth firm and inflation sticky, further upside reinforces my view that 3.75–4% is already too loose. The curve prices a hike for December and about 3 by next September, and on my read that is still too few...
So the Fed will be forced to hike even more, and later even higher than expected, when oil shock is there...

With the $5,000 rebate tied to a GOP win gone, the remaining economic momentum comes from committed spending and liquidity mechanics.
The datacenter projects already breaking ground keep capex flowing even as build-out returns look more questionable, while slower approvals can shift projects across states or push spending further out.
Treasury cash running down into EoY adds liquidity too. I’d therefore look for financing to deteriorate alongside weaker earnings and demand before calling an immediate post-election contraction.

Equities can absorb growth-led yield upside while earnings keep up, whereas a higher term premium is more damaging because funding costs rise without a matching cash-flow upgrade. If bonds are bid while equities are offered, I’d become more concerned about the growth outlook, and that is exactly the copper-and-yields-down signal I flagged in Oct. The transition I’m watching is funding costs outrunning earnings, followed by weaker credit creation and a reversal of the wealth effect. The rally delays that adjustment while feeding the inflation that brings it closer.
The Dow still has the strongest completed breakout, and I’m watching for gold and $BTC follow-through alongside an SPX breakout.
$GLD Gold’s bounce is constructive, but gold has not hedged equities this year and I treat its trough as a function of peak hawkishness, so a confirmed reversal needs the hike path to top out first, ideally with silver confirming. Until then it is a bounce, not a bottom. BTC trades on the same liquidity read, a bottom there needs the resistance above the recent range to clear, and losing the recent lows reopens the downside. Levels for both are in my Oct 15 note.

text:
HERE WE GO...

Voilà, Kenny G just said what I’ve been seeing for the past 20 months.
He said the AI selloff is people doing research. I had called out the inflated tech bubble in my July 2025 post and argued for selling into strength on 6 January 2026. 
GPUs are like airline seats, where overcapacity means free-falling marginal prices and another dark-fiber cycle. 
Nobody can defend year 7 of a chip, and Corporate America is auditing its AI bills. 
In my January post I attributed the dotcom collapse to overbuilding rather than startups, discussed stretched depreciation and writedowns, and described the hype as marketing for lenders. I extended that argument to $TSMC oversupply and $NVDA’s non-cancellable obligations in my 20 March post...
Deleveraging is the lazy answer, which fits my March argument to trade the chart, not the bias. Fast money frontruns a troubled fund. 
I wrote about insiders flushing the AI names in February 2025 and the liquidity premium that would rise sharply the following January.
He also says the Reps lose a chamber and the Iran war is unpopular. I wrote about the market being held up to win the midterm at any cost since last year, and forecast oil above $95 for years in February 2026. 
His tariffs are pro-inflation claim, consistent with my March 2025 stagflation call, also his discussion of the debt burden, crowding out, the 30y and mortgage rates echoes my May and June 2025 posts on bills as hidden QE, the Bessent put and the bond market about to crack, that I called beforehand... 
If Washington doesn't listen, inflation, a weaker dollar and a falling standard of living follow. 
In my 20 March post this year, I argued that inflating the debt away was the policy...

What he could not/wasn't allow to say is that the flow his firm intermediates is the engine. 
Dealer hedging accounts for most trading, as I wrote in that March post. 
Research sets the direction, while positioning sets the shape of the distribution. 
That is why there is no bear market tomorrow. As I explained in my 27 of Oct post, customers are hedged for the crash and naked for the grind. 
A crash needs uninsured forced sellers, and the forced selling of this cycle gets absorbed and reversed through the process Griffin and me described. 
The move remains a grind until the absorbing balance sheets are exhausted.

The midterm matters because the bid was a policy product. Very important, and thats why I wrote a lot of articles about the political game thats going on.
Bill-tilted issuance, GSE mortgage buying and a buyback window that closes the day after the vote were all built to carry the market through election day. 
The textbook says the year after a midterm is the strong one, but that rule depends on stimulus coming after the vote. Here the stimulus was spent before it and the Fed’s next move is a hike, so the rule is inverted. The put expires with the vote, and the transition is political first, financial after.

The real AI problem is demand, as I wrote since last year autumn, and more in details in my 6 January post. 
Most of the demand is the buildout buying from itself, while end users adopt slowly and not without limit. 
When packaging, memory and the grid catch up, the shortage flips to surplus and the pricing power that justified the useful-life accounting is gone. 
Regulation, energy constraints, privacy concerns and psychological harms then eliminate most of the flashy applications. Because it is debt-financed with non-cancellable obligations, the writedown is a credit event, not an equity event, the argument I made on 20 March. 
That is why a cut will not save it. 
The cuts of 2001 and 2008 saved nothing when demand collapsed.

My March posts on Iran and the First Island Chain explain why the energy shock is structural. 
Iran means years of destabilization, and the First Island Chain is the next lever (that is already happening slowly, chinese-mode, with the administrative blockade already being built). 
The East’s only weapon is the hypersensitivity and divisions of the Western people, so the cost base gets repriced whenever it needs to be. 
Repeated pricelevel shocks mean inflation, trapping the Fed between cuts that reignite it and holding rates while the debt arithmetic runs. 
Higher yields are guaranteed, and the Bessent put only slows them. First comes debt deflation in 2028 to 2030, with the spiral bottoming at pre-COVID levels. 
Then comes the inflationary policy response, Griffin’s warning and my base case.

As I said in January, I think green energy will be the next bubble because the capital that leaves AI needs another investment story, and the AI buildout itself created the energy problem it now has to solve. 
Europe already pivoted behind its regulatory wall, and the subsidies are there. 
Griffin’s own list, fusion, fission, batteries and robotics, lays out the next narrative I discussed in my January post. 
I will be a cautious investor there, not a believer.

Also I argued in the same posts, that this system cannot address geopolitical realignment, population aging, inequality, climate change and the extraction of value by crossborder capital networks at the same time. 
When a market society overruns itself, society re-embeds the economy. The form of that re-embedding is the open question.
My guess is distributism. The new marketplace is being built in the Middle East, tokenized, with trade monitored and controlled, by pragmatic religious-nationalist monarchies inside the US, Russia and Gulf alliance I described as Holy Alliance 2.0 in March 2025. At least on a level of plan... bcs things are being messed up by the british royals and globalists big capitalists... thats why Trump was attacking UK and Canada hard... I explained it many times.
As I wrote this March, that alliance demands sovereign national economic models from everyone, and the only model that fits a religious-nationalist world and a democratic one at once, with national priorities, distributed ownership and no state monopoly over goods, is the third way of the social encyclicals, not socialism or the East’s state capitalism. 
The Arabs supply the infrastructure and legitimacy, while the West supplies the distributive form. The transition is slow, but the direction is set.

The realist play is to detach Russia from China through the Gulf and push China out of the economic process. At least, this was the plan since 2017 between Trump and Putin and Tahnoun Bin Zayed. 
I explained this back in March 2025, also with Venezuela as the first chapter and the Board of Peace as the framework. 
The East plays for time and waits for the Western crisis it expects after the midterm, as I wrote in my August 2026 post.
And Putin will choose the winner.

However the problem is that Russia is an imperialist state. Always has been, always will be. Trump has been willing to give Putin things like tech for Shtokman fields, and getting the arctic LNG in reverse, but Putin wants the old soviet territories back, slowly as his herritage. Thats why I said West has a 1938 München moment. 
What I see, and pretty sure about is that peace will come first because Russia wants a fake peace now as I explained in August, with sanctions relief on its terms. 
As I explained in my 6 March post, the promise of peace is the East’s primary weapon and trap. NATO knows it, but it is out of time already. The treaty is a pause for rearmament...
And very importantly: as this East-West conflict roots in ideology (like every conflicts basically), the pope will visit Moscow. That will be the sign. Everybody will talk about peace. But if ortodoxy remains against catholics, then you know, that the escalation will happen pretty fast, north from Carpathians first. It will be fast, short, but devastating.
I expect the Pope to come in, around Q2 to Q3 next year.
The riots you see in Western EU, is a part of the plan coming from Iran, I also called back in spring and you didn't believe me...

So Griffin kinda agrees with me...
The rest, you will see, how accurate I was all along. Be prepared 😉

Alex, you’re absolutely right. The New York GOP burned to the ground, and much of that destruction was self-inflicted.

They placed their hope in voter loyalty, their confidence in political dissatisfaction, and their entire strategy in passivity.

They apparently believed New Yorkers were so frustrated with Democratic leadership that Republicans could simply wait for voters to come running.

That’s not leadership. That’s political indolence masquerading as strategy.

Where was the sustained grassroots organizing? Where was the serious engagement with struggling urban communities? Where was the compelling alternative to decades of Democratic leadership?

I’m from Buffalo, where Democrats have dominated city government for decades, yet educational proficiency, generational poverty, and economic stagnation remain serious problems.

The Republican Party should have been in those neighborhoods every day, listening, organizing, offering solutions, and demonstrating measurable results.

Instead, too often, Republicans treat urban communities as electorally irrelevant and then act astonished when those communities don’t vote for them.

You cannot abandon entire populations, expect their loyalty, and call it a political strategy.

And you certainly cannot build a statewide movement by relying exclusively on people who already agree with you.

Democrats didn’t have to convince every New Yorker that their policies were successful. Republicans needed to convince enough New Yorkers that they offered something better.

They failed.

New York Republicans didn’t simply lose an election. They exposed the consequences of years of political complacency.

And unless that changes, they’ll keep losing while congratulating themselves for winning the geographic map.
