text:
November 5, 1937. Nearly two years before the war, Adolf Hitler gathers his top military and foreign-policy chiefs in Berlin and, behind closed doors, lays out his intention to wage wars of conquest in Europe. A colonel named Hossbach takes notes, and the record he produces, the Hossbach Memorandum, would one day be used at Nuremberg as evidence that the Second World War was not a tragic accident but a plan.

The meeting was supposed to be about something mundane, a squabble over the allocation of steel and raw materials among the armed services. But Hitler turned it into something far larger. For hours he held forth to the assembled leaders, his war and foreign ministers, the heads of the army, navy, and air force, about his vision for Germany's future, and that vision was war. He declared that Germany needed Lebensraum, living space, which could only be won by force, and he laid out a timetable for aggression, aiming to secure Germany's position by around 1943 to 1945 at the latest, with the first targets being Austria and Czechoslovakia, to be seized to strengthen Germany for the greater struggle to come.

It was a chilling preview of exactly what happened. Within months Hitler would annex Austria, and within a year he would take the Sudetenland and then all of Czechoslovakia, precisely the steps he outlined. The Hossbach meeting is one of the clearest windows into his intentions, a moment when he spelled out to his own commanders that he meant to plunge Europe into war for conquest and racial empire.

And it is fascinating partly for the reaction in the room. This was not a gathering of fanatical Nazis nodding along. Several of the professional military men present, and the foreign minister, were alarmed. The war minister, Blomberg, and the army commander, Fritsch, raised objections, warning of the dangers, cautioning that Britain and France might not stand aside, that Germany was not ready, that this course was reckless. These were conservative officers of the old school, willing to rebuild German power but wary of Hitler's headlong rush toward a general war.

Their caution did not save them; it may have doomed them. Within a few months of this meeting, both Blomberg and Fritsch were gone, forced out in scandals, the Blomberg affair over his wife's past and the Fritsch affair on trumped-up charges, and Hitler used the opportunity to purge the conservative military leadership and take ever tighter personal control of the armed forces, replacing doubters with more compliant men. The objections raised at the Hossbach meeting were, in a sense, the last gasp of the old military establishment's independence before Hitler brought the army fully to heel.

Historians argue about exactly how to read the memorandum, whether it was a firm, fixed war plan or more of Hitler thinking aloud, testing his advisers, laying out aspirations that shifted with circumstances. The exact weight of it is debated. But its broad significance is not seriously in doubt: here, in November 1937, Hitler told his own leaders that he intended to wage aggressive war for conquest, named his first victims, and set a rough timetable, and then events followed the blueprint with grim fidelity.

That is why, after the war, the Hossbach Memorandum became a key piece of evidence at the Nuremberg trials, offered by the prosecution as proof that the Nazi leadership had conspired and planned to wage aggressive war, that the catastrophe that killed tens of millions had been, from early on, an intention and a design. The conference on the 5th was one of the signposts on the road to war, the day the plan was spoken aloud in a Berlin room, with the professional soldiers who doubted it soon to be swept aside.

Claude:

[I'll check where the war and any talks stand now before taking the challenge on.]

Challenge accepted. In five minutes I can write a list of the questions an exit strategy has to answer. I can't honestly write the answers, because each one depends on choices only governments can make. That gap is the real rebuttal to JM.

What any exit strategy has to settle:

1What counts as "done".

The administration hasn't held a fixed answer. On March 2 Hegseth set out four goals: preventing an Iranian nuclear weapon, destroying Iran's navy, destroying its ballistic missile arsenal, and destroying its ability to produce more. By late March Trump had listed five objectives. By August, CNN reported that the administration's early hawkish goals had shrunk noticeably as the war ground on, and ranking stable oil prices above denuclearization marked a notable shift in its stated priorities.

2Who signs on Iran's side.

JM says the regime are all liars, yet any exit short of total conquest needs an agreement with that same regime. Arms control has never depended on trust. It depends on inspection and verification, which is exactly what the February offer included through the IAEA.

3Sequencing.

Iran said it won't reopen the Strait of Hormuz unless the United States lifts its blockade and ends the war. Someone has to move first.

4Spoilers.

Israel's fronts, Hezbollah and the Houthis can each wreck a deal.

Saudi Arabia said Iran's Houthi allies carried out another strike at Riyadh's airport during the recent stalled talks.

5Domestic politics.

Democrats swept the House and Senate on Tuesday, giving the party leverage to pressure Trump to end the war.

JM's own points also contradict each other. He says regime change would have wrapped it up, then says Iran has gone the way of Vietnam. Your Mosaic Doctrine post already answers the "couple of SEAL teams" idea: the top tier has been killed and the system keeps firing. Decapitation was the opening move, not an untried option. 

The offensive launched on 28 February was predicated on a gamble that a decapitation strike against Khamenei could replicate an earlier quick win, and Iran named Mojtaba Khamenei as his father's successor.

The timing matters too. As of today Trump has said it is "largely true" that the Iran war caused the midterms loss, after Vance's comments, and Vance posted "The reason we lost is the war." At the same time, the New York Times reports US forces are poised to resume major combat operations on Trump's orders, and Trump says he's weighing an Iran deal against action to "finish them". 

So nine months in, the people with the whole intelligence picture still haven't picked between the two basic exits.
Your strongest angle is probably the February offer. It was an exit on the table before the war began. Shall I draft a reply?

Data Centers Lose At The Ballot Box:

Voters in communities across the U.S. backed limits on data centers in Tuesday's elections.

That puts local rules in the path of the AI construction boom.

Some measures ban new construction.

Others pause building for a set time or only advise local officials.

Piqua, Ohio, offers a concrete example.

About two-thirds of voters backed a change to the city charter, according to the county's unofficial results.

It bans construction of data centers with power demand above 25 megawatts.

That threshold targets large facilities rather than every room with a server in it.

In Boulder City, Nevada, voters rejected a proposal to allow data centers on city-owned land in the Eldorado Valley.

AI companies can order more chips, but those chips still need somewhere to live.

The neighbors have discovered the settings menu.

The votes have different local effects, not the force of a nationwide ban.

They do not establish that existing projects have been canceled.

For the AI buildout, land and local permission remain part of the job.

Even after someone has written the enormous check.

That speed figure is the company's claim.

Actual waiting time depends on the request and quality settings.

For developers, the API adds SVG exports.

On the arid ranches of New Mexico during the Great Depression in the early 1930s, 11-year-old Andres Gonzalez, orphaned at a young age, herded sheep with his grandfather until a flood wiped out their flock, forcing them to follow harvests. He ran away, learned rail-riding from hobos, rejected a sheriff's job offer in Vaughn for jail time instead.

Escaped to a notorious Tempe camp, and later labored four years at Boulder Dam, turning loss into rugged independence. Andres later shared with his family: “From orphan to dam builder, those barren paths built my backbone—proving floods can't drown a determined soul.”

text:
TRUMP PROPOSES PAYING OFF NATIONAL DEBT BY SELLING SEEDS

“The kid in the ad got a bicycle. We’re thinking bigger.”

WASHINGTON — President Trump unveiled a sweeping debt reduction initiative Tuesday after discovering an advertisement in the back of an old comic book promising valuable prizes to enterprising youngsters willing to sell packets of seeds door to door.

“I was reading about our defense capabilities,” Trump explained, holding up an issue of The Incredible Hulk, “and there it was. A complete economic plan. Right between the X-ray glasses and the opportunity to become a locksmith.”

Under the proposal, every Cabinet member will receive a starter kit containing flower seeds, vegetable seeds, an order form, and an inspirational booklet titled Grit, Determination, and a Stamped Return Envelope.

“Nobody thought of this,” Trump said. “We’ve had economists. Harvard people. Very expensive people. Meanwhile, a nine-year-old in Ohio was earning a telescope.”

The Treasury Department initially attempted to explain the difference between balancing the federal budget and paying down the accumulated national debt, but the president interrupted to ask whether anyone had checked how much they could get for the deluxe assortment.

“You’re looking at the small packet,” he told officials. “That’s why we’re in this mess.”

The administration’s preliminary projections assume each federal employee sells several billion dollars’ worth of marigolds.

Asked whether that target was realistic, a White House spokesperson said the figures had been independently reviewed by the same department responsible for estimating how quickly Americans could assemble a backyard shed.

Cabinet members have already been assigned territories. The secretary of state will handle foreign governments, the commerce secretary will approach major retailers, and the defense secretary will begin with houses displaying a flag.

Congress requested an exemption after discovering the program required members to knock on doors without first knowing whether the occupants were donors.

The president rejected the request.

“They’re always telling us they’re grassroots,” he said. “Let’s see them move some grass.”

Early diplomatic outreach has reportedly been encouraging. One European government agreed to purchase twelve packets of zinnias after being assured that declining would not automatically trigger a tariff.

China requested to see the catalog, then offered to manufacture the seeds, the envelopes, and the bicycle.

The program encountered its first setback when the original company’s fulfillment address turned out to be a post office box that had been closed for decades. Administration officials described this as evidence that excessive regulation had destroyed another great American business.

Trump remained undeterred, announcing that the government would establish its own distribution center and appoint a special seed czar.

Within hours, Congress authorized a warehouse, a national advertising campaign, a seed security task force, and a feasibility study on whether tomatoes constitute critical infrastructure.

The startup appropriation exceeded projected seed revenue by a considerable margin, but officials emphasized that the program was still in its planting phase.

At the closing press conference, a reporter asked what would happen if the country failed to sell enough seeds to retire the debt.

Trump turned the comic book over.

“We have options,” he said. “Apparently, you can also make a fortune drawing this turtle.”

text:
AI IN DAILY LIFE — 

A Smarter Thermostat, a Smaller Bill: AI at Home Without the Hype

IMAGE (direct URL, not an attachment): https://t.co/ywyCOWYJdK
Image attribution: HUUM, via Unsplash. Image source: https://t.co/Vzyaqe0DYi
Reuse terms: Free to use under the Unsplash License — https://t.co/f9atxJH4kf(observe license conditions).
The best everyday AI does not need to interrupt your life. It can quietly notice a pattern, make a modest adjustment and leave you with a more comfortable home and a smaller energy bill.
Smart thermostats illustrate that idea. Many connected models learn preferred temperatures or use occupancy signals to reduce heating and cooling when a home is empty. These features are not equally advanced across products, and not every smart thermostat uses the same machine-learning techniques. But they show how data-driven automation can serve a practical purpose.

Where the savings come from

Heating and cooling account for a substantial share of household energy use. A thermostat cannot make a poorly insulated building efficient by itself, but it can reduce unnecessary equipment operation. Instead of maintaining the same temperature around the clock, it can follow a schedule or adjust settings based on presence and preferences.

The US Environmental Protection Agency’s ENERGY STAR program says certified smart thermostats are evaluated using real-world field data. Its guidance estimates average savings of about 8% on heating and cooling bills, or roughly $50 per year. Actual results vary with climate, equipment, energy prices, insulation and household habits.
Google offered another perspective on April 16, 2026: it estimated that Nest thermostats had collectively saved more than 200 billion kilowatt-hours since 2011. That is a company estimate extrapolated from studies and usage assumptions, not a measurement of every individual home’s savings.

Make the technology work for you

Start with comfort and safety. Choose reasonable temperature ranges, verify that the thermostat is compatible with your heating and cooling equipment, and test its schedule during ordinary weekdays and weekends. If a household member needs a stable indoor temperature, convenience should never override that requirement.

Review privacy settings as carefully as temperature settings. Occupancy information can reveal routines. Check whether remote access is needed, who can see the household’s data, and how to disable features that do not fit your preferences. Keep device software updated and protect the account with strong authentication.
Intelligence is not the same as autonomy

A thermostat can automate adjustments, but it does not understand every circumstance. Guests, unusual work hours, pets and changing weather can defeat simplistic assumptions. Manual controls and clear override options matter.

The larger lesson extends beyond thermostats. Good household AI should have a specific job, a measurable benefit and a way for people to remain in charge. When the system is useful, the technology becomes less visible rather than more demanding.
Takeaway: Start with one everyday task where smart automation can save effort or resources, then measure the actual benefit instead of trusting the marketing.

Google, Nest energy savings estimate (April 16, 2026): https://t.co/PvPF94Z6T0

The @MiamiDolophins should do everything possible to bring Lamar Jackson to Miami!!

Previously posted this post.  But due to some confusion I want it to be known that I believe this is something that should happen in March and not before Tuesday trade deadline. 

Why it makes sense for the @MiamiDolphins to trade for  Lamar Jackson!!      

Lamar Jackson holds all the leverage. He has a no-trade clause, a no-tag clause, and an $84M cap hit. Because of that, Baltimore is facing three choices: trade him to a team of his choice on terms favorable to the acquiring team, cut him and get nothing, or keep him on the roster with an $84M cap hit.  

If Lamar wanted Miami, the Dolphins could potentially offer Malik Willis plus a conditional 2028 2nd-round pick that could become a 2029 1st-round pick. From Baltimore's perspective, that's a better return than letting Lamar play out the final year of his contract and potentially ending up with only a 2029 compensatory 3rd-round pick.  

Miami is projected to have around $100M in cap space, and trading for a top-5 QB may be a better use of those resources than overspending in free agency, especially when the front office has traditionally preferred to draft and develop talent.  Including Willis would help offset some of the cap concerns, and Lamar's roughly $52M cap hit in 2026 could be lowered through an extension. I could also see Miami using a front-loaded structure, taking advantage of its cap space in 2026 while maintaining flexibility down the road.  

The biggest benefit for Miami is that it accelerates the rebuild. Instead of spending years hoping to find and develop a franchise QB, Miami would already have one in place while still being able to draft and develop a young quarterback such as LaNorris Sellers behind him. That potentially shortens the timeline back to contention while giving the Dolphins both a proven veteran and a long-term plan at the position.  

I know some will say Lamar is injury prone. I get it. he has had some injuries. If Lamar’s injuries were the result of him taking off and running down the field you might be onto something.   But Lamar’s injuries have been because the OL  failed to protect him.   And this thumb injury was just a fluke.   Miami has a better OL with Paul, Proctor, Brewer than the Ravens have right now.  Miami can add a RT in the Offseason and Lamar would have the protection needed for him to stay on the field.

text:
In 2016, a woman in New York hit a $42,949,672 jackpot on a penny slot machine. It would have been the biggest slot jackpot in US history.

The casino offered her a steak dinner.

Her name is Katrina Bookman. In the video below, she shows the selfie she took next to the machine, with the number right there on the screen. A crowd gathered. Then security showed up.

They told her the machine had malfunctioned. One employee told her: “You didn’t win nothing.” Under state rules, the most she could get was $2.25, the amount the machine printed on her ticket. The machine’s real maximum payout was $6,500.

“It’s a lot of money. Y’all gonna claim that it’s broke?”

She is not the only one. In Alabama, a construction worker named Jerry watched a slot machine tell him he had won $1.3 million. Twenty-four hours later, he was told the machine malfunctioned.

Outside Seattle, Veronica’s machine showed $8.5 million. She took out her camera. She was told it was another broken machine. “They took my money, and they didn’t want to pay my winnings.”

The casinos’ position: malfunctions are extremely rare, and when they happen, payouts are void. In every one of these cases, the jackpot was bigger than the machine was ever allowed to pay.

Should a casino have to pay what its own machine says you won, or is “malfunction” a fair excuse when the number is $42 million?

Thanks for waiting. Let's break this down properly. 

Let me put this into perspective. Voter suppression doesn’t have to specifically be about preventing someone from being able to cast a ballot. It involves laws, policies, or administrative decisions that make voting extremely difficult. There are voter suppression, voter disenfranchisement, and vote dilution that make voting difficult. 

A lot of rural and low-income Americans who want to vote cannot afford transportation to go to vote. Some can request a mail-in ballot, but it can be turned down for irregularities like missing signatures or identification errors, which makes it harder to verify. Some Republican policies want to introduce limits on or get rid of mail-in ballots except for a specific group of people. Donald Trump, for example, has accused Democrats of cheating in elections by using mail-in ballots, despite the President on record voting by mail-in ballot. 

Some policies limit or restrict the number of mail-in ballot drop boxes or lack ballot curing. Some people don’t really check their status to see if their ballot was turned in and didn't realize their ballot wasn't counted because they didn't check a notification on the system. Also, some states do have ballot curing, but some do not. 

Political barriers include certain parties not having ballot access or, in some cases, their votes not being counted if they miss deadlines, which happens because of long processing or administrative problems. Some Republicans go out of their way to challenge vote extensions. They often ask courts to delay extending the voting hours due to claims of election security. For example, Republicans challenged voting-hour extensions, as in Arkansas in 2002, where the GOP challenged extended polling hours following an administrative issue. The Supreme Court of Arkansas stated the lower court had lacked the authority to extend voting hours. 

We don’t have an Election Day Holiday where people can leave work early to go vote or have the day off so they can go vote, so they may miss the opportunity to vote. Some states, like Mississippi, Alabama, and New Hampshire, don't offer early voting, which discourages people from voting because they think Election Day is too hectic to wait in long lines, or they can’t vote early because of work, suppressing potential votes. A lot of Republicans gerrymander redistricting maps to ensure Democrats’ seats are removed in hopes of getting Republican gains, which creates voter dilution. I know (obviously democrats respond back with their own gerrymander maps).

They also change where you can vote. For example, Marsha gets off work and intends to vote at her local voting center. Republican voting laws, like polling place closures or consolidation policies, cause Marsha to have to travel from 20 minutes to 1 hour and 30 minutes, which she cannot afford, causing her not to vote on that day. Some examples are Maricopa County 2016, Randolph County, Georgia 2018, and Lincoln County, Georgia 2022.

text:
We're done writing Cold-Email copy.

Here's 104 Agent Rules that pump out relevant 2 liners and subject lines:

-Use the current offer and audience.
-Review the course and approved examples.
-Apply your latest feedback over older drafts.
-Write only for verified, safe leads.
-Use each company’s own research.
-Keep facts separate from financing hypotheses.
-Never borrow another company’s details.
-Line one establishes relevance.
-Make it a statement, not a question.
-No greeting or first name.
-No CTA in line one.
-End it with a period.
-Anchor it in one useful detail.
-Prefer named machines over generic equipment.
-Use facility size when supported.
-Use location counts when supported.
-Use specific processes when assets are unknown.
-Connect that detail to financing relevance.
-Observation-first openings are welcome.
-Conditional relevance-first openings also work.
-“Saw,” “With your,” and “Relevant if” work.
-Never use the word “mind.”
-No “I was thinking” substitutes.
-No “why I’m reaching out.”
-No “listed on your website” narration.
-No disconnected facts or company descriptions.
-No invented projects or expansion angles.
-Line two adds the offer and CTA.
-Add a concrete reason to work with us.
-Bring existing lenders into competition.
-Or emphasize financing tailored around the assets.
-Never sell a lender search.
-Never imply we still need lender relationships.
-Generic “we can help” is too thin.
-Avoid assessment or administrative-service pitches.
-Keep the offer connected to line one.
-Use “that equipment” or “those sites.”
-Don’t repeat machine names, cities or measurements.
-Add another asset only when evidence supports it.
-Keep the financing direction coherent.
-Link the offer and CTA with a comma.
-Keep the entire second line together.
-End with one CTA question.
-Vary conversation, discussion and meeting naturally.
-Conditional openings need a complete CTA.
-Never start both lines with “If.”
-Keep the language human.
-Use short, familiar words.
-Speak directly with “you” and “your.”
-Avoid “may,” “may be” and formal hedging.
-Cut filler and explanatory tails.
-Vary openings, clause order and rhythm.
-Scramble the whole construction, not just synonyms.
-Carry variation across batch boundaries.
-Don’t rotate through fixed templates.
-Don’t force awkward wording for uniqueness.
-Natural repetition is allowed.
-Read both lines as one email.
-Keep every claim supportable.
-Don’t invent machines, counts or facility sizes.
-Separate machinery used from products sold.
-Separate facilities from service coverage.
-Keep parent and subsidiary facts distinct.
-Keep U.S. and foreign facilities distinct.
-Don’t present historical assets as current.
-“Another machine” requires evidence of existing use.
-A proposed refi doesn’t prove existing borrowing.
-Don’t invent ownership, balances or maturities.
-Don’t invent intent, urgency or purchasing plans.
-Don’t promise approval, savings or committed financing.
-Don’t invent sender proof or results.
-Unknown financing needs aren’t an exclusion.
-Don’t mention who pays our compensation.
-Don’t promise a completely free refi.
-Compensation alone isn’t the value proposition.
-Apply the vocabulary and formatting rules.
-Use “financing,” never bare “finance.”
-Use “refinancing” or “refi,” never bare “refinance.”
-Remove the state after a city.
-Preserve actual names like Oklahoma City.
-Preserve relevant standalone state footprints.
-No em dashes; use a hyphen.
-No ALL-CAPS acronyms.
-No spintax inside these cells.
-Run the full SpamGuard vocabulary checks.
-Examples banned: fees, upfront, loans, debt, credit.
-Also banned: structure, compare, terms, new, additional.
-No pressure, urgency or hype.
-A clean scan doesn’t prove good copy.
-A clean scan doesn’t guarantee inbox placement.
-Generate and verify carefully.
-Use GPT-6 Luna through Loopster.
-Use your own OpenAI connection.
-Keep research tools disabled during copy generation.
-Preserve approved rows outside the edit scope.
-Review wording, evidence and both-line cohesion.
-Validate exact row-to-copy mapping.
-Save finished plain text.
-Read every written value back.
-Stay within the approved spend cap.
-Copy approval never authorizes sending.

Full wording: [First-line rules](/Users/redacted/Documents/Outbound Automations/gtme-engine/knowledge/outbound-copy/relevant-opener-playbook.md).

text:
100% agree!

Connecticut GOP leadership has presided over a multi-year collapse.

Since 2021 the party has gone from a functioning minority that could still influence outcomes to a near-irrelevance in both the legislature and local government. The numbers are unambiguous.

In the state Senate the caucus stood at 12 seats after the 2020 election. It is now projected at 3–4.

3 to 4 seats!?!?! That is an absolute embarrassment! That is the smallest Republican presence in the chamber IN MODERN HISTORY. Longtime members and the Minority Leader himself were defeated. In the House the caucus went from 54 seats after 2020 to the mid-30s or low-40s after 2026—a net loss of roughly 15 seats across two cycles, with the steepest drop this year. Democrats did not lose a single seat in either chamber in 2026.

At the municipal level the picture is the same. In 2025 alone Democrats flipped an estimated 25–29 mayor or first-selectman seats that had been under Republican control. The statewide balance of chief executives moved from roughly 73 Democratic / 92 Republican to about 102 Democratic / 65 Republican. Comparable races that Republicans had won by an average of nearly 2 points in 2021 swung to a Democratic average margin of more than 7 points. High-profile losses included long-held seats in New Britain, Stratford, Ansonia, Bristol, Milford, and Westport.

These are not isolated bad nights. They are consecutive cycles of net losses at both the state and local level, culminating in a 2026 result that left the party with historically small legislative minorities in an already deep-blue state. Leadership has offered no effective response to registration trends, suburban shifts, or the national environment. Candidate recruitment, message discipline, and turnout infrastructure have failed to protect even seats that were previously competitive or safe. The result is a party that now holds fewer than 10 percent of Senate seats and has surrendered large numbers of local executive offices it once controlled.

A leadership that produces this trajectory has not delivered and it's not even up for debate. The data speaks for itself and it shows SUSTAINED EROSION, not a temporary setback. The messaging is NOT working!!

The CT GOP Party Leadership needs to immediately resign.

text:
YAKUZA 5 REMASTERED: TATSUYA, EVERY RESTAURANT RECOMMENDATION AND FOOD COMPLETION

Food completion is not just buying one of everything from the first menu you see. Tatsuya adds new dishes, substories change menus, some restaurants hide orders behind observations, and Pronto changes its menu with the time of day.

HOW TATSUYA WORKS

Each character meets him through story progression. Speak to him at his standing location to activate the request, then eat at the three qualifying places. Your character comments when a restaurant is suitable. Report it to Tatsuya and the visit with him happens automatically. After all three recommendations, attend his filming scene to complete that character's route and unlock the new dish or shop item.

Recommendation 1 grants Gourmet in Training: restaurants can fill a yellow overcharge health bar above ordinary health. Recovery items cannot refill that bar. Food can also add Strength, Focus or Spirit bonuses; drinks do not.

Recommendation 2 grants Master Gourmet, allowing a second level of the food bonuses. Recommendation 3 grants King/Queen of Gourmets, slowing the overcharge's natural drain. Once the yellow bar is gone, its associated bonuses are lost.

Strength boosts unarmed damage, or Haruka's dance points. Focus keeps Heat above a floor. Spirit improves Heat Action damage, or Haruka's Heat gain. After trying a dish, its bonus is recorded on the menu. Use the displayed effect rather than assuming every meat dish follows the same rule.

KIRYU / NAGASUGAI

Trigger: Tatsuya is a taxi fare during Part 1 Chapter 2. His text directs you to Ose Bridge. Talk there before collecting recommendations.

Eat at and recommend:
1. Hakataso.
2. Hango Zosui Yama.
3. Udon West.

For the concluding scene, go to the southwest food-stall row at sunset or night, near the ramen minigame location. This creates the Senbo stall and its new dish. Looking for a new item on an unrelated restaurant's daytime menu won't finish this route.

SAEJIMA / TSUKIMINO

Trigger: after leaving Polaris for the first time in Chapter 4, encounter him by the road.

Recommend:
1. Curry Shop S.
2. Matsuo Lamb Barbeque.
3. Miyoshino.

Then attend the filming at Tsukimino Café Alps. The local café gains its new dish. This is not the Kamurocho Café Alps.

HARUKA / SOTENBORI

Trigger: after the Chapter 2 game show. Find him on Bishamon Bridge.

Recommend:
1. Kushikatsu Daruma.
2. Tsuruhashi Fugetsu.
3. Magutako.

Then find the filming at Montblanc Coffee near Bunzaemon Mall, a little north of the save point. The reward is a baumkuchen sold as a takeout recovery item. Montblanc is not an ordinary sit-down restaurant with a whole menu to empty, so don't assume the route is stuck because no restaurant interface appears.

AKIYAMA / SOTENBORI, THEN KAMUROCHO

Trigger: after his story visit to Crest Bar. Find Tatsuya on Bishamon Bridge.

Recommend:
1. Komian.
2. Zuboraya.
3. Kani Douraku.

His filming is at KANRAI IN KAMUROCHO. You cannot finish that last step while confined to Part 3's Osaka chapter. Return during the finale, attend the scene and then buy the added menu item.

SHINADA / KINEICHO

Trigger: early in his story outside the apartment. Tatsuya subsequently stands at the nearby intersection.

Recommend:
1. Daruma.
2. Kaburaya.
3. Sekai no Yamachan.

Attend the filming at Café Alps at Kumano/Honjincho. This adds the local café's new dish. You can combine visits to these three recommended restaurants with Igarashi's later chicken-eating assignment, but make sure each task has actually been activated before relying on those meals for its progress.

Finishing Tatsuya's full training unlocks Frozen Banana at the Completion Office.

FOOD-COMPLETION CLEANUP ROUTE

1. Finish all five Tatsuya sequences, including filming. “I recommended all three” is not the endpoint.
2. Finish the food-related substories Dragon Seafood Rice Bowl, Treats from All Over and The Perfect Seasoning. These unlock additional menu entries, including changes at Kanrai, Café Alps and Kushikatsu Daruma.
3. In restaurants that offer observation or conversation, check the wall, other customers and staff before ordering. At Tamasa Ramen, inspect another customer and the bar: these expose two otherwise-hidden orders.
4. Clear Pronto in Kamurocho twice: Café menu during the day, Bar menu in evening/night. These are different menus, not a random rotation.
5. Include alcohol at the named bars, not only meals at restaurants.
6. Use the completion list to identify the precise remaining venue and item. A repeated brand can share credit across its locations; unrelated bars do not share credit simply because they sell the same whisky. Drinking Yamazaki 25-years-old in one named bar does not clear it in every other named bar.

APPETITE AND ALCOHOL MANAGEMENT

Buy AppStimRx and Legendary Drinker of Ryukyu from pharmacies or stocked convenience stores. AppStimRx lowers health so you can eat again. Legendary Drinker reduces intoxication, allowing further drinks. Keep enough stock for a whole district rather than making a pharmacy trip after every menu.

Before starting a dangerous fight, restore the health you deliberately lowered. Before an ordinary story boss, restaurant overcharge can make the food cleanup useful combat preparation. Before the Coliseum, it cannot: the arena removes Gourmet health and buffs, so don't buy a giant meal expecting to carry it into a tournament.

Check unlocked dishes again after their associated scenes. A restaurant you cleared earlier may become incomplete when a new menu item appears. Conversely, a missing filming scene, a hidden order or Pronto's second menu is a more plausible explanation for a tiny final percentage gap than needing to repeat every meal in every city.

text:
YAKUZA 5 REMASTERED: KAMIYAMA CRAFTING, MATERIALS AND MONEY

The important distinction at Kamiyama Works is INVEST versus MATERIAL. Investing an item permanently unlocks a recipe but consumes that item. A material is carried in your inventory and consumed when you buy the finished product. Donating a rare item just because a recipe mentions it can leave you needing another copy.

UNLOCK AND LOCATIONS

During Kiryu's Part 1 Chapter 3, rescue Kamiyama at the exclamation mark north of the apartment. His Nagasugai shop is halfway down Chikuzengawa Street South in the southeast. Other shops can be visited before their arrival text adds the van icon:
• Tsukimino: west side of Main Street, south side of the road.
• Sotenbori: Shofukucho parking lot across from Komian.
• Kineicho: parking lot in the block south of Kume Boulevard.
• Kamurocho: off Park Alley, south of Kamurocho Hills.
Haruka cannot use K-Works.

SHOP INVESTMENT

The money thresholds for successive level increases are: level 2 ¥5,000; 3 ¥10,000; 4 ¥15,000; 5 ¥20,000; 6 ¥30,000; 7 ¥50,000; 8 ¥100,000; 9 ¥120,000; 10 ¥150,000. Work from the shop's current investment display instead of treating the final figure as the entire campaign budget. Invest required unlock items first, then add money as needed.

A RELIABLE COMPLETION WORKFLOW

1. Keep rare materials, equipment rewards and Shinada's Sturdy weapons in storage until you've checked their recipes.
2. Unlock the recipe by investing the required item once.
3. Buy or retrieve the base weapon, carrying it in personal inventory.
4. Buy the upgrade. Check the completion entry, then decide whether the result is needed for another recipe before selling or investing it.
5. Build chains from the bottom upward. A late upgrade may require a weapon you already made and then accidentally sold.
6. Use Completion Office replacements intelligently. Once one of its reward items is consumed, sold or discarded, another can be claimed. Only one copy can be out at a time across the cast; if a different character holds it, that can block the replacement.

PRACTICAL CHAINS

Police baton branch: Police Baton at shop level 8, ¥58,000 → invest Super Resilient Resin and use the baton to buy Kamiyama's Police Baton at level 9, ¥62,000 → invest Pearl and use that upgraded baton for Colorful Parasol at level 10, ¥100,000 → invest Sturdy Pole and consume the parasol for Extremely Sturdy Iron Pipe, ¥100,000.

Knife branch: buy Nameless Short Sword → invest Chili Pepper and use it for Super Spicy Knife at level 6, ¥25,000 → Chinese Broadsword at level 7, ¥40,000 → Lotus Clan Broadsword at level 9, ¥60,000 → invest Dragon Scale and consume the Lotus blade for Divine Dragon Short Sword at level 10, ¥200,000. That dragon sword is needed by later recipes, so don't discard it.

Katana branch: Nameless Katana → invest Cherry Tree Branch and make Sakura Storm at level 6, ¥23,000 → Photon Blade MG at level 7, ¥20,000 → invest Gravity Converter and make Photon Blade PG at level 8, ¥43,000 → invest Eye of the Dragon and make Dragon Slayer at level 10, ¥200,000.

Pole branch: invest Gravity Converter to buy Photon Blade WG at level 9, ¥98,000 → invest Seal of the Dragon and consume it for Mighty Dragon Spear at level 10, ¥200,000.

Bat branch: invest Block of Brass to buy Patriarch's Bat at level 9, ¥98,000 → invest Sacred Wood and use the bat for Golden Dragon Bat at level 10, ¥200,000.

Hammer branch: invest Super Resilient Resin for Toy Hammer at level 7, ¥50,000; invest Maguro and use the toy hammer for Frozen Tuna at level 9, ¥53,000. Raging Dragon Hammer is a separate level-10 purchase unlocked by investing Dragon Tail, ¥220,000.

Kali sticks branch: invest Large Blow-Up Doll for Cutie Girl Sticks at level 8, ¥65,000 → invest Dragon Talon and use those sticks for Twin Dragon Sticks at level 10, ¥180,000.

Tonfa branch: Steel Tonfa at level 5, ¥27,000 → invest Kamaitachi Utility Knife and use the tonfa for Slashing Tonfa at level 8, ¥42,000 → invest Dragon Talon and use the slashing pair for Dragon Horn at level 10, ¥180,000.

Other useful endpoints: Dragon Nunchaku needs a Seal of the Dragon investment, level 10 and ¥220,000. Dragon Grudge Gloves needs Dragon Fang invested, Konpeito carried as its material, level 10 and ¥200,000. Smoking Gun needs SSS Gunpowder invested, Zap Gun carried and ¥190,000 at level 10; Zap Gun itself is unlocked by Small Motor at level 7 and costs ¥80,000.

Defensive chains: invest Durable Cloth and use Steel Shin Guards for High-Tech Shin Guards at level 8, ¥35,000, then consume those for High-Tech Arm Guards at level 9, ¥45,000. Invest Fitness Gear to buy Yakuza Training Gear at level 9, ¥20,000; invest Eye of the Dragon and consume that gear for Dragon Shirt at level 10, ¥150,000. Dragon's Binding needs Mystery Stone INVESTED and Bloody Binding carried as the material, ¥80,000 at level 10.

SHINADA'S STURDY-WEAPON TRAP

The names deliberately cross over. The investment is not necessarily the same weapon category as the output:
• Sturdy Pole unlocks Extremely Sturdy Iron Pipe; material is Colorful Parasol.
• Sturdy Katana unlocks Extremely Sturdy Knife; material is the Divine Dragon Short Sword.
• Sturdy Knife unlocks Extremely Sturdy Katana; material is Dragon Slayer.
• Sturdy Iron Pipe unlocks Extremely Sturdy Pole; material is Mighty Dragon Spear.
All are level 10, ¥100,000 each. Keep these Sturdy rewards. Shinada receives the iron pipe through his story; the other Sturdy weapons come from his baseball side story.

WHERE THE IMPORTANT MATERIALS COME FROM

Side-story and training completion:
• Dragon Scale: complete Taxi Driver.
• Seal of the Dragon: complete Hunter and Killer.
• Dragon Tail: complete The Cost of a Swing.
• Eye of the Dragon: complete Tendo training.
Collect these through the Completion Office, not by searching the ending scene for a dropped item.

Substories and side activities:
• Sacred Wood: Shinada's Saving Yourself.
• Cherry Tree Branch: Shinada's Dirty Heart or Wanna Party?, also a blue Drawing Tickets prize.
• Fitness Gear: Akiyama's Haggle Wars or Kamurocho locker B1.
• High-Grade Platinum: Kiryu's A Knock on the Door or Shinada's A Precious Meal, also Coliseum exchange.
• Block of Brass, Magnetized Metal, Bloody Binding: hunting rewards; Bloody Binding also has a Coliseum source.
• Durable Cloth: garbage collection or Akiyama's Bad Boys.
• Pearl: Drawing Tickets grand prize.
• Mystery Liquid: IF8 repeat reward.
• Small Motor: IF8 or blue Drawing Tickets reward.
• Gravity Converter: IF8 or Sotenbori locker D2.

Lockers worth preserving:
• Sotenbori C2 Large Blow-Up Doll; C3 Squid; F5 Chunk of Wood (Ash); H3 Super Resilient Resin.
• Kamurocho A2 SSS Gunpowder; B1 Fitness Gear.
The blow-up doll also appears among white lottery rewards and resin among red rewards.

Shop purchases:
• Aji Spicy Roe 240g (Regular): Fukuya in Nagasugai, for Cod Roe Blackjack.
• Aoyagi Sweet Rice Cake 5pcs: Dagaya in Kineicho, for Uirou Pole.
• Battery: Don Quijote in Sotenbori/Kamurocho, for Stun Gun.
• Chili Pepper: Don Quijote in Sotenbori/Kamurocho, also garbage collection.
• Rubber Ball: Don Quijote in Sapporo, also garbage collection, for Slime Gun.
• Lighter Oil: Sapporo Don Quijote, hunting contract reward or blue lottery prize, for Bottomless Lighter.
• Kamaitachi Utility Knife: Ebisu Pawn in Tsukimino, Kineicho or Kamurocho, also baseball rewards.

Fish: Squid is available through sea fishing as well as its locker. Marlin comes from Nagoya sea fishing or a red Drawing Tickets prize. Maguro means tuna and comes from Tokyo sea fishing. A fish needed as an INVESTMENT and a base weapon needed as a MATERIAL are different parts of the order.

Coliseum exchange supplies Dragon Talon and Dragon Fang at 150,000 points each, Bloody Binding at 150,000, High-Grade Platinum and SSS Gunpowder at 100,000, and Mystery Stone at 200,000. Don't spend every point on recovery items before budgeting these.

THE NINE MODIFIED DRAGON WEAPONS

At shop level 10, invest the corresponding ordinary dragon weapon to unlock its Modified version. Each Modified weapon costs ¥800,000 and normally lists Mystery Stone as its material. The nine are Golden Dragon Bat, Divine Dragon Short Sword, Dragon Slayer, Mighty Dragon Spear, Raging Dragon Hammer, Twin Dragon Sticks, Dragon Horn, Dragon Nunchaku and Dragon Grudge Gloves.

Budget ¥7.2 million for the nine Modified purchases alone, before base weapons and other upgrades.

CyricZ documents a same-order material-consumption quirk: once all nine recipes are unlocked, one carried Mystery Stone can cover all nine if they are selected and bought in ONE order. Don't buy one, exit and expect the stone to remain. The guide also warns that multiple stones carried can all be consumed by that order. Save first, put spare stones in storage and verify the order before confirming. This is a documented quirk, not a requirement to gamble your only save on it. Dragon's Binding still needs its separately invested stone.

MONEY PLAN

Early on, use your protagonist's substantial side activities rather than selling irreplaceable-looking crafting pieces: taxi work for Kiryu, hunting for Saejima and baseball progression for Shinada. Save plates and saleable surplus for when cash is needed, but remember Tendo needs one Gold Plate.

Late-game Deathmatch 100 can pay over ¥1 million for a successful clear. It requires Coliseum rank 20 or better and real combat preparation, so it is a funding route after training, not an early shortcut. Repeat with a character whose crowd control you can reliably use.

Keep ¥5 million available for Hinata's final relationship event. That money only needs to be shown, not spent, so finish that event before pouring the same fortune into Modified weapons. Likewise, Honoka's event asks you to offer your money but does not actually take it.

This is the route and bottleneck checklist, not a claim that every cheap shop entry is reproduced here. Use the in-game equipment completion list to buy remaining straightforward items and the linked recipe reference for their exact level, price and dependencies. The expensive mistakes are losing a prerequisite, confusing investment with material, and crafting piecemeal before the final budget is ready.

text:
1. Satan is called “the god of this world”2 Corinthians 4:4 (KJV):“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.”

Paul identifies Satan as “the god of this world” (Greek: ho theos tou aiōnos toutou — “the god of this age”). 

He actively blinds the minds of unbelievers so they cannot see the gospel of Christ.Related titles in the KJV:
“The prince of this world” — John 12:31; 14:30; 16:11
“The prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience” — Ephesians 2:2
“The whole world lieth in wickedness” (under the sway of the evil one) — 1 John 5:19

2. He offered JESUS the kingdoms of the world because he claimed influence over them Luke 4:5–7 (KJV):5 And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
6 And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.
7 If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.(See also the parallel in Matthew 4:8–9.)

Satan explicitly claimed that the kingdoms and their glory had been “delivered unto” him and that he could give them to whomever he wished—if Jesus would worship him.

Intellectual understanding
Usurped, not ultimate authority: Satan is not the Creator or sovereign God. He is a fallen angel who rebelled (Isaiah 14:12–15; Ezekiel 28:12–17 traditions; Revelation 12). His power is real but limited, temporary, and always under the ultimate sovereignty of God (as seen in the book of Job, where he must seek permission).

Influence over the present age: “This world” / “this age” refers to the present fallen system—human societies, governments, cultures, and values that operate in opposition to God’s kingdom. 

Fallen humanity, through sin beginning in the Garden, effectively handed him influence (Romans 5:12; the “delivered unto me” claim in Luke 4). He works through deception, blinding minds, and promoting philosophies, religions, and systems that keep people from Christ.

Why he could offer the kingdoms: JESUS did not dispute the claim of influence. Instead, He rejected the offer on the basis of worship belonging only to God (Luke 4:8; Deuteronomy 6:13). Accepting it would have been a shortcut to messianic rule without the cross—the very path Satan wanted. Jesus’ true kingdom is “not of this world” (John 18:36); He receives all authority from the Father after His death and resurrection (Matthew 28:18; Philippians 2:9–11).

Temporary and judged: JESUS said the prince of this world has been judged (John 16:11) and will be cast out (John 12:31). Believers are delivered from his dominion into CHRIST'S KINGDOM (Colossians 1:13; Acts 26:18). His final defeat is certain (Revelation 20:10).

In short: The KJV affirms that Satan currently functions as the god/prince of this present age and that he offered JESUS worldly kingdoms he claimed authority over. JESUS refused, and HIS VICTORY ON THE CROSS and RESURRECTION breaks that power for all who believe.

text:
In a world where it is easy to connect with people but difficult to find genuine relationships, we must understand the value of real friendship.

A real friend celebrates your victories without jealousy, stands beside you during difficult seasons, speaks truth even when it is uncomfortable and supports you when you have nothing to offer in return.

The Bible reminds us that true friendship is not just about being present when life is good; it is about standing together when life gets difficult.

Don’t just look for good friends…strive to be one.

Be the friend who prays, encourages, supports, forgives and shows up. Don’t take genuine relationships for granted.

In a world full of temporary connections, be intentional about building lasting friendships. It’s better to have a few genuine friends who stand with you than a crowd of people who only stand around you.

“ A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.”

- Proverbs 17:17

DR. ASLAM ALIYU LEADS MASSIVE GRASSROOTS EMPOWERMENT DRIVE AS BABA TINUBU FISABILILLAHI PROJECT 2027 DEBUTS IN ZAMFARA

The City Boy Movement, under the leadership of Seyi Tinubu, has officially launched the Baba Tinubu Fisabilillahi Project 2027 in Gusau, Zamfara State, under the matronship of Dr. Princess Aslam Aliyu, Gimbiyar Kaura.

The official flag-off ceremony was performed by the Executive Governor of Zamfara State, Dauda Lawal, marking the commencement of an ambitious empowerment initiative designed to improve livelihoods, support grassroots communities and strengthen mobilisation ahead of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s 2027 re-election campaign.

The Zamfara launch represents the beginning of a 19-state empowerment tour across Northern Nigeria, with distribution teams taking the initiative directly to beneficiaries across all 14 Local Government Areas of the state.

The empowerment package includes:

* 1,000 sewing machines.
* 3,000 spaghetti-making and grinding machines.
* 1,000 soybean processing (Awara) kits.
* 700 solar generators.
* 150 motorcycles.
* 20,000 bags of rice.
* ₦350,000,000 direct cash donations to each of 15,000 beneficiaries.

Beyond the immediate empowerment intervention, the movement has also incorporated a Clean Water Project, with 150 hand-pump boreholes constructed to improve access to safe drinking water across local communities.

Following the launch, the Deputy Governor of Zamfara State commissioned one of the newly constructed boreholes at Mareri Village in Gusau Local Government Area, marking another important step towards addressing water accessibility challenges at the grassroots.

This ambitious intervention deserves commendation, particularly for its scale, diversity and direct focus on improving the economic circumstances of ordinary people. By providing equipment for small businesses, agricultural processing, transportation, financial assistance and access to clean water, the initiative goes beyond conventional political mobilisation to offer practical support with the potential to create lasting socioeconomic benefits.

Dr. Princess Aslam Aliyu deserves special recognition for her leadership, commitment and determination in driving this initiative in Zamfara State. Her role in bringing together an extensive empowerment programme of this magnitude reflects an impressive commitment to grassroots engagement and community development.

The leadership of Seyi Tinubu and the City Boy Movement equally deserves recognition for extending this initiative across Northern Nigeria through a coordinated 19-state empowerment tour.

Ultimately, the Baba Tinubu Fisabilillahi Project 2027 reinforces the importance of connecting political support with tangible interventions that improve people’s lives. It also demonstrates the growing grassroots mobilisation behind President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

President Tinubu deserves commendation for providing the leadership and political vision that continue to inspire supporters and organised movements to mobilise around his administration’s agenda and the call for continuity in 2027. A prosperous Nigeria requires sustained commitment to empowerment, opportunity and inclusive development, and initiatives of this nature add practical substance to that aspiration.

text:
NQ / NASDAQ — POST-OPEN REGIME RADAR
AI Sell-Off Wipes Out Wednesday's Rally as Semiconductors Plunge Despite Strong US Labour Data — 5 November 2026
5 NOVEMBER 2026 | 17:29 SWITZERLAND | 10:29 CME/CHICAGO | 11:29 NEW YORK
SECOND REPORT OF THE DAY — US CASH SESSION

MAIN CONCLUSION
The US cash market has reversed Wednesday's broad post-election rally, and the sell-off has intensified considerably since this morning's NQ report. At 11:00 New York (17:00 Switzerland), Associated Press reported the Nasdaq Composite down 5.0%, the S&P 500 down 3.2% and the Dow lower by 1,146 points, or approximately 2.1%. The selling is concentrated in the AI computing and data-centre investment chain, with NVIDIA down 8.3%, AMD down 15.9% and CoreWeave down 14.9% in the same observation. Remarkably, this occurred after US unemployment claims fell to 189,000 and third-quarter productivity exceeded expectations. The immediate market problem is not a sudden collapse in US economic activity; it is a repricing of the cost, financing and potential regulatory constraints of AI infrastructure.

KEY CONFIRMATION / RISK
Early selling in Qualcomm and semiconductor shares became a much broader liquidation after the opening. A Reuters observation at 09:57 New York showed the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 7.1%; later reports described still deeper pressure across chips, cloud infrastructure and suppliers of electricity equipment. Treasury yields have declined as investors have bought government bonds, but this has not arrested the decline in technology shares. The crucial issue for the rest of the session is whether selling continues to spread beyond AI-related companies while investors prepare for Friday's official US employment report.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE THE FIRST REPORT

This morning's report identified an important divergence: the Dow was holding up better than NQ futures, while Qualcomm and Arm earnings and weaker Asian chip markets raised concerns about technology participation. The US cash opening resolved part of that uncertainty. The weakness did not remain confined to a handful of stocks. Semiconductor selling intensified, AI infrastructure operators fell sharply, and the broader S&P 500 surrendered more than Wednesday's advance in the AP observation.

The important change is therefore the scale and breadth of the repricing, not simply its direction. Early futures weakness has turned into substantial cash-market losses. Even so, an index-level decline must not be treated as a verified futures quote: the Nasdaq Composite, Nasdaq-100 and NQ contracts are different instruments.

US EQUITY MARKET — VERIFIED TIMED OBSERVATIONS

REUTERS, 09:57 NEW YORK / 15:57 SWITZERLAND:

DOW JONES: −0.66% | S&P 500: −1.66% | NASDAQ COMPOSITE: −3.09%.

PHILADELPHIA SEMICONDUCTOR INDEX: −7.1%.

ASSOCIATED PRESS, 11:00 NEW YORK / 17:00 SWITZERLAND:

DOW JONES: −1,146 POINTS, APPROXIMATELY −2.1%.

S&P 500: −3.2% | NASDAQ COMPOSITE: −5.0%.

These observations illustrate the acceleration in selling during the first 90 minutes of the US cash session. They are not simultaneous quotations taken at the publication time. No unverified live NQ futures price, VWAP, POC or support/resistance level is assigned to this report.

SEMICONDUCTORS — SELLING HAS BROADENED
The industry that helped power the AI expansion is now the centre of the equity decline. Reuters recorded the semiconductor index down 7.1% at 09:57 New York, with NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and Marvell under pressure. The AP's later 11:00 observation reported NVIDIA down 8.3% and AMD down 15.9%.

That matters for NQ because the index is highly sensitive to the share-price performance of large semiconductor and technology businesses. A decline concentrated in one chipmaker can reflect a company-specific earnings issue. Simultaneous weakness across processors, memory, cloud infrastructure and power-equipment suppliers points to a wider reassessment of the investment cycle.

QUALCOMM AND ARM — EARNINGS REACTIONS WERE THE INITIAL SPARK

Qualcomm entered the session under pressure after disappointing smartphone-chip sales and weaker demand linked to the handset market and declining Apple-related business. Reuters recorded a decline of approximately 9% at 09:57 New York. Its data-centre ambitions do not immediately offset the financial importance of existing smartphone revenues.

Arm's recent results showed strong licensing growth but slower royalty growth, exposing a difference between near-term licence receipts and the recurring revenue earned as chips are shipped. The wider market was already demanding exceptional operating results and attractive valuations. These reactions helped establish a weak starting point for Thursday's chip complex, although they cannot by themselves explain every subsequent decline.
DATA-CENTRE OPERATORS — FINANCING RISK IS NOW CENTRAL

The pressure extends beyond chip suppliers. CoreWeave fell 14.9% in the AP observation at 11:00 New York. Reuters also reported steep declines in Nebius, IREN, Applied Digital and other operators associated with AI capacity expansion. Companies supplying electricity infrastructure, including GE Vernova, were caught in the selling as well.

The economic question is increasingly specific: if new facilities take longer to obtain approvals, connect to the grid or reach commercial utilisation, when will invested capital produce cash flow? Companies using debt and long-term lease commitments may be especially sensitive to delays. Funding terms, credit spreads and refinancing requirements are relevant even when US Treasury yields decline.

REGULATORY UNCERTAINTY — DISTINGUISH PROPOSALS FROM ENACTED RULES

Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the 3 November midterm elections, with the new legislature taking office in January. Investors are considering whether federal oversight and local resistance will slow the rapid construction of data centres. However, no nationwide ban on AI infrastructure follows automatically from the election result. The president retains veto powers, while state and local planning decisions operate under their own legal frameworks.

Reuters cited a UBS estimate that around 30% of projected US data-centre capacity additions for 2028 could be exposed to potential construction pauses. That is an analyst scenario, not a confirmed cancellation of 30% of planned projects. The distinction matters: markets can price a risk before it materialises, but a credible financial report must not confuse a forecast with an enacted restriction.

THE AI FINANCING EQUATION

The market's concern now covers several parts of the same economic chain: demand for AI services, chip orders, construction budgets, access to electricity, financing costs and eventual cash generation. Strong semiconductor revenue does not guarantee a profitable outcome for every company funding the facilities. Nor does a fall in stock valuations mean that commercial AI demand has disappeared.

The critical change is that investors are scrutinising the return on capital rather than rewarding ever-larger infrastructure announcements automatically. A delay in commissioning a data centre may affect the operator's cash flow, suppliers' orders and the timing of expected earnings at different stages of the chain.

MARKET BREADTH — THE DAMAGE IS NO LONGER ISOLATED

In Reuters' 09:57 observation, declining issues outnumbered advancing shares by approximately 2.17 to one on the Nasdaq and 1.36 to one on the NYSE. The Nasdaq recorded 247 new 52-week lows against 132 new highs. The AP's 11:00 report indicated that only around two in five S&P 500 shares were higher.

Those figures show that the decline has broadened beyond a handful of mega-cap stocks. Nonetheless, dispersion remains important. Some companies are advancing on their own earnings, so a sweeping statement that every equity sector is falling would be inaccurate.

COMPANY EXCEPTIONS — EARNINGS STILL MATTER

AppLovin was up approximately 30.2% in the AP's 11:00 observation after better-than-expected financial results and an enlarged share buyback programme. Tapestry rose around 6.7% after beating profit expectations and raising guidance. Reuters also reported energy as the strongest major S&P 500 sector in its earlier observation.

These exceptions matter analytically. They show that the market is differentiating between demonstrated financial performance and businesses facing uncertainty over future investment returns. The broad sell-off has not eliminated company-specific buying.

US LABOUR MARKET — INITIAL CLAIMS FELL TO 189,000

The Department of Labor reported 189,000 seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims for the week ending 31 October, down 6,000 from a revised 195,000 in the preceding week. The Reuters consensus was approximately 196,000. The four-week moving average declined to 194,750.

Continuing claims increased to 1.718 million for the week ending 24 October, up 23,000 from a revised 1.695 million. These figures offer a mixed but not contradictory picture: layoffs remain relatively limited, while some people who are already unemployed are continuing to claim benefits. Stronger-than-expected initial claims data did not produce a sustained equity recovery.

PRODUCTIVITY — A SIGNIFICANTLY BETTER INFLATION-GROWTH MIX

The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported nonfarm business productivity growth of 3.6% at a seasonally adjusted annualised rate in the third quarter. Output rose 3.7%, while hours worked increased only 0.1%. Unit labour costs declined 0.7% at an annualised rate, reflecting compensation growth of 2.9% alongside faster productivity.

These are relevant economic figures. Greater output per hour can help companies expand without an equivalent rise in unit labour costs. That may moderate some underlying inflation pressure, although it does not cancel the effects of energy-price shocks or establish the future path of Federal Reserve policy.

The result is especially noteworthy because the equity decline has been severe despite what is, on its face, a favourable productivity and labour-cost combination. Today's technology selling is primarily about prospective capital returns and risk pricing, not the immediate collapse of labour-market conditions.

FEDERAL RESERVE — RATE EXPECTATIONS REMAIN A CONSTRAINT

The Federal Reserve left its policy rate unchanged at 3.75%–4.00% at its October meeting. Inflation remains above target, while the labour market and productivity reports show resilience. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack supported a gradual approach to further rate increases in comments reported Thursday.

Higher prospective financing costs are important for long-duration infrastructure projects, although the effect differs by business. An established hyperscaler financing investment from operating cash flow has a different exposure from a smaller cloud operator relying on external capital. The market's interest-rate interpretation should therefore be linked to business models and balance sheets, not reduced to a single directional assumption about NQ.

TREASURIES — BOND DEMAND HAS NOT RESCUED TECHNOLOGY

Associated Press reported the 10-year Treasury yield near 4.84% around 11:00 New York, down from about 4.90% late Wednesday. Lower yields accompanied substantial technology selling, consistent with investors seeking the relative safety of government bonds.

This is the central intermarket divergence. Declining government yields can lower a valuation discount rate, but they do not guarantee that investors will accept a company's earnings assumptions or financing risks. A rally in Treasuries can therefore coexist with falling Nasdaq shares. No synchronised 2-year, 5-year, 20-year or 30-year yields are assigned to the report's publication minute.

BANK OF ENGLAND — THE RATE INCREASE IS NOW CONFIRMED

The Bank of England raised Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 4.00%, in an 8–1 vote. One member preferred a 50-basis-point increase. The Bank said UK CPI inflation had reached 3.5% in September and projected a rise towards approximately 5% by the middle of 2027, reflecting the effects of energy prices.

This is not a Federal Reserve decision, and the UK policy outlook cannot be applied mechanically to US futures. It does reinforce the broader challenge faced by central banks as elevated energy costs complicate financial conditions and longer-term corporate investment decisions.

OIL — PARTIAL REBOUND AFTER WEDNESDAY'S COLLAPSE

In the AP's 11:00 observation, Brent crude rose approximately 2.2% to $96.70 a barrel after falling nearly 9% on Wednesday. That illustrates how rapidly geopolitical risk is being repriced. Falling energy costs can ease inflation and operating pressure, but the conflict involving Iran and regional supply routes has not been resolved.

For AI infrastructure, electricity costs and availability remain material. For monetary policy, the inflation consequences of the energy shock matter more than any isolated hourly move in crude. Today's modest rebound does not reverse all of Wednesday's decline.

ASIA AND THE GLOBAL HANDOVER

South Korea's Kospi fell around 5.3% and Japan's Nikkei approximately 1.8%, according to the AP. The semiconductor-heavy Korean market has been particularly exposed to concerns about AI investment demand. European markets were mixed; London's FTSE 100 was down modestly after the Bank of England's rate decision.

The global weakness in technology helps explain why the US opening was vulnerable, but international index moves are not direct instructions for NQ. Company weightings, currencies and local market structures differ.

FRIDAY'S US EMPLOYMENT REPORT — NEXT MAJOR CATALYST

Friday, 6 November, at 14:30 Switzerland / 07:30 Chicago / 08:30 New York, the Bureau of Labor Statistics is scheduled to release the October Employment Situation report. Reuters reported a market expectation of approximately 65,000 additional nonfarm payrolls and an unemployment rate near 4.2%. These are forecasts, not actual results.

Today's claims and productivity figures provide useful context but do not predetermine the official payroll report. Changes in wages, employment and the unemployment rate could materially affect Treasury yields and the market's interpretation of future Federal Reserve decisions.

CROSS-MARKET CONFIRMATION FRAMEWORK

SOX — breadth and persistence of semiconductor selling.

NVIDIA, AMD AND QUALCOMM — the degree of chip-sector participation.

COREWEAVE AND OTHER DATA-CENTRE OPERATORS — financing and project-delay risk.

US 2Y AND 10Y — monetary-policy expectations and sovereign yield conditions.

BRENT — energy-price and inflation risk.

VIX AND NASDAQ BREADTH — the scale of risk reduction beyond headline indices.

NQ RELATIVE TO ES — whether technology underperformance is accelerating or moderating.

No unverified futures price, chart level or volatility quotation has been inserted for the exact publication minute.

BULLISH SCENARIO — CONDITIONS FOR STABILISATION

A more constructive case requires observable evidence that the selling in chips and data-centre companies is being absorbed, market breadth improves and Treasury conditions remain orderly. Strong productivity and low initial claims could provide a supportive macroeconomic context, but that support would need to appear in actual equity demand. An isolated upward rebound after a large decline would not by itself resolve the concerns about financing and project economics.

BEARISH SCENARIO — CONDITIONS FOR CONTINUED PRESSURE

The negative case remains better supported by the verified cash-session evidence: semiconductor losses, broadening Nasdaq declines, sharp falls in AI infrastructure operators and defensive Treasury buying. Further widening of corporate credit spreads or renewed selling in mega-cap technology would deepen that environment. The magnitude of the earlier fall does not guarantee continuation during every subsequent interval.

ANALYTICAL EDGE

BEARISH CASH-SESSION REGIME. The evidence is the Nasdaq's approximately 5% decline at 11:00 New York, pronounced semiconductor and data-centre weakness, and deterioration in broader market breadth. This is an assessment of observed conditions, not a statistically calibrated probability of the next trade.

CURRENT REGIME

AI INFRASTRUCTURE REPRICING / SEMICONDUCTOR LIQUIDATION / DATA-CENTRE FINANCING PRESSURE / DEFENSIVE TREASURY DEMAND / STRONG LABOUR PRODUCTIVITY / ELEVATED ENERGY AND POLICY UNCERTAINTY / PRE-PAYROLLS EVENT RISK.

OPERATIONAL CONCLUSION

Thursday's session has become materially more volatile than the pre-market picture suggested. For NQ and MNQ, the principal operational consideration is whether predefined financial risk remains appropriate in the presence of fast-moving prices and potentially wider execution slippage. A correct assessment of the economic backdrop does not establish a reliable entry price. The cash-market information is valuable precisely because it distinguishes confirmed selling from assumptions about what should happen next.

FINAL ANALYTICAL VIEW

WHAT CHANGED: Pre-market semiconductor weakness became a broad US cash-session sell-off. At 11:00 New York, the Nasdaq Composite was down 5.0%, with NVIDIA, AMD and CoreWeave among the companies suffering particularly large declines.

WHAT THE DATA ADDED: Initial claims fell to 189,000; productivity rose at a 3.6% annualised rate and unit labour costs declined 0.7%. Those figures are not consistent with a sudden deterioration in all aspects of the US economy.

WHAT REMAINS THE MAIN RISK: The potential financial consequences of slower AI infrastructure construction, expensive capital, uneven demand across suppliers and uncertainty surrounding future policy decisions.

WHAT MATTERS NEXT: Semiconductor breadth, financing conditions, Treasury yields, any change in the pace of selling, and Friday's official US employment report at 14:30 Switzerland.

Opinion: Where We Stand on the Iran Conflict After the 2026 Midterms

The November 3 midterm results have sharply narrowed the political space for managing the eight-month U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran that began with Operation Epic Fury on February 28. Democrats have secured majorities in both the House and Senate. Trump and Vance have publicly linked Republican losses in part to the war’s contribution to higher fuel prices and broader cost-of-living pressures. Exit polling and post-election commentary reinforce that the electorate registered dissatisfaction with continued hostilities.

Domestic posture.
A Democratic Congress, once seated in January 2027, can advance War Powers measures, conduct oversight of the campaign and Defense Department leadership, and apply pressure through appropriations. Democrats lack a two-thirds majority to override a veto, so executive authority over the use of force remains intact. Political and resource headroom is reduced, however, and Republican ranks are divided. The present lame-duck period before the new Congress takes office is the most permissive window for any renewed military action.

International posture.
Iranian officials have publicly framed the results as a “NO TO WAR” message and a political setback for the administration while warning that renewed strikes would trigger wider retaliation involving Hormuz, proxies, and other chokepoints. Tehran appears more inclined to harden sequencing demands (sanctions and blockade relief first) than to offer rapid concessions. Analysts describe a dual risk: a face-saving negotiated off-ramp becomes more attractive to a constrained White House, or residual nuclear targets (such as Pickaxe Mountain) and other sites are struck in the lame-duck window in an attempt to reclaim initiative. Gulf partners prefer de-escalation but remain wary of both a weak deal and further rounds of combat. Israeli calculations are also complicated by its own recent election dynamics and the narrower U.S. political window.

Bottom line.
The electoral outcome has not ended the conflict or removed residual Iranian capabilities, but it has raised the domestic political and fiscal cost of sustained or renewed major operations. Near-term decisions—whether limited strikes, continued talks, or a hybrid approach—will be made under tighter constraints and higher scrutiny than existed before November 3. The lame-duck period is the critical variable; after January the balance of institutional power shifts further against open-ended military escalation.

text:
Why the Market Is Selling Off, And What Could Make It Bounce Back?

This started in #stocks, not in crypto. Bitcoin sat near $80,000 until the US session got going, then dropped toward $76,500 as the #Nasdaq 100 fell more than 4% and the S&P 500 lost 2.6%. The VIX jumped about 40% in that initial move.

The centre of it is the AI trade. AMD dropped 14%, Qualcomm and Arm around 11%, Tesla 9% and Nvidia 6%. Qualcomm’s smartphone business disappointed, while Arm’s royalty revenue missed expectations and its guidance offered only a small beat. Investors are demanding more from the companies behind the AI buildout.

The midterms matter too. #Democrats won both chambers of Congress and key governor races, including Texas and Georgia, where opposition to data centres featured in campaigning. Electricity bills, water consumption and pressure on local infrastructure are now political issues. Investors are pricing in the possibility of tighter approvals and construction delays. Yesterday’s relief rally has shifted into reassessing what those results mean for individual sectors.

There is also Iran. Reports before the election described preparations for possible renewed US–Israeli strikes after the midterms. Trump said there were no immediate plans to attack, but escalation remains a risk. Further disruption to Gulf oil supplies could push energy prices and inflation higher, adding pressure to markets.

Another concern is financing. Companies are borrowing heavily to fund #AI expansion while investors question how quickly that spending will generate returns. Borrowing costs do not need to rise today to remain a problem.

What did not move matters too. The 10-year yield and dollar were broadly flat in the initial selloff, while some defensive stocks held up. That suggests rotation away from tech alongside wider risk reduction.

#Crypto is trading with tech. Around $295M of longs were liquidated during the drop against $18M of shorts, making the move sharper.

Spectre’s heatmap highlights potential liquidity zones around $75.2K and $73.7K below, with $81.85K and $83.45K overhead if a sustained recovery develops. These are modelled concentrations, not guaranteed targets.

So what could make it bounce back? Tech finding buyers, credible de-escalation around Iran and a jobs report showing cooling wage pressure without a growth scare would help. If forced liquidations slow and spot demand returns, conditions for a rebound improve. A liquidity sweep followed by a strong reclaim would be an encouraging sign.

Next up is the US jobs report tomorrow at 13:30 UTC.

text:
Chip stocks just lost a vote in Texas, and it cost Wall Street $2 trillion in a morning

Wall Street gave back an entire rally in about a day, and the reason has less to do with Congress than with three governor races in Texas, Ohio and Georgia.

On Wednesday the Dow jumped more than 1,500 points because the midterms were finally over. Micron fell 7% that same day, and that was the tell. By late Thursday morning the Nasdaq was down nearly 5%, more than 10% below its record, the S&P 500 was down more than 3%, and roughly $2 trillion in value was gone. Nvidia fell about 7%, Micron 12%, AMD 13%. 

Nothing in the economy changed overnight. October layoff announcements were the lowest since 2023.

Democrats flipped all three governor's offices, and every winner campaigned on pausing or reining in data centers, which many voters blame for higher power bills. Texas is the one nobody saw coming. The race wasn't even considered close, and Texas has 88.4 GW of planned data centers, more than any other state. 

Gina Hinojosa ran on a moratorium until Texas writes new rules. Nine states now have a governor or governor-elect who has promised or already imposed a pause, and together they hold 41% of all planned US data center capacity, according to Cleanview's project tracker. Data centers were also on the ballot in 41 local elections. The side limiting them won at least 36.

Chips got hit hardest because of what they were priced on. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta have guided to more than $700 billion of capex this year, and Alphabet says spending will rise "significantly" in 2027. 

That next wave of spending needs buildings that haven't been started yet, and new construction is exactly what the pauses target. Memory is the most exposed. In July, Amazon raised its 2026 capex plan from $200 billion to $220 billion and pinned the increase on memory getting more expensive. Part of this boom is shortage pricing. Fewer new buildings, smaller shortage.

The money isn't leaving AI. It's switching sides. Amazon rose 8% on Wednesday while the chipmakers fell. When a city stops issuing building permits, the builders suffer and whoever already owns the apartments raises the rent. Amazon has said it won't have enough capacity to meet demand this year or next. Alphabet's cloud backlog hit $561 billion last quarter, and its cloud revenue doubled.

What turned a chip problem into a market problem is how big and how jumpy chips had become. They were 19.7% of the S&P 500 at the end of June, more than double their weight before the dot-com crash. Leveraged ETF exposure to semis rose 175% between March and June, and retail traded about $1.9 billion of chip options premium a day in June, three-quarters of it in calls. Rates offer no cushion either. Fed funds futures put the odds of a December hike around 85%, and the 10-year is still near 4.9%.

None of this ends the buildout. Most of these are pauses, not bans. About 56.7 GW is already under construction, and Texas stopped issuing data center permits back in September under a Republican governor. The damage is in the price investors will pay. If they pay 22 times earnings instead of 30, a chip stock falls 27% without losing a dollar of profit.

For two years the scarcest thing in AI was chips, so chips got paid. Now it's a signature from a governor in Austin.

What happens to the information these AI tools collect about our children?

Has your school board weighed the benefits against the potential privacy and security risks of using AI in the classroom?

➡️ What student data these tools collect and store?
➡️ Who has access to that information?
➡️ Whether student information is shared with third parties or used to train AI models?

AI may offer valuable educational opportunities, but innovation should never come at the expense of children’s privacy.
